- Indian departments, policies, programmes, etc in agriculture (Unverified) -
Name Time of Initiation Reason for Initiation Impact Examples
1. Departments / Ministries (Government)
Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DAFW) 1947 (restructured 2015) To oversee agricultural development, farmer welfare, and implementation of policies and schemes for sustainable agriculture and food security. Coordinates 27 divisions, manages schemes like PM-KISAN, and supports research via ICAR. Enhanced productivity and farmer incomes.
  • Manages Soil Health Card Scheme and e-NAM.
  • Supports ICAR for climate-resilient crop research.
Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) 1973 To promote agricultural research and education through ICAR to address productivity and sustainability challenges. Developed 7 climate-resilient varieties and 650 district contingency plans under NICRA.
  • National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA).
  • Support for agricultural universities.
2. Statutory / Autonomous Bodies (Organizations)
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) 1929 Coordinate agricultural research & education. Led Green Revolution; 113 institutes, 731 KVKs; climate-resilient varieties.
  • HYVs of wheat & rice.
  • KVK technology transfer.
Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI) 1942 Regulates agricultural marketing, maintains AGMARK standards, and supports market reforms including e-NAM.
  • Grading & standardization (AGMARK).
  • Market surveys and price dissemination.
  • Supports agricultural marketing infrastructure.
  • AGMARK-certified products enforcement.
  • Integration of mandis into e-NAM.
National Seeds Corporation (NSC) 1963 Produces, certifies, and distributes high-quality seeds of various crops to farmers.
  • Foundation and certified seed production.
  • Runs seed farms across India.
  • Implements seed development programs.
  • Distribution of HYV and hybrid seeds.
  • Seed minikit programs under NFSM.
Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP)
(formerly Agricultural Prices Commission)		 1965 Recommend Minimum Support Prices (MSP) and analyse cost of cultivation. Recommends MSP for 23 crops twice a year; central to Swaminathan C2+50% debate.
  • A2+FL vs C2 formula controversy
National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) 1965 Statutory body aimed at dairy development, cooperative strengthening, and implementing sustainable dairy programs nationwide.
  • Implemented Operation Flood (White Revolution).
  • Supports dairy cooperatives and milk producer companies.
  • Promotes clean milk production and dairy infrastructure.
  • Operation Flood: transformed India into the largest milk producer.
  • Formation of producer companies like IRMA-linked cooperatives.
Food Corporation of India (FCI) 1965 Ensures food security through procurement, storage, and distribution of foodgrains under PDS and buffer stocking.
  • Procures wheat & rice at MSP.
  • Maintains central pool stocks.
  • Supplies foodgrains under NFSA and PMGKAY.
  • Large-scale procurement for NFSA.
  • Free grain distribution during COVID (PMGKAY).
Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) 1972 Promotes marine product exports, regulates aquaculture, and supports seafood quality standards.
  • Certification of aquaculture farms.
  • Infrastructure for seafood processing.
  • Supports marine product marketing and exports.
  • Export promotion of shrimps and marine products.
  • Quality certification of aquaculture units.
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NaBARD) 1982 Apex rural development financial institution providing refinance, rural credit, and support for agriculture and allied sectors.
  • Operates RIDF (Rural Infrastructure Development Fund).
  • Refinances cooperative banks & RRBs.
  • Promotes SHGs, Farmer Producer Organization (FPOs), microfinance.
  • Financing of Farmer Producer Organization (FPOs) under Central Sector Scheme.
  • RIDF funds for rural roads and irrigation.
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) 1986 National standards body responsible for quality certification of goods, including food, agricultural machinery, fertilizers, and consumer goods.
  • Sets quality standards (ISI mark).
  • Ensures certification of agri-machines and fertilizers.
  • Regulates packaged commodities standards.
  • Quality control for packaged water, fertilizers.
  • ISI mark enforcement on agri machinery.
Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) 1986 Promotes export of agricultural and processed food products; develops export infrastructure and quality standards.
  • Certifies GI products for export.
  • Manages packhouses and export zones.
  • Training & quality control for exporters.
  • Promotion of basmati, mangoes, grapes exports.
  • GI-tagged products export facilitation.
Small Farmers’ Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) 1994 Promotes agribusiness, supports Farmer Producer Organization (FPO) formation, and manages venture capital assistance for agri-startups.
  • Nodal agency for Farmer Producer Organization (FPO) formation (Central Sector Scheme).
  • Provides Venture Capital Assistance (VCA).
  • Operates e-NAM integration support.
  • Formation of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organization (FPOs) initiative.
  • VCA to agri-startups (food processing, logistics).
National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA) 2006 Formulate policies for rainfed farming (52% net sown area). Works with NMSA, RADP; prepares district agriculture plans.
  • Contingency plans for drought-prone areas.
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) 2006 Statutory authority responsible for regulating, supervising, and standardizing food safety and quality across India.
  • Frames food standards and enforces the Food Safety Act.
  • Licensing & registration of food businesses.
  • Monitors food quality, contamination, and adulteration.
  • Food recall operations (e.g., Maggi 2015 case).
  • Eat Right India initiative.
3. Cooperative Societies / Federations
National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India (NAFED) 1958 To promote cooperative marketing of agricultural produce, stabilize prices, and support farmers through procurement, buffer stocking, and market intervention.
  • Nodal agency for pulses & oilseeds procurement under PSS/PM-AASHA.
  • Maintains national buffer stock of pulses & onions.
  • Supports price stabilization operations during shortages and gluts.
  • Pulses & oilseeds procurement during price crashes (PSS).
  • Onion buffer stock operations to control price volatility.
National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) 1963 Finances and promotes cooperatives in agriculture, dairying, fisheries, horticulture, and processing sectors.
  • Loans for cooperative infrastructure.
  • Support for dairy, fisheries, and marketing cooperatives.
  • Implements cooperative modernization programs.
  • Financing Farmer Producer Organization (FPOs) and PACS modernization.
  • Support to dairy cooperatives under umbrella schemes.
National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India (NCCF) 1965 Apex cooperative institution for consumer goods distribution and procurement, ensuring availability of essential commodities at fair prices.
  • Supplies essential goods during shortages.
  • Acts as a central procurement agency for government schemes.
  • Operates consumer stores and fair-price outlets.
  • Distribution of pulses, sugar, and essentials during inflation.
  • Participation in price stabilization operations.
Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO) 1967 World’s largest farmers’ cooperative focused on manufacturing and distributing fertilizers and agricultural inputs.
  • Produces urea, NPK fertilizers, and agri-inputs.
  • Runs digital platforms for farmers.
  • Supports farmer training and extension services.
  • Iffco Nano Urea rollout.
  • Major supplier of fertilizers under DBT regime.
Krishak Bharati Cooperative Limited (KRIBHCO) 1980 Major cooperative society producing fertilizers, promoting balanced nutrient use, and supporting farmers through agri-services.
  • Large urea production at Hazira plant.
  • Provides seeds, compost, and soil health support.
  • Operates agri-retail outlets.
  • Hazira fertilizer expansion.
  • Promotion of bio-fertilizers and compost.
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) 2003 (under Companies Act 1956/2013) Collective organization of farmers to improve production, marketing, and bargaining power. Legally registered as a Producer Company or Cooperative Society.
  • Promotes collective farming, input procurement, and marketing.
  • Access to credit, subsidies, and government schemes (e.g., PM-FME, SFAC support).
  • Capacity building and technical assistance for members.
  • Market linkages for farm produce.
  • Improved price realization for members.
  • Access to government programs without direct ownership by government.
4. Commodity-Specific Corporations
Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) 1970 Ensures MSP operations for cotton and stabilizes the cotton market by procuring from farmers when prices fall.
  • Purchases cotton at MSP.
  • Maintains buffer stocks.
  • Supports cotton ginning and grading.
  • Massive MSP procurement during 2020–21 price crash.
  • Market stabilization operations in cotton-producing states.
Jute Corporation of India (JCI) 1971 Implements MSP for raw jute and supports jute farmers by procurement during price fluctuations.
  • Procures raw jute at MSP.
  • Ensures fair price to jute farmers.
  • Promotes jute quality and grading.
  • MSP procurement in WB, Bihar, Assam.
  • Support during jute glut seasons.
5. Policies
National Agriculture Policy 2000 To achieve over 4% annual growth, ensure equitable regional growth and maximize export potential. Increased agricultural GDP contribution and export growth by 10-15% in key commodities.
  • Seed certification standards.
  • Promotion of cooperative farming.
National Policy for Farmers 2007 To improve farmers’ economic viability, nutrition, and sustainable practices to address rural poverty. Raised rural incomes by ~20% in targeted areas through diversification and market access.
  • Support for Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs).
  • Promotion of organic farming.
6. Land Reform Acts
Zamindari Abolition Acts
(State-specific: U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 is the model act)		 1949–1955
(U.P. Act passed 1950, enforced 1952)		 To abolish the zamindari (intermediary) system inherited from the British, eliminate exploitative rent-seeking landlords, and establish direct tenant–state relationship (“Land to the tiller”).
  • Abolished zamindars, jagirdars, inamdars across states.
  • ≈ 20–25 million tenants became landowners.
  • Ended permanent settlement system in Bihar, UP, etc.
  • Reduced rural inequality and landlord political power.
  • Laid foundation for subsequent Green Revolution (direct incentives to cultivators).
  • Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 (most comprehensive).
  • Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950.
  • West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953.
  • Compensation was paid to zamindars via bonds (often inadequate).
Tenancy Reform Acts
(State-level, 1950s–70s)		 1950s onwards Provide security of tenure, regulate rent (max 1/4th–1/5th of produce), and confer ownership rights to tenants. Operation Barga (West Bengal, 1978) registered 1.4 million sharecroppers; many states gave ownership to tenants.
  • West Bengal’s Operation Barga.
  • Kerala & West Bengal most successful.
Land Ceiling Acts
(State-level, 1950s–1970s)		 1950s–1970s Impose ceiling on maximum landholding and redistribute surplus land to landless labourers/SC-ST. ≈ 73 lakh acres declared surplus, ≈ 53 lakh acres distributed (poor implementation due to benami transfers).
  • Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (most radical).
  • West Bengal & Karnataka relatively better implementation.
7. Marketing & Seed Related Acts
Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) Act 2003 (model act, state-specific) To regulate agricultural marketing and ensure fair prices through organized markets. Improved infrastructure in 7,000+ APMCs; 2017 reforms increased market access by 15%.
  • Maharashtra direct farmer-buyer sales.
  • Karnataka’s e-NAM integration.
Model Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (Promotion & Facilitation) Act 2017 To liberalise agricultural marketing, allow private markets, single state license, and end APMC monopoly. 23 states amended APMC Acts; enabled private markets & e-trading; reduced marketing cost by 10-15%.
  • Unified trading license in Gujarat & Maharashtra.
  • Private mandis in Rajasthan.
Protection of Plant Varieties & Farmers Rights Act (PPV&FR) 2001 India’s TRIPS-compliant sui generis system; protects breeders & farmers’ rights. 13,000+ varieties registered; farmers can save, sow, exchange seeds.
  • Only Indian law that recognises “Farmers as breeders”
Farmers’ Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act 2020 (repealed 2021) To allow barrier-free trade outside APMCs for better price realization.
  • Positive Impact
    • Improved farmer price realization (10–20%) in adopting states.
    • Allowed inter-state trade without mandi fees.
    • Reduced transportation and transaction costs.
    • Enabled online trade and private marketplaces.
  • Farmer Concerns
    • No legal guarantee for MSP; fear of its eventual dilution.
    • Weakening of APMCs over time, leading to loss of mandi infrastructure.
    • Fear of private players dominating procurement, reducing farmer bargaining power.
    • Small farmers feared exclusion from private platforms.
  • Protest Reasons
    • Dispute resolution given to SDM/collector instead of courts.
    • Possibility of corporates bypassing mandis and controlling prices.
    • Demand for statutory MSP guarantee before any market liberalisation.
    • Lack of consultation with farmer groups before passing the law.
  • Outcome
    • Mass protests beginning in Punjab and Haryana.
    • Law repealed in November 2021.
  • Direct sales by Punjab farmers.
  • Inter-state pulses trade between MP–UP.
Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act 2020 To deregulate stock limits on cereals, pulses, oilseeds, onion, potato.
  • Positive Impact
    • Reduced price volatility (e.g., onion ~10% on average).
    • Encouraged private investment in warehouses and cold chains.
    • Reduced wastage due to flexible stocking limits.
    • Enabled large retailers to stabilize supply during peak-demand seasons.
  • Farmer Concerns
    • Fear of large-scale hoarding by corporate players.
    • Small traders feared unfair competition from big storage owners.
    • Possibility of artificial scarcity to manipulate market prices.
    • Farmers feared receiving lower prices at harvest due to private stock controls.
  • Protest Reasons
    • Deregulation seen as helping corporates more than farmers.
    • Fear that companies could influence MSP by controlling stocks.
    • Act was linked to the other two farm laws in protest narratives.
  • Outcome
    • Continues to remain in force (not repealed).
    • Stock limits still imposed under exceptional circumstances.
  • Onion storage expansion in Maharashtra.
  • UP potato cold storage chain modernisation.
Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act 2020 (repealed 2021) To enable contract farming with assured prices and private partnerships.
  • Positive Impact
    • Assured prices protected farmers from market crashes.
    • Enabled technology transfer through private partners.
    • Promoted high-value crops like processing potatoes, vegetables, seeds.
    • ~1,000 contracts signed in the first year.
  • Farmer Concerns
    • Imbalance of power between corporations and small farmers.
    • Companies could reject produce citing “quality issues.”
    • Fear of indirect land control through long-term agreements.
    • Pricing formula clarity often missing in draft agreements.
  • Protest Reasons
    • Disputes not allowed in civil courts; only SDM-level settlement.
    • No MSP guarantee for contracted crops.
    • Farmers feared forced dependence on corporate buyers.
  • Outcome
    • Withdrawn in 2021 after extended protest movement.
  • PepsiCo potato contract farming in Gujarat.
  • Sugarcane contract farming practices in UP.
8. Schemes / Missions / Programmes
Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) – “Package Programme” 1960–61 Test concentrated input approach in 7 selected districts. Pilot for Green Revolution; proved “technology + credit + price” works.
  • One district from each state model
High Yielding Varieties Programme (HYVP) 1966–67 Introduce Mexican wheat (Lerma Rojo, Sonora-64) and Philippine rice (IR-8) with fertiliser + irrigation package. India became food surplus; wheat production from 11 mt (1960) → 55 mt (1990).
  • Punjab, Haryana, Western UP as “wheat bowl”
Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme 1998 Provide timely & adequate credit through a single card. 14+ crore cards issued; 2020 reforms included animal husbandry & fisheries.
  • Interest subvention 2% + prompt repayment incentive 3%
National Food Security Mission (NFSM) 2007 Increase production of rice, wheat, pulses & coarse cereals. Added ~50 mt to foodgrain production; merged under Green Revolution–Krishnonnati Yojana.
  • Accelerated Pulses Production Programme (A3P).
  • Focus districts for wheat & rice.
National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) 2014 Promote sustainable agriculture in rainfed areas (52% net sown area). Includes RADP, Soil Health Management, PKVY; climate-resilient villages in 151 districts.
  • Rainfed Area Development Programme (RADP).
  • Integrated farming in Bihar.
National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP → NMEO-OP)
National Mission on Edible Oils – Oil Palm		 2014 → 2021 Reduce 60%+ edible oil import dependency. Oilseeds production ↑ from 31 mt to 41 mt; NMEO-OP targets self-sufficiency.
  • Oil palm in Andhra & NE states.
  • Soybean package in MP.
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) 2014 Umbrella scheme (National Horticulture Mission (NHM), Horticulture Mission for North East & Himalayan States (HMNEH), National Bamboo Mission (NBM), etc.) for horticulture growth. Horticulture production 350+ mt (2nd globally); surpassed foodgrains.
  • National Horticulture Mission (NHM).
  • Horticulture Mission for North East & Himalayan States (HMNEH) for NE & Himalayan states.
Rashtriya Gokul Mission (under National Livestock Mission) 2014 Conserve & develop indigenous cattle breeds (White Revolution 2.0). 30+ Gokul Grams; livestock contributes ~30% agri-GDP.
  • Gir, Sahiwal breed improvement.
  • Ettupattu scheme in AP.
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) 2015 “Har Khet Ko Pani” and “Per Drop More Crop”. Added 11+ lakh ha irrigated area; major component: Per Drop More Crop (PDMC).
  • Drip irrigation in Gujarat cotton.
  • Micro-irrigation in Rajasthan.
Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) – Micro-irrigation component of PMKSY 2015 Promote drip & sprinkler irrigation for water efficiency. Covered 8+ million ha; water saving 20-40%, yield increase up to 50%.
  • Sugarcane drip in Maharashtra.
  • Sprinklers in MP pulses.
Soil Health Card Scheme 2015 Issue soil health cards with nutrient recommendations. 23+ crore cards distributed; reduced fertilizer misuse.
  • Reduced urea overuse in Punjab & Haryana.
Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) 2015 Promote organic farming through clusters. 2+ million ha under organic; 10,000+ clusters formed.
  • Sikkim organic model.
  • Organic turmeric in MP.
Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) 2015 Provides refinance (lending money to a financial institution) and credit support to micro and small enterprises under Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY).
  • Offers Shishu, Kishor, Tarun loans.
  • Refinances banks/NBFCs lending to micro units.
  • Supports rural & agri-allied micro-enterprises.
  • Financing small agri-allied units (dairy, poultry).
  • Credit expansion for rural micro businesses.
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) 2016 Affordable crop insurance against natural calamities. 56+ crore farmer applications; ₹1.5 lakh crore claims paid till 2025.
  • Paddy flood claims in Andhra.
  • Drought compensation in Gujarat.
e-National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) 2016 Pan-India electronic trading portal integrating APMCs. 1,000+ mandis integrated; trade volume ₹2.5+ lakh crore.
  • Turmeric trade Karnataka → Maharashtra.
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) 2018 Ensure MSP through three components:
  • Price Support Scheme (PSS): Central + state procurement of pulses & oilseeds through NAFED.
  • Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS): Direct payment of the difference between MSP and market price.
  • Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPSS): Empanelling private players to procure at MSP.
  • Procurement of 1,200+ lakh MT pulses/oilseeds under PSS.
  • PDPS successfully implemented for soybean in Madhya Pradesh.
  • NAFED major role in stabilizing dal prices through buffer stock creation.
  • PDPS for soybean in Madhya Pradesh.
  • NAFED procurement of tur and moong under PSS.
  • PPSS pilots in selected districts for oilseeds during price crash.
PM Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyaan (PM-KUSUM) 2019 Solarise agriculture (pumps & grid-connected plants). 4+ lakh solar pumps installed; 10,000 MW solar plants targeted.
  • Solar pumps in Haryana & Rajasthan.
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) 2019 Direct income support of ₹6,000/year to small & marginal farmers. ₹3+ lakh crore transferred to 11+ crore farmers till 2025.
  • Seed & fertilizer purchase support in Bihar.
  • Tribal farmers in Odisha.
Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) 2020 ₹1 lakh crore fund for post-harvest infrastructure. ₹45,000+ crore sanctioned for 70,000+ projects (cold storage, warehouses).
  • Cold chains in UP & Maharashtra.
  • Farmer Producer Organization (FPO) processing units.
Formation & Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) 2020 Aggregate small farmers for better bargaining and market access. 15,000+ FPOs formed by 2025; ₹18,000 crore support.
  • Sahyadri Farms (grapes) Maharashtra.
  • Onion FPOs in MP.
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) 2020 Blue Revolution – double fisheries production & exports. Fish production ↑ from 95 lakh tonnes (2014) to 175+ lakh tonnes (2024).
  • Deep-sea fishing vessels.
  • Aquaculture in Andhra & West Bengal.
Nano Urea & Nano DAP (Liquid) 2021 (Nano Urea) → 2023 (Nano DAP) IFFCO’s liquid nano fertilizers to reduce chemical fertilizer dependency by 50%.
  • Nano Urea: 1 bottle (500 ml) = 1 bag (45 kg) urea.
  • 8 plants operational by 2025; target 44 crore bottles/year.
  • Included in PM PrANAM Scheme (2023) for 50% subsidy.
  • 2023 & 2024 Prelims MCQs.
  • Criticism: Efficacy still under ICMR/ICAR long-term trials.
World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector 2023 – ongoing
₹1.25 lakh crore		 Decentralised storage at Primary Agri Credit Societies (PACS), godowns using Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode to reduce post-harvest losses and eliminate foodgrain wastage.
  • Pilot in 11 states, 700+ godowns sanctioned by Dec 2025.
  • Convergence of PM-KUSUM, AIF, MIDH, NaBARD RIDF.
  • Inter-Ministerial Committee under Amitabh Kant.
  • Target: 700 lakh MT capacity in 5 years.
  • Part of 100-day agenda after 2024 elections.
  • Directly asked in 2024 Mains 10-marker.
Digital Public Infrastructure for Agriculture (DPI / AgriStack) 2023 – ongoing Open-source, federated digital framework: Farmer ID, land records digitisation, crop sown registry, soil profile, geo-referenced village maps.
  • Farmer registry linked to PM-KISAN database (13+ crore farmers).
  • Krishi Decision Support System (DSS) launched 2024.
  • Integration with e-NAM, PMFBY, Soil Health Card.
  • MoUs with Cisco, Jio, ITC, Ninjacart for private layer.
  • 2024 Mains question on digital agriculture.
  • Criticism: Privacy concerns, data monopoly fears.
Agriculture Accelerator Fund Budget 2023 Fund to bring innovative and affordable solutions by young entrepreneurs in rural areas through start-ups.
  • Operated via NaBARD & agri-startup ecosystem.
  • Focus on drones, AI, precision farming, FPOs.
  • ₹750+ crore allocated in subsequent budgets.
  • Repeated in 2023 & 2024 Prelims/Mains.
International Year of Millets – “Shree Anna” Campaign 2023 (UN declaration on India’s proposal) Global promotion of millets as climate-resilient, nutritious “superfood”.
  • India world’s largest producer & second-largest exporter.
  • Inclusion in ICDS, Mid-Day Meal, PDS.
  • ₹1,200+ crore branding & research fund.
  • Millets export up 25% in 2023–24.
  • Multiple questions in 2023 & 2024.
  • “Shree Anna” branding by PM.
PM-PrANAM Scheme
(PM Promotion of Alternate Nutrients for Agriculture Management Yojana)		 Budget 2023 Incentivise states to reduce chemical fertilizer use; 50% subsidy saving shared as grant.
  • ₹1 lakh crore fertilizer subsidy burden reduction target.
  • Promotes Nano Urea, bio-fertilizers, organic farming.
  • First allocation 2024–25.
  • Expected in 2025 Mains.
Computerisation & Modernisation of 2 lakh Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) 2023 – ongoing Make Primary Agricultural Credit Societies multi-service hubs (PACS as CSCs, fertiliser/pesticide retail, storage, FPO support).
  • ₹2,516 crore project approved 2023.
  • Link PACS with NaBARD ERP, GeM, DBT.
  • Integration with World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan.
  • Cooperative sector revival theme.
GOBARDhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) 2023 – scaled up 2,000+ biogas plants (CBG) under SATAT & umbrella scheme to convert cattle dung, agri residue into compressed biogas & bio-fertilizer.
  • 500 plants operational by 2025.
  • ₹10,000 crore viability gap funding.
  • Farmers get additional income from waste.
  • Circular economy + renewable energy.
NAMO Drone Didi (Namo Drone Didis) Budget 2024 Train 15,000 women SHGs to provide drone services for rental to farmers (pesticide, fertilizer spraying, crop assessment).
  • ₹1,261 crore scheme (2024–26).
  • Women SHGs get 80% subsidy on drones.
  • Part of Lakhpati Didi programme.
  • 2025 hot topic (women empowerment + agri tech).
9. Revolutions in Indian Agriculture
Green Revolution 1966–67 onwards Introduce HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers & assured irrigation to achieve food self-sufficiency. Wheat production ↑ from 11 mt (1960) to 110+ mt (2024); India became net food exporter.
  • HYVP (1966), Mexican wheat (Norman Borlaug), IR-8 rice.
  • Punjab, Haryana, Western UP benefitted most.
  • Criticism: Regional imbalance, groundwater depletion.
White Revolution
(Operation Flood)		 1970–1996
Phase I: 1970, Phase II: 1981, Phase III: 1985		 To make India self-sufficient in milk production through cooperative dairy farming model. India became world’s largest milk producer (198 mt in 2023–24); per capita availability ↑ from 130 g/day (1970) to 428 g/day (2023).
  • National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) & Dr Verghese Kurien.
  • Anand (Gujarat) model → Amul → GCMMF.
  • Three phases funded by World Bank & EEC.
Yellow Revolution 1986–87 onwards Increase oilseeds production to reduce edible oil imports. Oilseeds production ↑ from 11 mt (1985) to 41 mt (2024); still import 55–60%.
  • Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986).
  • Led to → NMOOP (2014) → NMEO-OP (2021).
Grey Revolution 1990s onwards Increase production and supply of cement, limestone, and construction materials to support infrastructure and housing growth. Cement production ↑ from ~6 mt (1950s) to 400+ mt (2024); major infrastructure boost.
  • Modernization of cement plants and adoption of new technology.
  • Public-private partnerships and government incentives for production.
  • Supports national housing and infrastructure programs.
Golden Revolution 1991–2003 Rapid growth in horticulture (fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices). Horticulture production surpassed foodgrains for the first time in 2012–13.
  • National Horticulture Mission (2005–06) was its institutional phase.
  • Now under MIDH.
Silver Revolution 2000s Increase in egg production through poultry development. Egg production ↑ from 30 billion (2000) to 130+ billion (2024).
  • National Livestock Mission support.
White Revolution 2.0
(Rashtriya Gokul Mission + National Programme for Dairy Development)		 2014 onwards Increase milk productivity through indigenous breed improvement, sex-sorted semen, IVF, and better nutrition/feed. Milk production growth rate ↑ to 6%+ per annum; 50+ Gokul Grams, e-Pashu Haat portal.
  • Rashtriya Gokul Mission (2014).
  • Goal: 310 mt milk by 2025–26.
Blue Revolution
(Neeli Kranti)		 2015–2020 (umbrella phase) Comprehensive development of fisheries & aquaculture (inland + marine). Fish production ↑ from 95 lakh tonnes (2014) to 175+ lakh tonnes (2024); exports ↑ to ₹63,000 crore.
  • Creation of Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying (2019).
  • Fisheries & Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF).
10. Committees
Swaminathan Committee (National Commission on Farmers) 2004–06 Address agrarian distress; recommend farmer-centric policies. Recommended MSP = C2 + 50% (i.e., 50% profit over their total economic cost); shaped National Policy for Farmers.
  • C2+50% formula.
  • Focus on soil health & water.
Shanta Kumar Committee 2015 Restructure Food Corporation of India (FCI) & food procurement system. Recommended direct cash transfer, reduce procurement, end PDS leakage.
  • Only 6% farmers benefit from MSP.
  • Shift procurement to states.
Ashok Dalwai Committee (Doubling Farmers’ Income) 2016–19 Roadmap to double farmers’ income by 2022. 14-volume report; influenced PM-KISAN, e-NAM, FPOs, etc.
  • 7 sources of income growth.
  • Focus on high-value crops & livestock.
- Important financial bodies in different sphere like ministries, darparments, etc (Validated) -
Financial Body Sphere Establishment Year Parent Organization Purpose Additional Details
Constitutional Financial Authorities
Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) Constitutional Authority 1950 Article 148, Constitution of India
  • Audits accounts of the Union and State governments
  • Examines expenditure from Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts
  • Ensures legality, propriety, and efficiency in public spending
  • Independent constitutional authority
  • Reports submitted to President/Governors and laid before legislatures
  • Acts as guardian of the public purse
  • Key pillar of legislative financial control
Finance Commission Constitutional Body 1951 Article 280, Constitution of India
  • Recommends distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States
  • Recommends principles governing grants-in-aid of the States from the Consolidated Fund of India
  • Addresses vertical and horizontal fiscal imbalances
  • Independent constitutional body (not quasi-judicial)
  • Constituted by the President every five years or earlier
  • Advisory in nature; recommendations are not legally binding
  • Core instrument of fiscal federalism
Goods and Services Tax Council Constitutional Body 2016 Article 279A, Constitution of India
  • Recommends GST tax rates, exemptions, and threshold limits
  • Recommends model GST laws, principles of levy, and place of supply
  • Ensures a harmonised structure of goods and services tax across India
  • Federal constitutional body comprising Union and State representatives
  • Chairperson: Union Finance Minister
  • Decisions taken through weighted voting mechanism (Union: one-third, States: two-thirds)
  • Key institution for cooperative federalism in indirect taxation
MAJOR ECONOMY MINISTRIES
Ministry of Railways Rail Transport and Logistics 1905 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Operates national rail transport system
  • Facilitates freight and passenger movement
  • Supports industrial and regional connectivity
  • Largest public sector transporter
  • Key logistics backbone
Ministry of Finance Economic and Fiscal Administration 1947 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Formulates fiscal policy and manages public finance
  • Prepares Union Budget and manages public debt
  • Oversees taxation, financial sector, and capital markets
  • Departments: Economic Affairs, Revenue, Expenditure, Financial Services
  • Central pillar of macroeconomic management
Ministry of Commerce and Industry Trade and Industrial Policy 1947 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Formulates foreign trade and industrial policy
  • Promotes exports and regulates imports
  • Oversees industrial development and investment promotion
  • Departments: Commerce; Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
  • Handles WTO matters and trade agreements
Ministry of Textiles Industrial and Export Promotion 1947 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Promotes textile and apparel industry
  • Supports exports and employment-intensive manufacturing
  • Implements production-linked and cluster schemes
  • Major contributor to exports and jobs
  • Important for labour-intensive growth
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Agriculture and Allied Sectors 1947 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Formulates agricultural policy and farm welfare measures
  • Promotes crop production and allied activities
  • Supports food security and rural livelihoods
  • Key role in primary sector of the economy
  • Linked with MSP, inputs, and productivity
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Food Security and Price Stability 1947 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Manages public distribution system
  • Ensures food security and buffer stock management
  • Monitors prices of essential commodities
  • Critical for inflation control
  • Administers food subsidy framework
Ministry of Power Electricity and Energy Infrastructure 1947 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Formulates power sector policy
  • Oversees generation, transmission, and distribution
  • Promotes energy access and reforms
  • Backbone of industrial and services growth
  • Linked with renewable energy transition
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Maritime Trade and Logistics 1947 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Develops ports and shipping infrastructure
  • Promotes coastal and inland water transport
  • Facilitates international trade logistics
  • Critical for export-import economy
  • Supports logistics cost reduction
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas Energy Sector Administration 1954 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Formulates policy for oil and gas sector
  • Oversees exploration, refining, and distribution
  • Manages energy security
  • Major impact on fiscal balance and inflation
  • Strategic economic ministry
Ministry of Coal Core Energy Resource Administration 1975 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Manages coal production and supply
  • Ensures fuel security for power and industry
  • Implements coal sector reforms
  • Strategic for power and steel sectors
  • Important for energy pricing
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways Surface Transport Infrastructure 2000 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Develops national highways and road infrastructure
  • Facilitates logistics and mobility
  • Supports infrastructure-led growth
  • Critical for logistics efficiency
  • High multiplier effect on economy
Ministry of Corporate Affairs Corporate Governance and Regulation 2004 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Administers company law and corporate compliance
  • Regulates corporate governance framework
  • Implements Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (policy side)
  • Administers Companies Act and Limited Liability Partnership Act
  • Key role in ease of doing business
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises MSME Development 2007 Allocation of Business Rules
  • Promotes growth and competitiveness of MSMEs
  • Implements MSME development schemes
  • Supports entrepreneurship and employment generation
  • Critical for manufacturing and services employment
  • Linked with credit, skilling, and technology upgradation
Central Banking Authority
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Central Bank 1935 Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
  • Formulates and implements monetary policy of India
  • Issues and manages banknotes (₹2 and above)
  • Acts as banker, agent, and adviser to the Government of India
  • Regulates and supervises banks and NBFCs
  • Manages foreign exchange under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA)
  • Statutory body with functional autonomy
  • Monetary Policy Committee introduced by RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016
  • Headquarters: Mumbai
  • Not a constitutional body; established by an Act of Parliament
Ministry of Finance – Core Departments
Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) Ministry Department (Ministry of Finance) 1947 Allocation of Business Rules, Government of India
  • Formulates and monitors macroeconomic and fiscal policy
  • Responsible for preparation of the Union Budget
  • Manages public debt, capital markets, and financial sector policy
  • Handles external finance and relations with multilateral institutions
  • Nodal department for economic and fiscal policy of the Union
  • Deals with IMF, World Bank, Asian Development Bank, etc.
  • Administers the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) framework
Department of Expenditure Ministry Department (Ministry of Finance) 1947 Allocation of Business Rules, Government of India
  • Controls and authorises public expenditure of the Union Government
  • Ensures financial discipline and expenditure control
  • Examines and approves proposals with financial implications
  • Implements decisions relating to Central Pay Commissions
  • Responsible for expenditure-related aspects of the FRBM framework
  • Nodal department for public financial management and expenditure reforms
Department of Revenue Ministry Department (Ministry of Finance) 1947 Allocation of Business Rules, Government of India
  • Administers direct and indirect tax laws of the Union
  • Frames and implements tax policy and tax legislation
  • Administers Goods and Services Tax (GST) in coordination with States
  • Exercises administrative control over the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
  • Responsible for customs, central excise, and Goods and Services Tax (GST) administration
  • Plays a key role in tax compliance, enforcement, and revenue mobilisation
Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) Tax Administration Authority 1963 Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963
  • Administers direct tax laws, including the Income-tax Act, 1961
  • Frames policies for levy, assessment, and collection of direct taxes
  • Exercises administrative control over the Income Tax Department
  • Functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
  • Responsible for tax administration, enforcement, assessments, and appeals
  • Frequently tested in Prelims: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) vs Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) Tax Administration Authority 1963 Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963
  • Administers indirect taxes, including Goods and Services Tax (GST) and customs duties
  • Implements Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) and Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST)
  • Exercises administrative control over customs, central excise (residual), and GST field formations
  • Functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
  • Formerly known as the Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBEC); renamed in 2018
  • Principal operational arm of the Union’s indirect tax administration
Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Ministry Department 1996 Executive allocation of business
  • Manages government equity in CPSEs
  • Implements disinvestment and strategic sale policy
  • Advises on asset monetisation
  • Earlier Department of Disinvestment
  • Key role in privatisation policy
  • Works closely with NITI Aayog
Department of Financial Services (DFS) Ministry Department (Ministry of Finance) 2004 Allocation of Business Rules, Government of India
  • Formulates policy relating to the banking and insurance sectors
  • Exercises administrative oversight over public sector banks and financial institutions
  • Promotes financial inclusion initiatives of the Government of India
  • Policy-making and oversight department; not a financial regulator
  • Handles bank recapitalisation, reforms, and governance issues
  • Coordinates with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
Sector Regulators
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Capital Market Regulator 1988 (Statutory: 1992) Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
  • Regulates the securities and capital markets
  • Protects the interests of investors in securities
  • Promotes the orderly development of the securities market
  • Registers and regulates market intermediaries
  • Statutory regulator with enforcement powers since 1992
  • Regulates stock exchanges, mutual funds, Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
  • Forward Markets Commission (FMC) merged with SEBI in 2015
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Telecom Sector Regulator 1997 Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997
  • Regulates telecommunications services in India
  • Fixes and regulates tariffs and quality of service
  • Recommends spectrum pricing and licensing conditions
  • Protects consumer interests and promotes competition
  • Statutory regulator with rule-making powers
  • Does not grant licences (function of Department of Telecommunications)
  • Disputes and appeals handled by Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT)
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) Power Sector Regulator 1998 (Statutory: 2003) Electricity Act, 2003
  • Regulates tariffs for interstate electricity transmission
  • Regulates interstate power trading
  • Advises Central Government on electricity policy matters
  • Statutory regulator for interstate electricity matters
  • Ensures efficiency, competition, and grid discipline
  • State-level counterpart: State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) Insurance Sector Regulator 1999 Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
  • Regulates and promotes the insurance business in India
  • Protects the interests of policyholders
  • Prescribes solvency margins and licensing conditions for insurers
  • Statutory regulator for life, general, and health insurance
  • Issues regulations relating to products, pricing, distribution, and conduct
  • Supervises insurers, reinsurers, and insurance intermediaries
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) Pension Sector Regulator 2003 (Statutory: 2013) Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 2013
  • Regulates and develops the pension sector in India
  • Regulates and oversees the National Pension System (NPS)
  • Registers and supervises pension fund managers and other intermediaries
  • Statutory status conferred by Parliament in 2013
  • Covers Central and State Government as well as private sector subscribers
  • Plays a key role in ensuring old-age income security
Competition Commission of India (CCI) Competition Regulator 2003 Competition Act, 2002
  • Prevents practices having adverse effect on competition
  • Prohibits abuse of dominant position and anti-competitive agreements
  • Regulates combinations such as mergers and acquisitions
  • Statutory regulator with quasi-judicial powers
  • Promotes fair competition and consumer welfare
  • Appeals lie to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT)
Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) Energy Sector Regulator 2006 Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act, 2006
  • Regulates downstream petroleum and natural gas sector
  • Authorises pipelines and city gas distribution networks
  • Ensures fair trade and competition in the sector
  • Statutory regulator for refining, processing, storage, and distribution
  • Does not regulate upstream exploration and production
  • Key role in natural gas market reforms
Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India (AERA) Aviation Economic Regulator 2008 Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act, 2008
  • Regulates tariffs for aeronautical services at major airports
  • Determines development fees and passenger service fees
  • Ensures transparency in airport tariff setting
  • Statutory regulator for airport economics
  • Technical safety regulation handled by Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)
  • Key role in airport privatisation framework
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) Insolvency Regulator 2016 Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
  • Implements and regulates the insolvency and bankruptcy framework in India
  • Registers and regulates insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies, and information utilities
  • Frames regulations for corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation processes
  • Key institutional pillar of time-bound insolvency resolution
  • Applies to companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), partnership firms, and individuals
  • Works with the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT)
Technology and Service Provider
National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) Digital Payments Infrastructure Provider 2008 Section 8 Company under the Companies Act, 2013
  • Operates retail payment and settlement systems
  • Manages Unified Payments Interface (UPI), RuPay, and IMPS
  • Provides digital payment infrastructure across banks
  • Not a regulator; operates under oversight of Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
  • Promotes digital and cashless payments
  • Common UPSC trap: NPCI ≠ RBI
Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI) Financial Asset Registry 2011 Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002
  • Maintains central registry of secured transactions
  • Records mortgages, charges, and security interests
  • Prevents multiple lending against same asset
  • Non-regulatory statutory body
  • Supports credit discipline and financial transparency
  • Operational support to banks and financial institutions
Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) GST IT Backbone Institution 2013 Section 8 Company (Companies Act)
  • Provides IT infrastructure for GST implementation
  • Facilitates registration, return filing, and tax payments
  • Acts as common interface between taxpayers and tax authorities
  • Non-regulatory, non-constitutional body
  • Government holds majority stake
  • Common UPSC trap: GSTN ≠ GST Council
Information Utilities (IUs) Insolvency Information Infrastructure 2016 Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
  • Collects and stores financial information of debtors
  • Authenticates debt and default records
  • Supports insolvency resolution processes
  • Registered and regulated by Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI)
  • Does not adjudicate or resolve insolvency
  • Purely facilitative and informational role
Appellate and Redressal Bodies
Banking Ombudsman Grievance Redressal Mechanism 1995 Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Ombudsman Scheme)
  • Redresses complaints relating to deficiency in banking services
  • Provides free, fair, and time-bound grievance redressal to customers
  • Facilitates resolution of disputes between customers and regulated entities
  • Administered by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
  • Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 covers banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), and digital payment systems
  • Non-adjudicatory mechanism; appellate authority lies with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) Quasi-Judicial Appellate Tribunal 1995 Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
  • Hears appeals against orders passed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
  • Adjudicates appeals relating to securities market laws and regulations
  • Ensures appellate oversight and accountability of securities market regulators
  • Also hears appeals against orders of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
  • Headed by a Presiding Officer with judicial background
  • Appeals from SAT lie to the Supreme Court of India
Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) Quasi-Judicial Appellate Tribunal 2000 Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997
  • Hears appeals against orders of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)
  • Adjudicates disputes between telecom service providers and the Government
  • Resolves disputes among telecom service providers
  • Does not regulate or license telecom services
  • Licensing and spectrum allocation handled by the Department of Telecommunications
  • Appeals lie to the Supreme Court of India
Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) Quasi-Judicial Appellate Tribunal 2003 Electricity Act, 2003
  • Hears appeals against orders of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC)
  • Hears appeals against orders of the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs)
  • Ensures uniform interpretation of electricity laws
  • Specialised appellate body for electricity sector disputes
  • Does not regulate tariffs or issue licences
  • Appeals lie to the Supreme Court of India on questions of law
National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) Quasi-Judicial Appellate Tribunal 2016 Companies Act, 2013 / Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
  • Hears appeals against orders of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
  • Acts as appellate authority under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
  • Hears appeals against orders of the Competition Commission of India (CCI)
  • Key appellate body for company law, insolvency, and competition matters
  • Does not conduct insolvency resolution; only hears appeals
  • Appeals lie to the Supreme Court of India on questions of law
Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) Quasi-Judicial Appellate Tribunal Provided in 2017 (Operationalisation ongoing) Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
  • Functions as the appellate tribunal under Goods and Services Tax (GST) laws
    • Hears second appeals against orders of the First Appellate Authority
  • Aims to ensure uniform interpretation of Goods and Services Tax (GST) laws across India
  • Acts as the final fact-finding authority in Goods and Services Tax (GST) disputes
  • Structure modified pursuant to Supreme Court judgments on tribunal reforms
  • Principal Bench and State Benches provided under the law
  • Appeals lie to the High Courts and the Supreme Court of India on questions of law
Development Finance Institutions (DFIs)
Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) Industrial Development Finance Institution 1948 Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948
  • Provided long-term finance to the industrial sector
  • Supported industrial development and infrastructure projects
  • Offered project finance and advisory services
  • India’s first development finance institution
  • Corporatised in 1993 and converted into a company under the Companies Act
  • Played a key role in post-independence industrialisation
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) Agriculture and Rural Development DFI 1982 National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981
  • Provides refinance for agriculture, rural development, and allied activities
  • Promotes and supports institutional credit to the rural sector
  • Implements and supports rural development and livelihood initiatives
  • Wholly owned by the Government of India
  • Supervises Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and cooperative banks
  • Apex institution for rural credit and development policy
Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank) Export Credit Development Finance Institution 1982 Export-Import Bank of India Act, 1981
  • Finances and promotes India’s exports and imports of goods and services
  • Provides Lines of Credit for overseas infrastructure and development projects
  • Supports Indian exporters and overseas investments by Indian companies
  • Specialised development finance institution for external trade
  • Wholly owned by the Government of India; administratively under the Ministry of Finance
  • Supports trade diplomacy through concessional Lines of Credit
National Housing Bank (NHB) Housing Finance Development Finance Institution 1988 National Housing Bank Act, 1987
  • Promotes and supports housing finance institutions
  • Provides refinance for housing loans
  • Supports affordable housing and priority housing segments
  • Originally a subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
  • Ownership transferred to the Government of India in 2019
  • Post-2019, regulation of housing finance companies vested with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Finance Institution 1990 Small Industries Development Bank of India Act, 1989
  • Promotes, finances, and develops the micro, small, and medium enterprises sector
  • Provides refinance and direct lending to micro, small, and medium enterprises
  • Supports microfinance institutions and financial inclusion initiatives
  • Principal financial institution for the micro, small, and medium enterprises sector
  • Wholly owned by the Government of India (ownership transferred from the Reserve Bank of India in 2019)
  • Plays a catalytic role in entrepreneurship and innovation
India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) Infrastructure Finance Development Finance Institution 2006 Government Company under the Companies Act, 2013
  • Provides long-term finance for infrastructure projects
  • Supports public-private partnership (PPP) projects in infrastructure
  • Provides refinancing, take-out financing, and credit enhancement
  • Wholly owned by the Government of India
  • Acts as a specialised vehicle for infrastructure financing
  • Complements private and market-based infrastructure investment
National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) Infrastructure Development Finance Institution 2021 National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development Act, 2021
  • Provides long-term finance for infrastructure projects
  • Develops the bond market and facilitates infrastructure financing mechanisms
  • Acts as the principal development finance institution for infrastructure
  • New-age DFI created to address the infrastructure financing gap
  • Provides guarantees and credit enhancement for infrastructure projects
  • Regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as notified
Public Sector Banks and Insurance Institutions
State Bank of India (SBI) Public Sector Bank 1955 State Bank of India Act, 1955
  • Provides commercial banking and a wide range of financial services
  • Acts as banker to several State Governments and government agencies
  • Extends credit to priority and non-priority sectors
  • India’s largest public sector bank
  • Associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged into SBI in 2017
  • Plays a systemic role in financial stability and credit transmission
Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) Public Sector Insurance Corporation 1956 Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956
  • Provides life insurance and pension products
  • Mobilises household savings for long-term investment
  • Acts as a major institutional investor in the Indian economy
  • Statutory corporation established under an Act of Parliament
  • Majority-owned by the Government of India (post-2022 public issue)
  • Largest life insurer in India with a key role in financial inclusion and social security
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) Regional Banking Institutions 1975 Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976
  • Provides banking and credit services in rural and semi-urban areas
  • Promotes financial inclusion and rural development
  • Supports agriculture, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and self-help groups (SHGs)
  • Joint ownership: Government of India, concerned State Government, and Sponsor Bank (50:15:35)
  • Regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and supervised by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
  • Area-specific operations limited to notified districts
Nationalised Public Sector Banks; Public Sector General Insurance Companies Public Sector Banking and Insurance Institutions 1969–1972 Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Acts, 1969 & 1980; General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972
  • Provide commercial banking, credit, and deposit services
  • Offer general insurance products such as health, motor, and property insurance
  • Support priority sector lending and risk coverage across the economy
  • Nationalised banks created through bank nationalisation Acts
  • Public sector general insurers include companies under General Insurance Corporation framework
  • Operate as government-owned companies regulated by sectoral regulators
Capital Market Infrastructure & Industry Bodies
Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) Stock Exchange 1875 Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956
  • Provides a platform for trading in equities, debt instruments, and derivatives
  • Facilitates price discovery and capital formation
  • Maintains benchmark equity indices, including the Sensex
  • Oldest stock exchange in Asia
  • Flagship index: Sensitive Index (Sensex)
  • Recognised stock exchange and regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) Stock Exchange 1992 Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956
  • Provides a nationwide, fully electronic trading platform
  • Facilitates trading in equities, derivatives, and debt instruments
  • Enhances market efficiency, liquidity, and transparency
  • Pioneered screen-based electronic trading in India
  • Flagship index: Nifty 50
  • Recognised stock exchange regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Mutual Fund Institution
Unit Trust of India (UTI) Legacy Financial Institution / Mutual Fund Sponsor 1964 Unit Trust of India Act, 1963 (repealed by the Unit Trust of India (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act, 2002)
  • Pioneered the mutual fund industry in India
  • Mobilised household savings for investment in capital markets
  • Post-restructuring, mutual fund operations carried out by UTI Asset Management Company through UTI Mutual Fund (UTI MF)
  • Originally a statutory corporation established by Parliament
  • Split in 2003 into UTI Mutual Fund and the Specified Undertaking of the Unit Trust of India (SUUTI)
  • UTI Mutual Fund operates as a private asset management company regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) Industry Association / Self-Regulatory Organisation (Non-Regulatory) 1995 Section 8 Company under the Companies Act, 2013
  • Promotes ethical and professional standards in the mutual fund industry
  • Conducts investor awareness and education programmes
  • Acts as a Self-Regulatory Organisation for mutual fund distributors
  • Not a statutory regulator and does not exercise regulatory powers
  • Recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) as an SRO for distributors
  • Issues and administers AMFI Registration Number (ARN)
STATUTORY COMMODITY BOARD
Coffee Board of India Statutory Commodity Board 1942 Coffee Act, 1942
  • Promotes development of the coffee industry in India
  • Supports research, quality improvement, and productivity
  • Promotes export and marketing of Indian coffee
  • Functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Performs developmental and export-promotion functions
  • Important for plantation economy and agri-exports
Rubber Board Statutory Commodity Board 1947 Rubber Act, 1947
  • Promotes development of the rubber industry
  • Supports research, quality control, and productivity enhancement
  • Promotes marketing and export of rubber and rubber products
  • Functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Performs developmental and regulatory functions
  • Supports small growers and plantation sector
Central Silk Board Statutory Sectoral Board 1948 Central Silk Board Act, 1948
  • Promotes development of sericulture and silk industry
  • Supports research, training, and technology transfer
  • Coordinates silk production and quality improvement

Tea Board of India Statutory Commodity Board 1953 Tea Act, 1953
  • Promotes development of tea cultivation and tea industry in India
  • Regulates quality control, certification, and export of tea
  • Supports research, marketing, and market development initiatives

Coir Board Statutory Commodity Board 1953 Coir Industry Act, 1953
