Spices Board of India Statutory Commodity Board 1987 Spices Board Act, 1986
  • Promotes development and export of Indian spices
  • Regulates quality control, certification, and food safety standards for spices
  • Supports branding, research, and market development of Indian spices
  • Functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Performs both developmental and regulatory functions
  • Operates residue monitoring and certification systems for export compliance
Trade and Export Promotion
Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) Export Credit Insurance Agency 1957 Government Company under the Companies Act
  • Provides export credit insurance to exporters
  • Covers commercial and political risks in export transactions
  • Offers credit risk cover to banks financing exports
  • Functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Wholly owned by the Government of India
  • Plays a key role in promoting exports, especially for MSMEs
Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) Apex Export Promotion Organisation 1965 Registered Society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860
  • Represents Indian exporters at national and international forums
  • Provides market intelligence, trade facilitation, and policy advocacy
  • Supports capacity building and competitiveness of exporters
  • Supported by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Apex coordinating body of Export Promotion Councils
  • Advisory body; not a regulator or statutory authority
Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) Export Promotion Council 1966 Section 8 Company under the Companies Act, 2013
  • Promotes exports of gems and jewellery
  • Organises trade fairs, buyer–seller meets, and international exhibitions
  • Supports skill development and capacity building in the sector
  • Recognised by and works under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Largest export promotion council in India by export value
  • Plays a key role in branding and global positioning of Indian jewellery
India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) Trade Promotion Organisation 1977 Government Company under the Companies Act
  • Organises domestic and international trade fairs and exhibitions
  • Promotes Indian trade, commerce, and industry globally
  • Provides exhibition and convention infrastructure
  • Functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Manages the Pragati Maidan complex in New Delhi
  • Key institutional platform for international trade engagement
Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) Statutory Export Promotion Authority 1972 Marine Products Export Development Authority Act, 1972
  • Promotes development and export of marine products
  • Regulates quality control, certification, and export standards for marine products
  • Supports infrastructure development, market promotion, and traceability systems
  • Statutory body under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Performs both promotional and regulatory functions
  • Plays a key role in fisheries exports, including sustainability and residue compliance
Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) Statutory Export Promotion Authority 1985 Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act, 1985
  • Promotes development and export of agricultural and processed food products
  • Regulates quality control, certification, and traceability systems for exports
  • Facilitates market access, infrastructure development, and exporter registration
  • Statutory body under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Plays a key role in organic, Geographical Indication (GI), and value-added agri exports
  • Performs both promotional and regulatory functions
Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) Trade Regulatory Authority (Executive Body) 1991 Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992
  • Formulates and implements the Foreign Trade Policy of India
  • Regulates imports and exports through licensing and authorisation
  • Issues Importer Exporter Code (IEC) to exporters and importers
  • Functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
  • Principal executive arm for trade regulation and export–import controls
  • Administers export promotion and incentive schemes under Foreign Trade Policy
MSME & Rural Promotion Institutions
National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) Public Sector Undertaking – MSME Support Institution 1955 Government Company under the Companies Act
  • Promotes growth and competitiveness of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)
  • Provides marketing support, credit facilitation, and technology assistance
  • Facilitates MSME participation in government procurement
  • Functions under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
  • Implements the Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) for MSMEs
  • Acts as a nodal support agency for MSME development
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) Statutory Rural Industry Promotion Body 1957 Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956
  • Promotes development of khadi and village industries
  • Generates employment in rural and semi-urban areas
  • Supports sustainable livelihoods and self-reliant local economies
  • Statutory body under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
  • Implements the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
  • Institutional embodiment of Gandhian economic philosophy
Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) Public Sector Undertaking (Trading and Procurement Agency) 1970 Government Company under the Companies Act
  • Procures cotton at Minimum Support Price (MSP) on behalf of the Government of India
  • Stabilises cotton prices and ensures remunerative returns to farmers
  • Supplies cotton to the domestic textile industry
  • Functions under the Ministry of Textiles
  • Nodal agency for MSP operations in cotton (along with state agencies)
  • Not an export promotion body; role is domestic market intervention
Policy and Governance Institutions
Registrar of Companies (RoC) Corporate Compliance Authority 1956 Companies Act, 1956 / 2013
  • Registers companies and LLPs
  • Ensures statutory compliance under Companies Act
  • Maintains corporate records and filings
  • Functions under Ministry of Corporate Affairs
  • First point of regulatory interface for companies
  • Important for corporate governance enforcement
Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council (PMEAC) Economic Policy Advisory Body 2004 Executive Order of the Prime Minister
  • Advises the Prime Minister on macroeconomic policy and economic trends
  • Provides independent analysis on growth, inflation, employment, and fiscal issues
  • Publishes reports and policy notes on the Indian economy
  • Executive advisory body; not statutory or constitutional
  • Composed of eminent economists
  • No regulatory, financial, or implementation powers
National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) Policy Think Tank 2015 Executive Resolution of the Union Government
  • Provides policy advice on economic and social development
  • Promotes cooperative and competitive federalism
  • Acts as a platform for Centre–State coordination on development priorities
  • Replaced the Planning Commission
  • Does not allocate funds or approve projects
  • Plays an advisory role in reforms, policy innovation, and long-term vision
Training Institutions
National Academy of Customs, Indirect Taxes and Narcotics (NACIN) Fiscal and Taxation Training Academy 1986 Executive decision (Department of Revenue)
  • Trains officers in customs, indirect taxes, and GST administration
  • Builds capacity in fiscal enforcement and tax compliance
  • Supports implementation of indirect tax reforms
  • Functions under the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue)
  • Sector-specific fiscal training institution
  • Economy-focused through taxation and revenue administration
National Institute of Financial Management (NIFM) Public Financial Management Training and Capacity-Building Institute 1993 Executive Decision of the Ministry of Finance
  • Trains government officers in public financial management
  • Provides courses on budgeting, accounting, audit, and fiscal policy
  • Supports capacity building in public finance and fiscal governance
  • Functions under the Ministry of Finance
  • Primarily caters to civil services and public sector officials
  • Merged into the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP) framework as part of institutional restructuring
National Institute of Financial Management (NIFM) Public Financial Management Training and Capacity-Building Institute 1993 Executive Decision of the Ministry of Finance
  • Trains government officers in public financial management
  • Provides courses on budgeting, accounting, audit, and fiscal policy
  • Supports capacity building in public finance and fiscal governance
  • Functions under the Ministry of Finance
  • Primarily caters to civil services and public sector officials
  • Merged into the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP) framework as part of institutional restructuring
Centre for Advanced Financial Research and Learning (CAFRAL) Financial Sector Research and Capacity-Building Institution 2011 Not-for-profit institution (supported by RBI)
  • Conducts research on banking, financial markets, and macro-finance
  • Provides advanced training to financial sector regulators and policymakers
  • Supports financial stability and regulatory capacity building
  • Supported by the Reserve Bank of India
  • Purely economy and finance focused
  • No regulatory or supervisory powers
Defunct / Merged Financial Bodies
Planning Commission Defunct Central Planning Body 1950 Executive Resolution of the Union Government
  • Formulated Five-Year Plans for economic and social development
  • Allocated plan funds to Union Ministries and States
  • Set national development priorities under planned economy framework
  • Abolished in 2015
  • Replaced by the National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)
  • Key shift from centralised planning to cooperative federalism
Forward Markets Commission (FMC) Defunct Commodity Derivatives Market Regulator 1953 Forward Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1952
  • Regulated commodity futures and forward markets in India
  • Supervised commodity exchanges dealing in agricultural and non-agricultural commodities
  • Ensured orderly development and integrity of the commodity derivatives market
  • Merged with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in 2015
  • All regulatory powers transferred to SEBI
  • Important Prelims trap: FMC no longer exists as a separate regulator
Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Commission (MRTPC) Defunct Competition Regulation Authority 1969 Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969
  • Prevented concentration of economic power
  • Restricted monopolistic and restrictive trade practices
  • Enforced competition-related provisions under controlled economy
  • Abolished with repeal of MRTP Act
  • Replaced by Competition Commission of India (CCI)
  • Shift from control-based to competition-based economic policy
Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) Defunct Sick Industry Resolution Authority 1987 Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985
  • Identified and rehabilitated sick industrial companies
  • Recommended revival, merger, or winding up of sick units
  • Provided protection from creditor action
  • Abolished with enactment of Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
  • Replaced by time-bound insolvency resolution under NCLT
  • Important Prelims trap: BIFR no longer exists
Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) Defunct FDI Approval Body 1991 Executive Resolution of the Union Government
  • Approved Foreign Direct Investment proposals under government route
  • Facilitated foreign investment inflows into India
  • Coordinated FDI policy implementation
  • Abolished in 2017
  • FDI approvals shifted to automatic route and concerned ministries
  • Reflects liberalisation and ease of doing business reforms
- Important financial acts and rules (validated) -
Act/Rule Category Year Purpose Key Provisions/Additional Details
Constitutional & Core Banking Laws
Reserve Bank of India Act Central Banking Law 1934
  • Establishes the Reserve Bank of India as the central bank
  • Provides framework for monetary policy and currency issuance
  • Defines RBI’s role as banker to government and banks
  • Statutory basis of RBI
  • Provides for Monetary Policy Committee
  • Foundation of India’s monetary system
Banking Regulation Act Banking Regulation Law 1949
  • Regulates functioning of banking companies in India
  • Empowers RBI to supervise, license, and regulate banks
  • Provides norms for management, capital, and audits
  • Applies to commercial banks and cooperative banks
  • Key instrument of RBI’s supervisory control
  • Frequently asked in UPSC Prelims
State Bank of India Act Public Sector Banking Law 1955
  • Establishes State Bank of India as a public sector bank
  • Defines its governance, functions, and capital structure
  • Provides statutory backing to India’s largest bank
  • Successor to Imperial Bank of India
  • Key instrument for government banking operations
  • Frequently paired with RBI Act in UPSC questions
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Acts Bank Nationalisation Law 1970, 1980
  • Provides for nationalisation of major commercial banks
  • Transfers ownership and control to Government of India
  • Aims to expand banking to priority sectors
  • 1970 Act: nationalised 14 banks
  • 1980 Act: nationalised 6 banks
  • Foundation of public sector banking system
Monetary, Credit & Payment System Laws
Negotiable Instruments Act Payment Instruments Law 1881
  • Governs negotiable instruments such as cheques, promissory notes, and bills of exchange
  • Defines rights, liabilities, and transferability of such instruments
  • Provides legal framework for cheque-based payments
  • Section 138 deals with cheque dishonour
  • Criminal liability for cheque bounce
  • Frequently asked in Prelims (sections-based questions)
Bankers’ Books Evidence Act Banking Evidence Law 1891
  • Recognises bank records as admissible legal evidence
  • Facilitates use of banking documents in judicial proceedings
  • Reduces requirement of producing original books
  • Amended to include electronic records
  • Important for fraud, recovery, and prosecution cases
  • Often paired with Negotiable Instruments Act
Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act Credit Information Regulation Law 2005
  • Regulates credit information companies (credit bureaus)
  • Facilitates sharing of credit data among banks and financial institutions
  • Improves credit discipline and risk assessment
  • Empowers RBI to regulate credit bureaus
  • Legal basis for CIBIL and similar entities
  • Relevant for financial inclusion and lending reforms
Payment and Settlement Systems Act Payment Systems Regulation Law 2007
  • Provides legal framework for regulation of payment systems
  • Empowers RBI to authorise and supervise payment systems
  • Ensures safety and efficiency of electronic payments
  • Covers systems such as RTGS, NEFT, UPI, cards
  • Statutory basis for digital payments regulation
  • Important for questions on fintech and digital economy
Financial Stability, Recovery & Insolvency Laws
State Financial Corporations Act State-Level Development Finance Law 1951
  • Provides for establishment of State Financial Corporations (SFCs)
  • Supports industrial development at the state level
  • Facilitates credit to small and medium industries
  • Applies primarily to state-level industrial finance
  • Distinct from central DFIs like IFCI and SIDBI
  • Occasionally asked in Prelims as a pair with IFCI Act
Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act Deposit Protection Law 1961
  • Provides insurance cover to bank depositors
  • Ensures confidence and stability in the banking system
  • Protects small depositors in case of bank failure
  • DICGC is a subsidiary of RBI
  • Covers commercial banks and eligible cooperative banks
  • Important for questions on banking safety nets
Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act Debt Recovery Law 1993
  • Provides for establishment of Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs)
  • Facilitates speedy recovery of debts due to banks and financial institutions
  • Reduces burden on civil courts
  • Originally named RDDBFI Act, 1993
  • Applies to secured and unsecured bank debts
  • Often compared with SARFAESI Act in UPSC questions
Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act (SARFAESI) Asset Recovery Law 2002
  • Empowers banks to enforce security interests without court intervention
  • Allows seizure and sale of secured assets
  • Facilitates resolution of non-performing assets (NPAs)
  • Applies only to secured loans
  • Does not apply to agricultural land
  • Key Prelims distinction: SARFAESI vs IBC
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code Comprehensive Insolvency Law 2016
  • Provides time-bound insolvency resolution framework
  • Consolidates laws relating to insolvency of corporate persons and individuals
  • Aims to maximise value of assets and balance stakeholder interests
  • Establishes Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI)
  • Adjudicating authorities: NCLT and DRT
  • Cornerstone reform for banking sector clean-up
Foreign Exchange & External Sector Laws
Customs Act Trade Taxation Law 1962
  • Governs levy and collection of customs duties
  • Regulates import and export of goods
  • Prevents smuggling and illegal trade
  • Administered by Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
  • Provides powers of search, seizure, and adjudication
  • Core law for international trade taxation
Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act Foreign Trade Regulation Law 1992
  • Provides legal framework for development and regulation of foreign trade
  • Empowers Central Government to formulate Foreign Trade Policy
  • Regulates imports and exports
  • Implemented through Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)
  • Basis for export promotion and trade control measures
  • Frequently asked in context of EXIM policy
Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) Foreign Exchange Regulation Law 1999
  • Regulates foreign exchange transactions in India
  • Facilitates external trade and payments
  • Promotes orderly development of foreign exchange market
  • Replaced the more restrictive FERA, 1973
  • Administered by RBI and Directorate of Enforcement
  • Violations are civil offences in nature
Taxation Laws (Direct & Indirect)
Central Excise Act Indirect Tax Law (Residual) 1944
  • Provided for levy of excise duty on manufacture of goods
  • Regulated production and clearance of excisable goods
  • Largely subsumed under GST in 2017
  • Still applicable to limited products such as petroleum and tobacco
  • Important Prelims trap: not fully repealed
Central Sales Tax Act Indirect Tax Law (Inter-State Trade) 1956
  • Regulated taxation of inter-state sale of goods
  • Provided legal basis for levy and collection of CST
  • Substantially subsumed under GST
  • Still relevant for certain non-GST goods
  • Frequently paired with GST in UPSC questions
Income Tax Act Direct Tax Law 1961
  • Provides legal framework for levy and collection of income tax
  • Defines taxable income, exemptions, deductions, and assessment procedures
  • Applies to individuals, firms, companies, and other entities
  • Administered by Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)
  • Core statute for direct taxation in India
  • Frequently asked in UPSC Prelims and GS-III
Goods and Services Tax Acts Comprehensive Indirect Tax Law 2017
  • Introduces destination-based value-added tax system
  • Subsumes multiple central and state indirect taxes
  • Creates uniform indirect tax structure across India
  • Includes CGST, IGST, and UTGST Acts
  • Administered jointly by Centre and States
  • Backed constitutionally by the 101st Amendment
Finance Act Annual Taxation and Budget Law Annual
  • Gives legal effect to Union Budget proposals
  • Amends tax laws and authorises taxation measures
  • Provides statutory backing to fiscal policy changes
  • Passed every year by Parliament
  • Amends Income Tax, GST, Customs and other tax laws
  • Important UPSC distinction: not a permanent statute
Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act Tax Law Amendment 2021
  • Amends existing taxation laws
  • Provides clarity and certainty in tax regime
  • Addresses specific tax disputes and issues
  • Not a standalone tax code
  • Illustrates Parliament’s power to amend tax statutes
  • Often linked to retrospective taxation debates
Fiscal Management & Public Finance Laws
Public Debt Act Public Debt Management Law 1944
  • Provides legal framework for management of government borrowing
  • Authorises issuance and servicing of government securities
  • Regulates ownership and transfer of public debt instruments
  • Administered by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of Government
  • Foundation law for internal public debt
  • Often read with Government Securities Act
Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act Fiscal Discipline Law 2003
  • Provides statutory framework for fiscal discipline
  • Aims to reduce fiscal deficit and revenue deficit
  • Promotes transparency in fiscal operations of government
  • Applies to Central Government
  • Provides for fiscal targets and reporting requirements
  • Central to debates on fiscal consolidation
Government Securities Act Government Securities Regulation Law 2006
  • Consolidates laws relating to government securities
  • Provides for issue, holding, and transfer of government securities
  • Facilitates modernisation of government debt market
  • Complements the Public Debt Act
  • Provides legal backing to dematerialised government securities
  • Important for understanding G-Sec market structure
General Financial Rules Public Financial Management Rules 2017
  • Lay down principles for government financial administration
  • Regulate procurement, expenditure, and accounting procedures
  • Ensure economy, efficiency, and transparency in public spending
  • Issued by Ministry of Finance
  • Applicable to all Central Government ministries and departments
  • Important for questions on public procurement and finance rules
Corporate, Market & Competition Laws
Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act Securities Trading Regulation Law 1956
  • Regulates stock exchanges and securities contracts
  • Provides legal framework for recognition of stock exchanges
  • Controls trading in securities
  • Empowers Central Government and SEBI
  • Foundation law for exchange-based securities trading
  • Often tested with SEBI Act in Prelims
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act Capital Market Regulation Law 1992
  • Establishes SEBI as the capital market regulator
  • Protects interests of investors in securities
  • Promotes orderly development of securities market
  • SEBI has quasi-legislative, executive, and judicial powers
  • Core law for regulation of stock markets
  • Often paired with SCRA in UPSC questions
Competition Act Competition Regulation Law 2002
  • Prevents practices having adverse effect on competition
  • Promotes and sustains competition in markets
  • Protects interests of consumers
  • Establishes Competition Commission of India (CCI)
  • Replaced the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969
  • Regulates cartels, abuse of dominance, and combinations
Companies Act Corporate Governance Law 2013
  • Regulates incorporation, functioning, and winding up of companies
  • Provides framework for corporate governance and disclosures
  • Defines roles of directors, shareholders, and management
  • Administered by Ministry of Corporate Affairs
  • Introduced mandatory corporate social responsibility provisions
  • Replaced the Companies Act, 1956
Securities Laws (Amendment) Act Capital Market Enforcement Law 2014
  • Strengthens enforcement powers of SEBI
  • Enhances penalties for securities market violations
  • Targets market manipulation and fraud
  • Amends SEBI Act, SCRA, and Depositories Act
  • Introduced powers of search, seizure, and attachment
  • Important for questions on market integrity
Insurance, Pension & Social Security Laws
Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act Social Security Law 1952
  • Provides statutory social security to employees
  • Covers provident fund, pension, and insurance benefits
  • Ensures retirement income security
  • Administered by Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)
  • Applies to establishments above prescribed employment threshold
  • Frequently cited in questions on labour welfare
Life Insurance Corporation Act Public Sector Insurance Law 1956
  • Provides for nationalisation of life insurance business
  • Establishes Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)
  • Ensures spread of life insurance in the public interest
  • Nationalised 245 private life insurers
  • Creates a statutory corporation under Government of India
  • Cornerstone of India’s life insurance sector
Payment of Bonus Act Labour Welfare (Financial) Law 1965
  • Provides for payment of bonus to employees
  • Links bonus with profits or productivity
  • Aims at equitable sharing of profits
  • Applies to establishments meeting prescribed criteria
  • Part of labour welfare legislation with financial implications
  • Relevant for social security and labour policy questions
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act Insurance Regulation Law 1999
  • Establishes IRDAI as regulator of insurance sector
  • Protects interests of policyholders
  • Promotes orderly growth of insurance industry
  • Regulates life, general, and health insurance
  • Prescribes solvency and prudential norms
  • Key law for liberalisation of insurance sector
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority Act Pension Regulation Law 2013
  • Establishes PFRDA as pension sector regulator
  • Regulates National Pension System (NPS)
  • Promotes retirement savings and income security
  • Covers government and private sector subscribers
  • Provides framework for pension fund management
  • Important for old-age social security reforms
Financial Integrity & Economic Offences Laws
Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act Anti-Black Money Law 1988 (Amended 2016)
  • Prohibits benami property transactions
  • Deters concealment of ownership to evade taxes
  • Provides for confiscation of benami assets
  • Administered by Income Tax Department
  • 2016 amendment strengthened penalties and enforcement
  • Frequently paired with Black Money Act in UPSC
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act Foreign Funding Regulation Law 2010
  • Regulates acceptance and utilisation of foreign contributions
  • Ensures foreign funds do not affect national interest
  • Promotes transparency and accountability
  • Administered by Ministry of Home Affairs
  • Applies to NGOs, associations, and individuals
  • Frequently asked in governance-security linkage questions
Prevention of Money Laundering Act Anti-Money Laundering Law 2002
  • Prevents money laundering and related financial crimes
  • Provides for attachment and confiscation of proceeds of crime
  • Creates obligations for reporting entities
  • Enforced by Enforcement Directorate (ED)
  • Establishes Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND)
  • Linked to FATF compliance
Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) Act Foreign Undisclosed Assets Law 2015
  • Targets undisclosed foreign income and assets
  • Provides for stringent penalties and prosecution
  • Complements Income Tax Act
  • Separate from PMLA and Benami Act
  • Applies only to foreign assets
  • Important distinction for Prelims
Fugitive Economic Offenders Act Economic Offenders Law 2018
  • Addresses economic offenders who evade Indian law by remaining abroad
  • Provides for confiscation of properties of fugitive offenders
  • Deters large-scale financial fraud
  • Applies to offences involving large financial values
  • Administered through special courts
  • Important for banking fraud context
Development Finance & Infrastructure Laws
Industrial Finance Corporation of India Act Industrial Development Finance Law 1948
  • Establishes Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI)
  • Provides long-term finance to industrial undertakings
  • Supports post-Independence industrialisation
  • India’s first Development Finance Institution
  • Provides term loans and underwriting support
  • Important historical DFI for UPSC economy questions
Export-Import Bank of India Act Trade Finance Law 1981
  • Establishes EXIM Bank as India’s export credit agency
  • Provides financial assistance for exports and imports
  • Supports India’s external trade and project exports
  • Wholly owned by Government of India
  • Provides lines of credit and buyer’s credit
  • Key institution for trade finance questions
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act Rural Development Finance Law 1981
  • Establishes NABARD as apex institution for rural credit
  • Provides refinance to banks for agriculture and rural development
  • Promotes sustainable rural finance systems
  • Supervises Regional Rural Banks and cooperative banks
  • Key institution for agriculture and rural credit
  • Frequently asked in GS-III
Small Industries Development Bank of India Act MSME Development Finance Law 1989
  • Establishes SIDBI as principal financial institution for MSMEs
  • Provides refinance and direct lending support
  • Promotes micro, small, and medium enterprises
  • Subsidiary of RBI originally, now under Government of India
  • Supports entrepreneurship and MSME growth
  • Frequently paired with NABARD in UPSC questions
National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development Act Infrastructure Finance Law 2021
  • Establishes NaBFID as a dedicated infrastructure DFI
  • Provides long-term finance for infrastructure projects
  • Supports National Infrastructure Pipeline
  • Addresses infrastructure financing gap
  • Provides development and refinancing functions
  • Important for new-age infrastructure financing questions
Housing, Real Estate & Non-Banking Finance Laws
Chit Funds Act Non-Banking Financial Regulation Law 1982
  • Regulates conduct of chit fund businesses
  • Protects interests of subscribers
  • Provides legal framework for traditional savings schemes
  • Administered primarily by State Governments
  • Distinct from NBFC regulation under RBI
  • Important for informal finance questions
National Housing Bank Act Housing Finance Regulation Law 1987
  • Establishes National Housing Bank (NHB)
  • Acts as apex institution for housing finance
  • Promotes development of housing finance institutions
  • Originally a subsidiary of RBI
  • Now under administrative control of Ministry of Finance
  • Important for housing finance ecosystem questions
Factoring Regulation Act NBFC & MSME Finance Law 2011
  • Regulates factoring business in India
  • Facilitates conversion of receivables into immediate liquidity
  • Supports MSME cash-flow management
  • Regulated by Reserve Bank of India
  • Linked to Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS)
  • Relevant for MSME financing reforms
Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act Real Estate Regulation Law 2016
  • Regulates real estate sector to protect homebuyers
  • Ensures transparency and accountability in real estate projects
  • Mandates registration of real estate projects and agents
  • Establishes State-level Real Estate Regulatory Authorities
  • Applies to residential and commercial real estate
  • Frequently cited reform in housing sector
Labour, Welfare & Miscellaneous Financial Laws
Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act Labour Social Security Law 1952
  • Provides compulsory social security to employees
  • Covers provident fund, pension, and insurance benefits
  • Aims at income security after retirement
  • Administered by EPFO under Ministry of Labour
  • Applies to notified establishments
  • Frequently asked in labour–economy linkage questions
Payment of Bonus Act Labour Welfare (Financial) Law 1965
  • Provides for payment of bonus to employees
  • Links bonus with profits or productivity
  • Ensures fair distribution of surplus
  • Applies to establishments meeting prescribed conditions
  • Part of statutory wage framework
  • Occasionally asked in labour reforms context
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act Foreign Funding Regulation Law 2010
  • Regulates acceptance and utilisation of foreign contributions
  • Prevents misuse of foreign funds affecting national interest
  • Ensures transparency and accountability
  • Administered by Ministry of Home Affairs
  • Applies to NGOs, associations, and individuals
  • Frequently tested in governance–security linkage
General Financial Rules Public Financial Administration Rules 2017
  • Lay down principles of government financial management
  • Regulate procurement, expenditure, and accounting
  • Ensure economy, efficiency, and transparency
  • Issued by Ministry of Finance
  • Applicable to all Central Government departments
  • Important for public finance and governance questions
- Important government policies related to different spheres (validated) -
Policy Sphere Year Objective Key Features and Details Eligibility and Impact
Agriculture, Food Security & Allied Policies
National Agricultural Policy Agriculture 2000
  • Achieve sustainable agricultural growth
  • Enhance productivity and profitability of farming
  • Ensure food and nutritional security
  • Targets higher agricultural growth through diversification
  • Emphasises irrigation, credit, technology, and private investment
  • Promotes environmentally sustainable farming practices
  • Applies to all farmers, including small and marginal
  • Forms policy base for later schemes like PMKSY and PMFBY
  • GS-III: Agriculture
National Policy on Cooperatives Cooperatives 2002
  • Strengthen cooperative movement
  • Enhance democratic and professional functioning
  • Support rural and agricultural economy
  • Encourages autonomy and member participation
  • Supports agricultural, dairy, and credit cooperatives
  • Important backdrop for cooperative reforms
  • Applies to cooperative societies across sectors
  • GS-III: Economy, Rural Development
National Policy for Farmers Agriculture 2007
  • Improve economic viability of farming
  • Ensure income security for farmers
  • Reduce agrarian distress
  • Based on recommendations of M.S. Swaminathan Commission
  • Emphasises MSP, crop insurance, credit access
  • Focuses on risk management and climate resilience
  • Covers all categories of farmers
  • Important for questions on MSP and farmer income debates
  • GS-III: Agriculture, Economy
National Food Security Policy Food Security 2013
  • Ensure access to affordable food for vulnerable sections
  • Reduce hunger and malnutrition
  • Strengthen public distribution system
  • Operationalised through National Food Security Act
  • Legal entitlement to subsidised food grains
  • Special focus on women and children
  • Covers priority households and Antyodaya families
  • Critical for GS-II (Social Justice) and GS-III linkage
National Policy on Marine Fisheries Fisheries 2017
  • Promote sustainable marine fisheries
  • Enhance fish production and exports
  • Improve livelihoods of fisherfolk
  • Encourages responsible fishing practices
  • Focus on infrastructure, post-harvest management
  • Linked with PMMSY implementation
  • Targets marine fisher communities
  • Important for GS-III (Agriculture, Blue Economy)
Health, Education & Human Development Policies
National Health Policy Health 2017
  • Achieve universal access to quality healthcare
  • Shift focus from curative to preventive healthcare

Organization Time Location Formation Purpose Details Members
International Labour Organization (ILO) 1919 Geneva, Switzerland Established under Treaty of Versailles post-WWI as part of League of Nations. Promote labor rights, social justice, decent work conditions.
  • Adopts conventions on child labor, wages.
  • Became UN agency in 1946.
  • Criticized for weak enforcement.
  • 187 members (e.g., USA, Brazil, Japan).
  • India: Joined in 1919 as founding member.
League of Nations 1920 Geneva, Switzerland Formed post-WWI via Treaty of Versailles, proposed by Woodrow Wilson. Prevent conflicts, promote global cooperation.
  • Failed to stop WWII due to weak enforcement.
  • U.S. non-membership limited authority.
  • Dissolved in 1946, succeeded by UN.
  • 58 at peak (e.g., UK, France, Japan).
  • India: Joined in 1920 as a British colony.
Bank for International Settlements (BIS) 1930 Basel, Switzerland Created to manage German reparations post-WWI, foster central bank cooperation. Promote monetary, financial stability.
  • Facilitates global financial coordination.
  • Criticized for favoring rich nations.
  • 63 central banks (e.g., Federal Reserve, ECB).
  • India: Joined in 1996.
United Nations (UN) 1945 New York, USA Founded post-WWII via UN Charter, succeeding League of Nations.
  • Maintain peace, security.
  • Promote human rights, development.
  • Oversees WHO, UNESCO.
  • Security Council veto power criticized.
  • Mediates conflicts, provides aid.
  • 193 members (e.g., USA, China, Nigeria).
  • India: Joined in 1945 as founding member.
International Monetary Fund (IMF) 1945 Washington, D.C., USA Established at Bretton Woods Conference post-WWII.
  • Ensure monetary stability.
  • Provide financial assistance.
  • Provides loans with conditions.
  • Criticized for austerity measures.
  • 190 members (e.g., Germany, Brazil).
  • India: Joined in 1945 as founding member.
World Bank 1944 Washington, D.C. Supports reconstruction and development. Comprises IBRD and IDA.
  • Long-term loans and grants.
  • Low-interest financing.
  • Funds infrastructure, health, education, governance.
  • Difference from IMF:
  • IMF: Short-term stabilization loans.
  • Targets currency, economy, fiscal deficit.
  • Comes with austerity & reform conditions.
  • World Bank: Long-term development loans.
  • Used for roads, dams, ports.
  • Used for skill development.
  • Used for water & sanitation.
  • Used for digital governance.
  • 189 members.
  • Major development partner for India.
General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) 1947 Geneva, Switzerland Created post-WWII to reduce trade barriers, predecessor to WTO. Promote free trade via tariff reductions.
  • Facilitated trade liberalization.
  • Replaced by WTO in 1995.
  • 128 at dissolution (e.g., USA, UK).

North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) 1949 Brussels, Belgium Formed via North Atlantic Treaty to counter Soviet threat. Ensure collective defense.
  • Article 5 invoked post-9/11.
  • Expanded post-Cold War.
  • 32 members (e.g., USA, Germany, Sweden).
  • India: Not a member; NATO focuses on North Atlantic, India pursues non-alignment.
Organization of American States (OAS) 1948 Washington, D.C., USA Established via Charter of Bogotá, building on Pan-American conferences.

  • Support democracy, security.

  • 35 members (e.g., Brazil, Canada).

Warsaw Pact 1955 Moscow, USSR Formed in response to NATO, West Germany’s rearmament. Provide Soviet bloc defense during Cold War.

  • Dissolved in 1991 after USSR collapse.
  • 8 at dissolution (e.g., USSR, Poland).

European Economic Community (EEC) 1957 Brussels, Belgium Created by Treaty of Rome for economic integration. Promote free trade, cooperation in Europe.

Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) 1960 Vienna, Austria Founded by five oil-producing nations for petroleum policies. Stabilize oil markets, ensure supply.

- All constitutional articles, laws, policies, initiatives, etc for for family and society (Unverified) -
CategoryNameKey Provisions/AspectsImpact/Status (2024-2025)
Constitutional Articles
Constitutional ArticlesArticle 14: Equality Before LawEnsures equality before law and equal protection of laws; prohibits arbitrary discrimination in family matters (e.g., inheritance, marriage).Upheld in *Shayara Bano v. UOI (2017)* banning triple talaq; supports gender equity in family laws; 4.45 lakh crimes against women (2022) show enforcement gaps.
Article 15: Prohibition of DiscriminationBans discrimination on religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth; allows affirmative action for women/children (Clause 3), backward classes (Clause 5).Enables women’s reservation (2023 Bill); supports BBBP; NFHS-5 (2019-21): 57% women anemic, highlighting gender disparities.
Article 16: Equality in Public EmploymentEnsures equal opportunity in public jobs; allows reservations (Clause 4); promotes family stability via economic security.Backed 33% women’s reservation in SCBA (2024 SC ruling); FLFP: 41.7%; intersects with POSH Act for workplace equity.
Article 21: Right to Life and Personal LibertyProtects life, liberty, dignity; includes privacy, health, family planning; covers domestic violence, reproductive rights, elderly care.Upheld in *Suchita Srivastava (2009)* for reproductive choice; basis for PWDVA; 150M+ elderly, 6% live alone (Kerala).
Article 39: Directive Principles for WelfareDirects equal pay (Clause a), adequate livelihood (Clause d), protection of children/youth (Clause f); basis for family welfare policies.Supports PMMVY, Ujjwala; wage gap persists (women earn ₹40 per ₹100 for men); shapes family planning policies.
Article 42: Humane Work Conditions & Maternity ReliefEnsures humane work conditions, maternity relief; basis for childcare, paid leave policies.Supports PMMVY, Palna; 26-week maternity leave (2017); women spend 10x more on unpaid care work (NSSO 2019).
Article 44: Uniform Civil Code (UCC)Directs state to secure UCC for all citizens; aims for uniform family laws (e.g., marriage, divorce, inheritance).Debates ongoing (Chapter 7); Shah Bano case (1985) highlighted UCC need; supports gender equity but faces communal resistance.
Laws
LawsHindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005Gives daughters equal coparcenary rights in ancestral property; applies retrospectively; removes Section 23 restrictions.*Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020)* clarified retrospective application; 40% women lack property rights (Oxfam 2023).
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA), 2005Defines broad domestic violence (physical, emotional, sexual, economic); offers protection orders, residence rights, monetary relief; covers live-in relationships.3.2 lakh cases processed (2022); 31.4% cases involve cruelty by husband/relatives; *S.R. Batra (2007)* clarified residence rights.
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act, 2013Mandates Internal Complaints Committees; defines harassment; requires training, reports; penalties up to ₹50,000.422 cases (2022); 36% firms non-compliant (FICCI-EY 2015); Vishaka Guidelines (1997) precursor; 2024 SC directive for women’s SCBA quota.
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2024Replaces IPC; strengthens sexual offense penalties (rape: 20 years-life); decriminalizes adultery (gender-neutral); no marital rape provision.Effective July 2024; 4.45 lakh crimes against women (2022); *Joseph Shine (2018)* decriminalized adultery; criticized for marital rape omission (Chapter 7).
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012Protects children (<18) from sexual abuse; defines offenses, child-friendly procedures; mandatory reporting; penalties up to life imprisonment.1.5 lakh cases (2022); 23.3% girls married before 18; strengthens child safety in families; enforcement gaps in rural areas.
Policies, Initiatives, Schemes
Policies/Initiatives/SchemesMission Shakti (Sambal & Samarthya)Sambal: One Stop Centres, Women Helplines (181), BBBP, Nari Adalats.
Samarthya: Shakti Sadans, Sakhi Niwas, Palna, PMMVY, NHEW.		404 Shakti Sadans, 523 Sakhi Niwas, 2.92M beneficiaries (2014-2024); boosts FLFP (41.7%), family safety.
Shakti Sadan SchemeRehabilitation homes for women in distress/trafficking; provides shelter, counseling, legal aid, vocational training; ₹500 monthly deposit.35 in Assam (2024); 292,681 women supported (2014-2024); aids family reintegration.
Palna (Creche Scheme)Safe creches for children (0-6) of working mothers; linked to Sakhi Niwas; boosts women’s workforce participation.50 new Sakhi Niwas (2024); reduces childcare burden; supports 41.7% FLFP.
Sakhi Niwas (Working Women Hostel)Affordable hostels for working women; includes daycare; financial aid for rented facilities.523 functional (2024); 50 new planned; empowers urban migrant women.
Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)₹5,000 for first child, ₹6,000 for second girl child; conditional on health checkups; compensates maternity wage loss.3.4 crore beneficiaries (2024); extended to second girl child (2021); MMR down to 97/100,000.
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)Prevents sex-selective elimination; promotes girl child survival, education; enforces PCPNDT Act.SRB: 929 (NFHS-5); ₹96.71 crore spent on ads (2020); 23.3% child marriages persist.
Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)Free LPG connections to BPL women; reduces indoor pollution; promotes family health.10.3 crore connections (2024); 4.2 refills/year; cuts respiratory illnesses for women, children, elderly.
First Five-Year Plan (1951-56)Focused on agriculture, irrigation, community development; family welfare via health centers; refugee rehabilitation post-partition.3.6% growth; laid foundation for rural family health, family planning; addressed poverty (25.7% in 2011, <5% in 2024).
Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61)Industrialization, heavy industries; expanded family planning, women’s employment via labor policies.4.1% growth; introduced family planning department; set stage for population control policies.
Family Planning Department (1952)Established under Ministry of Health; promotes contraception, maternal/child health; later integrated into National Population Policy.Reduced TFR from 6 (1950s) to 2 (2020); supports family welfare; rural gaps remain (NFHS-5).
National Population Policy (NPP), 2000Aims for TFR of 2.1; promotes maternal/child health, contraception access, gender equity in family planning.TFR: 2 (NFHS-5); increased contraceptive use (56.5%); supports PMMVY, Mission Parivar Vikas; rural awareness low.
Emergency (1975-77)Controversial family planning drive; coercive sterilizations (8.3M in 1976-77); aimed to curb population growth.Backlash reduced trust in family planning; TFR decline slowed; shaped cautious approach in NPP 2000.
Mission Parivar Vikas (2016)Targets 146 high-fertility districts; promotes modern contraceptives, family planning awareness; focuses on rural women, youth.Increased contraceptive prevalence (56.5% in NFHS-5); supports TFR reduction; aligns with PMMVY.
National Health Mission (NHM), 2005Improves maternal/child health, family welfare; includes ASHA workers, Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), rural health infrastructure.JSY: 10 crore beneficiaries (2024); MMR: 97/100,000; IMR: 27/1000; rural health gaps persist.
Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB), 2015Promotes cultural integration, social cohesion via state-to-state partnerships; strengthens family/societal unity across diversity.Over 100 paired activities (2024); counters communalism (Chapter 7); fosters social harmony via cultural exchange.
Supreme Court Directions/Cases
Supreme Court Directions/CasesVishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)Established guidelines against workplace sexual harassment; mandated committees, policies; precursor to POSH Act 2013.Laid groundwork for POSH; 422 harassment cases (2022); 2024 SC directive for SCBA women’s quota reinforces.
Shayara Bano v. UOI (2017)Declared triple talaq unconstitutional; upheld women’s rights under Article 14; led to Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.Reduced triple talaq cases; supports UCC (Chapter 7); 26% Muslim women in segregated areas face ongoing challenges.
Joseph Shine v. UOI (2018)Decriminalized adultery (Section 497 IPC); made it gender-neutral; protected family dignity and individual autonomy.Reflected in BNS 2024; reduces patriarchal control in family law; marital rape exclusion criticized.
Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020)Clarified Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act 2005; daughters have equal coparcenary rights retrospectively.Enhanced women’s property rights; 40% women still lack access (Oxfam 2023); strengthens family equity.
Laxmi v. UOI (2014)Directed stricter acid attack regulations; mandated compensation, medical support; influenced BNS 2024 provisions.Reduced acid attacks (300 cases in 2022); supports PWDVA; enhances women’s safety in families.

Constitutional Bodies

National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)Statutory body (CPCR Act, 2005); monitors child rights (e.g., POCSO, RTE); advises on family, education policies; investigates child labor, trafficking.1.5 lakh cases (2022); 23.3% girls married before 18; supports BBBP, Palna; addresses digital safety risks (Chapter 8).
National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)Constitutional body (Article 338); investigates SC rights violations; promotes social justice in family, education, employment; reviews reservation policies.67,000+ cases (2022); 33.3% SCs in multidimensional poverty; supports SC/ST Act; enhances family equity for outcastes.
National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)Constitutional body (Article 338A); safeguards tribal rights; reviews land (FRA 2006), education, health policies for marginalized tribal families.50.6% tribals in multidimensional poverty; 2.5 lakh land claims settled (2024); addresses displacement, family welfare.
National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)Constitutional body (Article 338B); identifies OBCs; promotes family welfare, education, employment; advises on reservations.52% OBC population; 27.2% in multidimensional poverty; supports Mandal recommendations; boosts social mobility (M.N. Srinivas’ Sanskritization).
Statutory Bodies
National Commission for Minorities (NCM)Statutory body (NCM Act, 1992); protects minority rights (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, etc.); reviews family, education policies; counters communalism.20% minorities; Sachar Committee (2006) gaps persist; 59 riots (2024); promotes interfaith family harmony (Chapter 7).
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)Statutory body (Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993); investigates rights violations for women, children, elderly, SC/ST; recommends family welfare reforms.1.2 lakh complaints (2023); addresses trafficking, domestic violence; supports vulnerable families (Chapter 7).
National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK)Statutory body (NCSK Act, 1993); safeguards manual scavengers; promotes rehabilitation, education, family welfare for outcastes.94% scavengers SC/ST; 1,000+ complaints (2023); supports eradication; improves family dignity (Andre Béteille’s equality framework).
National Commission for Denotified, Nomadic & Semi-Nomadic Tribes (NCDNT)Statutory body (2005); protects denotified tribes; reviews welfare policies for nomadic families’ education, health.Covers 1,200+ communities; addresses criminal tribes stigma; underfunded, limiting family integration.
National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)Statutory body (Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987); provides free legal aid to poor, women, children, elderly, SC/ST; supports family law disputes.2 crore+ cases (2023); empowers vulnerable in marriage, inheritance disputes; improves access to justice.
Advisory Bodies & Committees
National Council for Senior Citizens (NCSC)Advisory body (2010); promotes elderly welfare; reviews pensions, health, family support; addresses ageism, abuse.Supports NSAP; 150M+ elderly (10.5% population); 6% live alone (Kerala); limited reach in rural areas.
Standing Committee on Social Justice and EmpowermentParliamentary committee; reviews policies for SC/ST/OBC/women/children; oversees schemes like Mission Shakti, MGNREGA.Annual reports shape family welfare budgets; 2024: Reviewed Sambal/Samarthya; influences social justice policies.
Justice Verma Committee (2013)Post-Nirbhaya; recommended stricter rape laws, POSH guidelines; focused on women’s safety in family/society.Led to Criminal Law Amendment 2013; 4.45 lakh crimes against women (2022); impacts PWDVA, POSH enforcement.
Sachar Committee (2006)Reviewed Muslim socio-economic status; recommended scholarships, employment for minority families.Highlighted 59% literacy gap; supports minority schemes; 26% Muslims in segregated areas (Chapter 7).
Mandal Commission (1979)Recommended 27% OBC reservation; addressed backward classes’ family welfare, education, employment.Implemented 1990; 27.2% OBCs in multidimensional poverty; boosts family mobility (Chapter 7).
National Population Policy (NPP) Implementation CommitteeOversees NPP 2000; coordinates family planning, maternal/child health; integrates with NHM, PMMVY.TFR: 2.0 (NFHS-5); 56.5% contraceptive use; supports family size control, women’s health.
Government Departments & Programs
Department of Family Welfare (1952)Under Ministry of Health; promotes contraception, maternal/child health; precursor to NPP, Mission Parivar Vikas.Reduced TFR from 6 (1950s) to 2 (2020); supports PMMVY; rural awareness gaps (NFHS-5).
National Health Mission (NHM) DirectorateManages NHM (2005); oversees ASHA workers, Janani Suraksha Yojana; improves maternal/child health, family welfare.JSY: 10 crore beneficiaries (2024); MMR: 97/100,000; IMR: 27/1000; rural gaps persist.
Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD)Oversees Mission Shakti, PMMVY, BBBP, Palna, Sakhi Niwas; coordinates policies for women, children, family welfare.2.92M Mission Shakti beneficiaries; 3.4 crore PMMVY users; drives FLFP (41.7%), child protection.
