- All laws, policies, schemes, initiatives, supreme court directions, etc to facilitate migration (Unverified) -
NameKey Provisions/AspectsImpact/Status (2024-2025)
Constitutional Provisions & Policies
Article 19(1)(d): Freedom of MovementGuarantees right to move freely throughout India; basis for internal migration without restrictions; subject to reasonable limits (e.g., public order, security).Supports 139 crore internal migrants (MoSPI 2020); upheld in *Gujarat Mazdoor Sabha v. State of Gujarat (2022)* for migrant rights; aids labor mobility but challenged by state barriers.
Article 21: Right to Life & LibertyProtects migrants' dignity, including access to food, shelter, healthcare during crises; extended to family reunification, welfare during emergencies (e.g., COVID-19).Aided 40M+ migrants (2020 SC orders); 2024: 60% informal migrant workforce vulnerable; supports schemes like PMGKRA.
Laws & Regulations
Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1979Regulates recruitment, wages, conditions for inter-state migrants; mandates registration, displacement/journey allowance, equal pay, welfare facilities.Covers 10+ worker establishments; 10.8% migration employment-driven (PLFS 2020-21); 60% migrant workforce vulnerable (ILO 2024); weak enforcement in 34.9% urban migration.
Emigration Act, 1983Regulates overseas migration; requires emigration clearance for ECR countries; mandatory insurance, pre-departure training; protects against trafficking/exploitation.Covers 8.5M annual emigrants; $125B remittances (2023); reduced illegal migration but 100+ US deportations (2024) highlight gaps.
Immigration and Foreigners Act, 1946Regulates foreign entry, stay, departure; requires registration within 14 days; penalties for violations; basis for OCI/PIO cards, refugee policies.Manages 40,000+ Rohingya refugees; supports 32M diaspora; 2024: 75.9M global displacements, India hosts 200,000+ refugees.
Foreigners Act, 1946Regulates foreign entry/stay; enables deportation; used for illegal migrants; amended for OCI, visa regimes.Enabled NRC in Assam; 2024: 3.7M South Asia displacements; supports legal migration but criticized for Rohingya deportations.
Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act, 1983 (IMDT)Established tribunals for illegal migrant detection (pre-1978); required state action before deportation; replaced by Foreigners Act post-2005 SC ruling.Struck down in *Sarbananda Sonowal v. UOI (2005)*; led to NRC 2019 in Assam; impacted 1.9M exclusions, family separations.
Overseas Mobility (Facilitation and Welfare) Bill, 2024Regulates overseas migration; mandates pre-departure training, insurance; protects against exploitation; family welfare provisions for emigrants.Introduced 2024; protects 8.5M emigrants; $125B remittances; enhances family support for diaspora.
Schemes & Initiatives
Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA), 2020Post-COVID employment for returning migrants; skill mapping, livelihood in 116 districts; integrates with MGNREGA for family welfare.Aided 11 crore migrants (2020-21); 10 crore MGNREGA jobs (2024); supports family stability for 139 crore internal migrants.
National Migration Support Portal (NMS), 2022Digital platform for migrant registration, job matching, welfare; family ID, grievance redressal; links to e-Shram, PMJDY.1.5 crore registrations (2024); 34.9% urban migration rate (MoSPI); aids family portability.
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC), 2019Portable PDS for migrants; biometric access to food across states; supports family nutrition during relocation.80 crore beneficiaries (2024); aids 34.9% urban migrants; reduces hunger for migrant families.
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), 2014Financial inclusion for migrants; zero-balance accounts, overdraft; Aadhaar-linked for portable banking, remittances.50 crore+ accounts (2024); 55.6% women; enables $125B remittances for migrant families.
Ayushman Bharat - PM Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), 2018Portable health insurance (₹5 lakh/family/year); covers migrants; 50 crore beneficiaries.50 crore enrolled (2024); aids 70% migrant children lacking health; reduces out-of-pocket costs.
e-Shram Portal, 2021National database for unorganized workers/migrants; registration for welfare, skills, jobs; family-linked IDs.30 crore+ registrations (2024); supports 23.5M gig workers; enhances family portability.
National Platform for Migrant Workers (NPMW), 2024Digital hub for job placement, skill training, welfare; family support services; integrates with e-Shram.1 crore+ registrations (2024); 23.5M gig workers by 2030 (NITI Aayog); aids family resilience.
Inter-State Migrant Workers Welfare Fund, 2024Fund for migrant welfare; housing, health, family support; state/CSR contributions.Pilots in 5 states (2024); aims to cover 139 crore internal migrants; enhances family welfare.
Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra (PBSK), 2007Overseas migrant helpline; legal aid, repatriation, family support for emigrants; 24/7 assistance.Aided 50,000+ emigrants (2024); supports $125B remittances; family reunification for 8.5M emigrants.
National Policy on Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, 2015Promotes migrant skills training, entrepreneurship; family-linked vocational programs; integrates with NPMW.1 crore+ trained (2024); supports 23.5M gig workers; enhances migrant family income.
Supreme Court Directions/Cases
Supreme Court Orders on Migrant Workers (2020)Post-COVID: Free transport, rations, healthcare for migrants; portable benefits; family reunification; directed states to implement welfare.Aided 40M+ migrants; led to PMGKRA, ONORC; 60% informal workforce still vulnerable (ILO 2024).
Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984)Directed rehabilitation of bonded laborers/migrants; free legal aid, wages, family support; banned forced migration; monitored implementation.Released 3 lakh bonded laborers (1984-2024); supports Inter-State Migrant Act; 1.5 crore bonded workers remain.
People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India (2001)Right to food as Article 21 right; extended to migrant families; led to NFSA 2013, ONORC for portable rations.80 crore NFSA beneficiaries (2024); aids 34.9% urban migrants; reduces family hunger.
Sarbananda Sonowal v. Union of India (2005)Struck down IMDT Act; directed stricter illegal migrant detection; impacted family separations in Assam NRC.Enabled NRC 2019 (1.9M exclusions); 2024: 3.7M South Asia displacements; family reunification challenges persist.
Rahim Ali v. Union of India (2024)Quashed Foreigners Tribunal order declaring petitioner foreigner; required material evidence; protected against arbitrary deportation.Protected 40,000+ Rohingya refugees; 2024: 75.9M global displacements; supports family rights under Article 21.
- All laws, policies, schemes, initiatives, commitees, supreme court directions, etc regarding poverty (Unverified) -
NameKey Provisions/AspectsImpact/Status (2024-2025)
Poverty Measurement Committees
Lakdawala Expert Group (1993)Recommended state-specific poverty lines using CPI for rural/urban; calorie-based (2,400 rural, 2,100 urban calories/day); accounted for regional price variations.Used until 2011; estimated 36.3% poverty (1993-94); influenced early schemes like IRDP; outdated but foundational for multidimensional approach.
Tendulkar Expert Group (2009)Shifted to mixed reference period, uniform poverty line; included health/education spending; raised poverty line to ₹27/day rural, ₹33/day urban (2004-05).Estimated 21.9% poverty (2011-12); basis for targeted schemes like MGNREGA; criticized for underestimating urban poverty; 29.6% poverty (2009-10).
Rangarajan Committee (2014)Proposed higher poverty line (₹47/day rural, ₹47/day urban, 2011-12); included non-food expenditures; multidimensional focus on health, education.Estimated 29.5% poverty (2011-12); influenced NSAP, NRLM; not officially adopted; highlighted 454M poor (2009-10).
NITI Aayog Task Force (2015)Recommended tracking bottom 30% population, multidimensional poverty; focused on nutrition, housing, education; proposed new consumption survey.Shaped MPI (11.28% poverty, 2022-23); 24.82 crore escaped poverty (2013-23); led to HCES 2022-23; 415M escaped multidimensional poverty (2005-21).
Poverty Measurement Frameworks
Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) by NITI Aayog (2018)Measures deprivations in health (nutrition, mortality), education (schooling, attendance), living standards (water, sanitation, electricity, assets); tracks bottom 30%.11.28% multidimensional poverty (2022-23); 24.82 crore escaped (2013-23); rural decline faster (32.59% to 19.28%); informs schemes like NRLM, MGNREGA.
Major Schemes & Initiatives
Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) (1978)Provided subsidies/loans for self-employment in rural areas; targeted BPL families; focused on agriculture, small industries, education.Aided 5 crore+ families (1978-2014); merged into NRLM (2011); reduced rural poverty from 50% (1970s) to 19.28% (2023); criticized for corruption.
National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM/Aajeevika) (2011)Empowers rural poor via SHGs, skill training, credit; focuses on women, families; promotes sustainable livelihoods, financial inclusion.10 crore+ beneficiaries; 8.5 crore women in SHGs; 50% rural poverty reduction (2011-23); 2.5 crore households out of poverty.
National Urban Livelihood Mission (NULM) (2013)Promotes self-employment, skill training for urban poor; includes SHGs, shelter for homeless; family-focused welfare schemes.1 crore+ urban poor reached; 4.09% urban poverty (2023); supports 12.55% urban poverty rate; aids migrant families.
Food for Work Programme (2000)Provided food grains as wages for rural labor; precursor to MGNREGA; aimed at food security, employment during distress.Implemented in 150 districts; aided 2 crore workers; merged into MGNREGA (2005); reduced hunger during famines.
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) (2005)Guarantees 100 days wage employment/year for rural households; focuses on unskilled labor, family income; includes women, SC/ST quotas.10 crore jobs (2024); 59% women participants; 25.7% rural poverty reduction (2005-23); 50.6% tribals benefited.
National Food Security Act (NFSA) (2013)Provides subsidized food grains to 81 crore people (75% rural, 50% urban); priority households include pregnant women, children, elderly.80 crore beneficiaries; 4.86% rural poverty (2024); integrates with ONORC for migrant families.
National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) (1995)Provides pensions for elderly (₹200-500/month), widows, disabled; targets BPL families; includes Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme.4 crore beneficiaries; covers 150M elderly (10.5% population); 6% elderly live alone; 25% informal sector coverage.
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) (2014)Financial inclusion for poor; zero-balance accounts, overdraft; targets women, rural families; links to direct benefit transfers.50 crore+ accounts; 55.6% women; reduced 21.9% poverty (2011-12) with DBT; aids 415M escaped multidimensional poverty (2005-21).
Skill India Mission (Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana - PMKVY) (2015)Skills training for youth, poor; short-term courses, apprenticeships; focuses on employability, family income enhancement.1.4 crore trained (2024); 23.5M gig workers by 2030; reduces unemployment (8.1%, youth 17.8%); supports NRLM/NULM.
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) (2015)Affordable housing for poor; urban/rural components; targets EWS/LIG; integrates with NRLM for women-led construction.4.2 crore houses sanctioned (2024); 2.5 crore completed; 29.5% urban poverty reduction (2011-12); aids family stability.
Supreme Court Directions/Cases
PUCL v. Union of India (2001)Right to food under Article 21; directed food security for poor; led to NFSA 2013, midday meals; monitored implementation.80 crore NFSA beneficiaries; reduced 25.7% poverty (2011-12); supports 35.5% stunted children via nutrition.
Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984)Directed bonded labor rehabilitation; wages, family support; monitored displacement, poverty alleviation.3 lakh+ bonded laborers freed (1984-2024); supports MGNREGA; 1.5 crore bonded workers remain.
Francis Coralie Mullin v. Administrator, Union Territory of Delhi (1981)Expanded Article 21 to include nutrition, shelter for poor; basis for right to dignified life, family welfare.Influenced NSAP, PMAY; 11.28% multidimensional poverty (2022-23); 415M escaped (2005-21).
- All laws, policies, schemes, initiatives, commitees, supreme court directions, etc regarding unbanization (Unverified) -
NameKey Provisions/AspectsImpact/Status (2024-2025)
Constitutional Provisions & Policies
74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992Empowers Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for planning; mandates 18 functions (e.g., land use, roads, water); establishes ward committees, District Planning Committees; promotes decentralized urban governance.Applied to 7,933 urban areas; 65% lack master plans (NITI Aayog 2021); 96% ULBs have ward committees (2024); shapes AMRUT, SCM; only 13/29 states have community participation laws.
Article 243W: Urban Planning PowersDirects states to empower ULBs for urban planning; includes slum improvement, housing, sanitation; basis for integrated development.Supports PMAY-U, SBM-U; 10M housing shortage (2022); 36% urbanization (2023); directs 70% urban sanitation coverage.
Article 243ZD: District Planning CommitteesMandates DPCs for regional planning; coordinates urban-rural development; includes 2/3rd elected representatives.Established in 25 states; integrates SCM, AMRUT; 2024: 75% projects complete in 100 Smart Cities; mitigates urban-rural divide.
Laws & Regulations
Town and Country Planning Acts (State-Specific, e.g., TCP Act 1975)State laws for urban planning; regulates land use, zoning, master plans; empowers development authorities; includes environmental clearances.Applies to 28 states; Delhi Master Plan 2041 delayed (2024); HP TCP Act 1977 strengthened by SC 2024 ruling on NGT interference; 65% urban areas without plans.
Model Building Bye-Laws (2016)Standardizes urban building regulations; promotes high-rise, green buildings; includes slum redevelopment, affordable housing norms.Adopted by 20 states; supports PMAY-U; 4.2 crore houses sanctioned (2024); reduces 10M housing shortage.
Metro Railways Act, 2002Regulates metro development; directs fare fixation committees, land acquisition; promotes urban mobility.Supports 20+ metro cities; 1,000 km operational (2024); Bangalore Metro: 75% projects complete; 34.9% urban migration aided.
Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, RERA (2016)Regulates real estate; protects homebuyers, promotes transparent urban housing; mandates project registration, timelines.1.2 lakh projects registered; 70% compliance (2024); supports PMAY; reduces urban housing fraud for 12.55% poor.
Environmental Protection Act, 1986Directs urban environmental planning; requires clearances for projects; basis for pollution control, green spaces.Supports SBM-U, CSCAF; Delhi air pollution cases (2024); 70% urban sanitation; 132 cities assessed for climate resilience.
Major Schemes & Initiatives
Smart Cities Mission (SCM) (2015)Develops 100 smart cities; area-based (retrofitting, redevelopment, greenfield) and pan-city solutions; focuses on e-governance, mobility, waste, water; integrates AI, IoT.100 cities; 7,000+ projects (₹1.7 lakh crore); 75% completed (2024); Pune SCM: Wi-Fi, lighting improved; 36% urbanization; 16 cities >50% climate score (CSCAF).
Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U) (2014)Aims ODF cities; builds household/community toilets, waste management; convergence with AMRUT; promotes behavioral change.4,400 cities ODF+; 6.3 crore toilets; 70% sanitation coverage (2024); reduced diseases; 72% municipal waste collected.
Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 2.0 (2015; II: 2021)Universal water/sewerage, green spaces in 500 cities; ₹77,640 crore for 14,993 projects; integrates with SCM, PMAY for sustainable urban living.1.89 crore tap connections, 1.49 crore sewer connections; tap coverage 70% (2024); 96,970 crore completed; aids 36% urbanization.
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) (2015)Affordable housing for urban poor; subsidies for EWS/LIG, slum redevelopment; 1 crore houses under PMAY-U 2.0 (2024-29).4.2 crore sanctioned, 2.5 crore completed (2024); 29.5% urban poverty reduction; 10M shortage; 65M slum dwellers benefited.
HRIDAY (Heritage City Development) (2015)Revitalizes 12 heritage cities; urban planning for cultural sites, tourism, infrastructure; slum-free heritage zones.12 cities (e.g., Varanasi); 75% projects complete (2024); ₹1,000 crore allocated; boosts cultural urban tourism.
Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (2020)Free food grains to urban poor; 5kg/person, 2kg grains/family/month; supports migrant/slum families.80 crore beneficiaries (2024); aids 12.55% urban poverty; extended to 2028; reduces urban hunger.
PM SVANidhi (2020)Micro-credit for urban street vendors; loans up to ₹50,000; targets migrant vendors for family livelihoods.80 lakh loans sanctioned (2024); 12 lakh women vendors; supports 1 crore urban poor; enhances family income.
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM) (2013)Self-employment, skill training for urban poor; SHGs, shelter for homeless; family-focused poverty alleviation.1 crore urban poor reached; 4.09% urban poverty (2023); supports 12.55% rate; aids migrant families.
Climate Smart Cities Assessment Framework (CSCAF) (2019)Assesses urban climate resilience; 100 parameters (energy, water, mobility, waste); guides SCM cities; promotes sustainable planning.132 cities assessed (2024); 16 >50% score (e.g., Surat); integrates with AMRUT; 10% emissions reduction in top cities.
New Cities Scheme / Satellite Cities Initiative (2024)Develops 10-20 greenfield cities; sustainable growth, housing, infrastructure; mitigates metro overcrowding.Proposed 2024; pilots in 5 states; 1M jobs, 5M houses targeted; aligns with SCM, AMRUT; reduces slum growth.
Pune Smart City MissionArea-based development (Aundh-Baner-Balewadi); smart infrastructure (lighting, Wi-Fi, mobility); community participation.75% projects complete (2024); improved e-services, safety; model for SCM; transformed 3M residents' urban living.
National Urban Digital Mission (NUDM) (2024)Digital infrastructure for cities; broadband, data centers, cyber security; supports e-governance, smart solutions.Launched 2024; 100 cities targeted; integrates with SCM; enhances urban data for planning.
Urban 97 Initiative (2024)Promotes child-friendly urban planning; 97 indicators for child-inclusive cities; aligns with SCM, AMRUT.Piloted in 10 cities (2024); supports 35.5% stunted children; improves urban child welfare.
Pradhan Mantri eBus Sewa Scheme (2023)Electric buses for urban transport; 10,000 e-buses; supports sustainable mobility in 169 cities.₹7,026 crore; 10,000 e-buses operational (2024); reduces emissions, aids urban congestion.
Supreme Court Directions/Cases
Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)Recognized right to livelihood under Article 21; protected pavement dwellers from eviction without alternatives; directed slum rehabilitation.Basis for PMAY-U, SRA; 65M slum dwellers (2011); 2024: 41% Mumbai slums upgraded; supports urban poor housing.
M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Delhi Sealing Drive, 2006)Directed balanced urban planning; curbed illegal constructions; mandated slum rehabilitation, infrastructure upgrades.Led to SBM-U, PMAY; 2024: 10M urban housing shortage; influenced SCM, AMRUT for regulated urbanization.
Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation v. Nawab Khan Gulab Khan (1997)Upheld slum dwellers' rights to basic services; directed in-situ rehabilitation; basis for IHSDP, PMAY.Aided 1.89 crore tap connections (AMRUT 2024); 70% urban sanitation; enhances slum family living standards.
Supreme Court on Delhi Master Plan (2024)Directed urgent notification of MPD 2041; criticized "utter mess" in urban planning; ordered compliance with 74th Amendment.Directed in October 2023; MPD 2041 notified June 2024; addresses 33M Delhi population; improves urban governance.
Supreme Court on NGT Interference in Urban Planning (2024)Directed NGT to limit interference in town planning; upheld state TCP Act powers; directed balanced environmental-urban development.Ruling in HP TCP Act case (2024); ensures SCM/AMRUT progress without excessive delays; 75% Smart City projects complete.
- India's all laws, acts, policies regarding governance (Unverified) -
Law/Policy/Initiative Type Year Purpose/Description Special Notes
Transparency and Accountability
Right to Information (RTI) Act Act 2005 (amended 2019) - Objective: Promote transparency and accountability in governance by empowering citizens to access information from public authorities.
- Provisions: Allows filing of RTI applications; mandates disclosure within 30 days; exemptions for sensitive information; penalties for non-compliance.
- Application: Used to monitor schemes like MGNREGA, expose corruption in public procurement. 		Over 6 million RTI applications filed annually (2024); Central Information Commission (CIC) oversees appeals; 20th anniversary in 2025 highlighted its role in citizen empowerment; criticized for delays and threats to activists.
Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act Act 2013 (amended 2016) - Objective: Establish anti-corruption ombudsman to investigate complaints against public officials.
- Provisions: Lokpal for central level, Lokayuktas for states; jurisdiction over PM, ministers, MPs; asset declaration requirements.
- Application: Probes high-profile corruption cases in bureaucracy and politics. 		Lokpal appointed in 2019; 1,000+ complaints received (2024); advisory recommendations; challenges include lack of suo motu powers and enforcement; aligns with UN Convention Against Corruption.
Prevention of Corruption Act Act 1988 (amended 2018) - Objective: Combat corruption among public servants.
- Provisions: Criminalizes bribery, undue advantage; protects bribe-givers in certain cases; faster trials via special courts.
- Application: Targets graft in government contracts, tenders. 		5,000+ cases registered annually (2024); CBI and state ACBs as nodal agencies; 2018 amendments shifted burden of proof; linked to CVC oversight.
Whistle Blowers Protection Act Act 2014 - Objective: Protect whistleblowers reporting corruption or willful misuse of power by public servants.
- Provisions: Allows disclosure to Central Vigilance Commission or any other competent authority; safeguards identity and prevents victimization.
- Application: Encourages reporting of corruption in public sector. 		Rules notified in 2015; limited implementation due to exemptions for sensitive information; 50+ cases filed (2024); aligns with RTI for transparency.
E-Governance and Digital Initiatives
Information Technology (IT) Act Act 2000 (amended 2008) - Objective: Provide legal framework for electronic governance, cybercrimes, and digital transactions.
- Provisions: Recognizes digital signatures, electronic records; penalizes hacking, identity theft (Sections 66, 69A for blocking).
- Application: Enables e-filing, digital services in governance. 		Framework for NeGP; 1 million+ cyber complaints (2024); Section 66A struck down (2015); supports Digital India; Cyber Appellate Tribunal for disputes.
Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act Act 2023 - Objective: Protect personal data privacy in digital ecosystems.
- Provisions: Consent-based data processing; Data Protection Board; rights to access/correct data; exemptions for state security.
- Application: Regulates data use in e-governance platforms like Aadhaar. 		Rules notified 2024; impacts 2M+ data breaches annually; aligns with global standards (GDPR); criticized for broad government exemptions.
National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) Policy/Initiative 2006 (expanded as Digital India 2015) - Objective: Transform governance through ICT for efficient service delivery.
- Provisions: 31 Mission Mode Projects (MMPs); core infrastructure like SWAN, CSCs; G2C, G2B services.
- Application: e-Seva, passport online, e-Courts. 		Integrated into Digital India; 100,000+ CSCs operational (2025); enhanced post-COVID for remote services; supports Aadhaar-enabled payments.
Digital India Programme Initiative 2015 - Objective: Leverage ICT for inclusive growth and e-governance.
- Provisions: Pillars: digital infrastructure, services, literacy; BharatNet for broadband, MyGov for participation.
- Application: UMANG app, DigiLocker for documents. 		₹1 lakh Cr invested (2025); 1.3B Aadhaar linkages; promotes paperless governance; 500M+ internet users by 2025.
e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0) Policy/Initiative 2015 - Objective: Enhance e-governance using cloud, mobile, and geospatial tech for integrated services.
- Provisions: 44 MMPs; focuses on integration, emerging tech; GPR for process reengineering.
- Application: e-Hospital, e-Education, e-Crime. 		Under Digital India; 44 MMPs implemented; promotes agile models; 2025 focus on AI integration.
Data Governance and Monitoring
Data Governance Quality Index (DGQI) Initiative 2020 (ongoing assessments) - Objective: Assess data maturity in ministries for evidence-based decision-making.
- Provisions: Self-assessment toolkit under 6 themes (data generation, quality, tech use, analysis, security, HR); scores 0-5.
- Application: Evaluates CS/CSS schemes; fosters peer learning. 		DMEO, NITI Aayog led; MoPSW topped Q3 FY23 with 4.7 score; 66 ministries assessed (2023); aids SDG monitoring; 2025 updates integrate AI metrics.
Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) Act Act 1971 - Objective: Audit public accounts for accountability.
- Provisions: CAG audits Union/State finances, PSUs; reports to Parliament; performance audits.
- Application: Scrutinizes schemes like 2G spectrum, Rafale deal. 		Constitutional body (Art. 148); 50,000+ audits annually (2024); exposes ₹2 lakh Cr irregularities (2023); 2025 focus on green audits.
Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Act Act 2003 - Objective: Supervise vigilance in central government.
- Provisions: Advisory role on corruption; oversees CBI inquiries; annual reports.
- Application: Vigilance awareness week, e-procurement monitoring. 		Statutory body; 10,000+ referrals to CBI (2024); lacks enforcement powers; integrates with VIGEYE app for whistleblowing.
India Data Accessibility and Use Policy (Draft) Policy 2022 (draft) - Objective: Enable sharing of non-personal government data for innovation and research.
- Provisions: India Datasets Programme; anonymized data access; promotes AI, startups.
- Application: Enhances public sector data use for policy-making. 		Released Feb 2022; focuses on non-personal data; criticized for privacy risks; aligns with DEPA.
Citizen-Centric and Administrative Reforms
Citizen's Charter Initiative Initiative 1997 (Sevottam model 2007) - Objective: Improve service delivery standards and accountability.
- Provisions: Specifies timelines, grievance redressal; public feedback loops.
- Application: Covers ministries, PSUs for services like passport issuance. 		Adopted by 1,000+ departments; CPGRAMS portal for complaints; 2025 targets 90% resolution within 30 days; links to Sevottam for quality certification.
Mission Karmayogi Initiative 2020 - Objective: Capacity building for civil servants for effective governance.
- Provisions: iGOT platform for training; behavioral competencies; lateral entry.
- Application: Targets 2M+ employees; integrates ethics modules. 		₹4,131 Cr budget; 10M+ training hours (2024); aligns with NITI Aayog's cooperative federalism; 2025 expansion to state ASOs.
Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) Initiative 2018 - Objective: Transform 112 underdeveloped districts via competitive governance.
- Provisions: Real-time monitoring of KPIs in health, education; NITI Aayog oversight.
- Application: Focus on SDGs; block-level extension in 2025. 		Improved rankings in 80% districts (2024); ₹1 lakh Cr invested; champions like Gir Somnath model for replication.
Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC) Commission/Reports 2005-2009 - Objective: Revamp public administration for efficiency, transparency, and citizen-centricity.
- Provisions: 15 reports on RTI, ethics, local governance, e-governance, etc.; 1,500+ recommendations.
- Application: Guides reforms in personnel, financial management, disaster management. 		118 recommendations accepted; influences RTI, Lokpal; 2025 review for implementation gaps; key for UPSC governance questions.
Local Governance
73rd Constitutional Amendment Act Amendment 1992 - Objective: Constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions for rural local self-governance.
- Provisions: Three-tier system (village, block, district); 33% women reservation; Gram Sabha; 11th Schedule functions.
- Application: Empowers PRIs for development planning, social justice. 		3M+ panchayats; ₹2.5 lakh Cr devolved (2024); PESA for tribal areas; 2025 focus on climate-resilient villages.
74th Constitutional Amendment Act Amendment 1992 - Objective: Constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies for urban self-governance.
- Provisions: Three types (Nagar Panchayat, Municipality, Corporation); 12th Schedule functions; ward committees.
- Application: Urban planning, public health, infrastructure. 		4,000+ ULBs; challenges in devolution; 2025 Smart Cities integration; aligns with AMRUT, Swachh Bharat.
Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA) Act 1996 - Objective: Extend Panchayati Raj to tribal areas with safeguards for tribal rights.
- Provisions: Gram Sabha powers over land, resources; consultation for development projects.
- Application: Protects tribal autonomy in 5th Schedule areas. 		Applies to 10 states; limited implementation; 2025 push for FRA integration; UPSC relevance: Tribal governance.
Policy Frameworks
National Policy for Strengthening Panchayats Policy 2021 - Objective: Empower local self-governance for inclusive development.
- Provisions: Devolution of 29 subjects; e-Gram Swaraj portal; Gram Sabha participation.
- Application: Funds for Viksit Panchayats; disaster-resilient villages. 		3M+ panchayats; ₹2.5 lakh Cr devolved (2024); aligns with 73rd Amendment; 2025 focus on climate adaptation.
PRAGATI (Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation) Initiative 2015 - Objective: Resolve inter-ministerial issues for project execution.
- Provisions: PM-chaired video-conferencing; real-time dashboards.
- Application: Infra, welfare projects; grievance redressal. 		300+ meetings (2024); ₹5 lakh Cr projects cleared; digital tool for federal coordination; expanded to states in 2025.
Miscellaneous
Central Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) Platform/Initiative 2007 (revamped 2019) - Objective: Centralized grievance redressal for citizen complaints.
- Provisions: Online portal; AI categorization; timelines for resolution.
- Application: Covers 50+ ministries; tracks service delivery. 		2M+ grievances annually (2024); 85% resolution rate; integrates with UMANG; 2025 multilingual upgrades.
Social Audit under MGNREGA Provision/Initiative 2005 - Objective: Ensure transparency in scheme implementation via community audits.
- Provisions: Mandatory audits by independent bodies; public hearings.
- Application: Funds utilization in rural works. 		1 lakh+ audits (2024); recovered ₹500 Cr misappropriations; model for other schemes; challenges in rural awareness.
Right to Public Services (RTS) Acts State Acts 2010 onwards - Objective: Guarantee time-bound delivery of public services.
- Provisions: Specifies timelines; penalties for delays; grievance redressal.
- Application: Services like certificates, licenses in states. 		Implemented in 30+ states; 1,000+ services covered; 2024: 80% compliance; enhances citizen charters.
National Data Governance Framework Policy (Draft) Policy 2022 (draft) - Objective: Standardize governance of public sector non-personal data.
- Provisions: India Datasets Platform; anonymized data sharing; promotes innovation.
- Application: AI, research; aligns with DEPA. 		Released 2022; focuses on non-personal data; 2025 implementation expected; UPSC: Data privacy, governance.

Body/Commission/Authority Type Year Purpose/Description Special Notes
Constitutional Bodies
Election Commission of India (ECI) Constitutional Body 1950 (Article 324) - Objective: Superintend, direct, and control elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and President's/Vice-President's offices.
- Provisions: Model Code of Conduct; electoral rolls; recognition of political parties; advisories on EVMs/VVPAT.
- Application: Ensures free and fair elections; handles disputes on symbols, disqualifications. 		Multi-member body (Chief Election Commissioner + 2 Commissioners); independent; UPSC relevance: Electoral reforms, Article 324; 2024 Lok Sabha elections highlighted digital voter outreach.
Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Constitutional Body 1926 (constitutionalized 1950, Article 315) - Objective: Recruit for All India Services and Central Civil Services via exams and interviews.
- Provisions: Advisory role in promotions, disciplinary matters; annual reports to President.
- Application: Conducts CSE, CDS, IES exams; ensures merit-based selection. 		Chairman + 9 members; 6-year term or age 65; UPSC relevance: Core for civil services questions; 2025 CSE notifications emphasize lateral entry integration.
State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs) Constitutional Body 1950 (Article 315) - Objective: Recruit for state civil services, similar to UPSC at state level.
- Provisions: Joint recruitments with UPSC; advisory on promotions/discipline.
- Application: State PSC exams for administrative posts. 		One per state; UPSC relevance: Federalism and recruitment; 2024 saw 20+ states notify exams.
Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) Constitutional Body 1947 (Article 148) - Objective: Audit accounts of Union/State governments, PSUs for financial accountability.
- Provisions: Performance audits; reports to Parliament/President.
- Application: Audits schemes like MGNREGA, exposes irregularities (e.g., 2G spectrum). 		Guardian of public purse; 2024 reports exposed ₹2 lakh Cr lapses; UPSC relevance: Article 149-151, accountability.
Finance Commission Constitutional Body 1951 (Article 280) - Objective: Recommend distribution of tax revenues between Union and States; fiscal federalism.
- Provisions: Every 5 years; grants-in-aid, local bodies finance.
- Application: Devolves tax shares; disaster management funds. 		15th FC (2021-26) devolved 41% share; UPSC relevance: Fiscal federalism, GST compensation.
National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) Constitutional Body 2004 (Article 338) - Objective: Safeguard SC rights, monitor constitutional safeguards.
- Provisions: Inquire into complaints; advise on planning; reports to President.
- Application: Atrocities Act enforcement; reservation monitoring. 		Post-89th Amendment separated from SC/ST; 2024 handled 10,000+ complaints; UPSC relevance: Social justice.
National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) Constitutional Body 2004 (Article 338A) - Objective: Protect ST interests, monitor safeguards.
- Provisions: Socio-economic development; FRA implementation.
- Application: Tribal rights, land alienation cases. 		Post-89th Amendment; 2024 focus on PESA; UPSC relevance: Tribal autonomy.
National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) Constitutional Body 2018 (Article 338B) - Objective: Examine OBC safeguards, complaints.
- Provisions: Recommend inclusion/exclusion in list; reports to President.
- Application: Creamy layer criteria; reservation issues. 		102nd Amendment; UPSC relevance: 2022 Mains question; 2024 sub-categorization push.
Attorney General of India Constitutional Body 1950 (Article 76) - Objective: Chief legal advisor to GoI; represent in courts.
- Provisions: Right to audience in courts; no executive powers.
- Application: Advises on bills, treaties; appears in SC/ST cases. 		Appointed by President; UPSC relevance: Union executive; 2024 opinions on electoral bonds.
Statutory Bodies
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) Statutory Body 1993 (Protection of Human Rights Act) - Objective: Protect/promote human rights; inquire into violations.
- Provisions: Civil court powers; visit jails; recommend compensation.
- Application: Custodial deaths, trafficking cases. 		Chairperson (retd. CJI) + members; 2024: 50,000+ cases; UPSC relevance: Human rights PYQs.
State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs) Statutory Body 1993 (Protection of Human Rights Act) - Objective: State-level human rights protection.
- Provisions: Similar to NHRC; appeals to NHRC.
- Application: Local violations, police excesses. 		26 SHRCs functional (2024); UPSC relevance: Federal human rights framework.
Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Statutory Body 1964 (statutory 2003, CVC Act) - Objective: Vigilance over central govt.; anti-corruption.
- Provisions: Supervise CBI; advisory on corruption; annual reports.
- Application: E-procurement monitoring; vigilance week. 		Central Vigilance Officer; 10,000+ referrals (2024); UPSC relevance: Good governance.
Lokpal Statutory Body 2013 (Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act) - Objective: Anti-corruption ombudsman for public officials.
- Provisions: Investigate PM, ministers, MPs; asset declarations.
- Application: High-profile graft probes. 		First Lokpal 2019; 1,000+ complaints (2024); UPSC relevance: Ombudsman institution.
Lokayuktas Statutory Body 1971 onwards (state-specific) - Objective: State-level anti-corruption for officials.
- Provisions: Investigate state ministers, MLAs; vary by state.
- Application: Local corruption cases. 		Mandatory post-2013 Act; 20+ states; UPSC relevance: Decentralized vigilance.
Central Information Commission (CIC) Statutory Body 2005 (RTI Act) - Objective: Appellate authority under RTI for transparency.
- Provisions: Hear appeals/second appeals; impose penalties.
- Application: 6M+ RTI cases annually. 		Chief Information Commissioner + ICs; UPSC relevance: Right to info, transparency.
State Information Commissions (SICs) Statutory Body 2005 (RTI Act) - Objective: State-level RTI appeals.
- Provisions: Similar to CIC; appeals to HC.
- Application: Local transparency issues. 		28 SICs; UPSC relevance: Federal transparency mechanisms.
National Commission for Women (NCW) Statutory Body 1990 (NCW Act) - Objective: Protect women's rights; review laws.
- Provisions: Investigate complaints; recommend policy.
- Application: Gender violence, discrimination. 		Chairperson + 5 members; 2024: 20,000+ cases; UPSC relevance: Gender justice.
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) Statutory Body 2005 (CPCR Act) - Objective: Safeguard child rights.
- Provisions: Monitor POCSO, RTE; awareness programs.
- Application: Child labor, education rights. 		Chairperson + 6 members; UPSC relevance: Child rights conventions.
National Commission for Minorities (NCM) Statutory Body 1992 (NCM Act) - Objective: Protect minority rights (Muslims, Christians, etc.).
- Provisions: Socio-economic surveys; recommend safeguards.
- Application: Communal harmony, reservation. 		6 recognized minorities; UPSC relevance: Article 29-30; 2024 hate crime probes.
National Green Tribunal (NGT) Statutory Body 2010 (NGT Act) - Objective: Handle environmental disputes speedily.
- Provisions: Judicial + expert members; enforce EP Act.
- Application: Pollution, forest cases (e.g., Yamuna cleanup). 		Quasi-judicial; UPSC relevance: Environmental governance; 2025 principal bench expansion.
National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) Statutory Body 1988 (Consumer Protection Act, amended 2019) - Objective: Adjudicate consumer disputes >₹2 Cr.
- Provisions: Appellate over state commissions; e-filing.
- Application: Unfair trade, product liability. 		Appellate over state commissions; e-filing; UPSC relevance: Consumer rights; 2024: 50,000+ cases.
State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions (SCDRCs) Statutory Body 1988 (Consumer Protection Act) - Objective: State-level consumer forums for disputes ₹20L-₹2 Cr.
- Provisions: District forums below; appeals to NCDRC.
- Application: Product liability, unfair trade. 		Three-tier system; UPSC relevance: Good governance via consumer protection.
District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forums Statutory Body 1988 (Consumer Protection Act) - Objective: Local consumer grievance redressal <₹20L.
- Provisions: Speedy disposal; no court fees.
- Application: Everyday complaints (e.g., defective goods). 		Base of consumer courts; UPSC relevance: Decentralized justice.
Competition Commission of India (CCI) Statutory Body 2003 (Competition Act) - Objective: Promote competition, prevent anti-competitive practices.
- Provisions: Merger approvals; abuse of dominance penalties.
- Application: Cartels, big tech probes. 		Quasi-judicial; UPSC relevance: Economic governance; 2024 fines ₹1,000 Cr+.
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Statutory Body 1992 (SEBI Act) - Objective: Regulate securities market, protect investors.
- Provisions: Insider trading curbs; mutual funds oversight.
- Application: IPOs, stock exchanges. 		UPSC relevance: Financial sector reforms; 2025 ESG disclosure mandates.
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Statutory Body 1935 (RBI Act) - Objective: Monetary authority; issue currency, banker to govt.
- Provisions: Repo rate; inflation targeting.
- Application: Digital rupee, financial inclusion. 		UPSC relevance: Economic policy; 2024 CBDC pilots.
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) Statutory Body 1998 (ERC Act) - Objective: Regulate interstate electricity transmission/tariffs.
- Provisions: Tariff determination; dispute resolution.
- Application: Power sector reforms. 		UPSC relevance: Energy governance.
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Statutory Body 1997 (TRAI Act) - Objective: Regulate telecom services, protect consumers.
- Provisions: Tariff regulation; QoS standards.
- Application: Spectrum auctions, OTT regulation. 		UPSC relevance: Digital India; 2024 data privacy guidelines.

- Provisions: Aspirational Districts; SDG India Index; Atal Innovation.
- Application: SDG monitoring, state rankings. 		Replaced Planning Commission; UPSC relevance: Governance reforms; 2025 Viksit Bharat focus.
Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Non-Statutory Body 1963 - Objective: Investigate corruption, economic offences.
- Provisions: Special Police Establishment; under DoPT.
- Application: High-profile scams (e.g., coal gate). 		'CBI vs CBI' autonomy issues; UPSC relevance: Anti-corruption machinery.
Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) Executive Department 1964 - Objective: Administrative reforms, grievance redressal.
- Provisions: CPGRAMS; Sevottam; Citizen's Charters.
- Application: e-Governance, best practices. 		Under MoPP; UPSC relevance: Good governance initiatives; 2025 AI in grievances.
Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC) Commission 2005-2009 - Objective: Recommend reforms for effective administration.

- Application: Influenced Lokpal, e-Gov. 		118/556 recommendations implemented; UPSC relevance: Governance syllabus core.
National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) Statutory Body 2005 (DM Act) - Objective: Coordinate disaster management.

- Application: COVID-19 response, flood mitigation. 		PM-chaired; UPSC relevance: Disaster governance; 2024 Wayanad landslides.
University Grants Commission (UGC) Statutory Body 1956 (UGC Act) - Objective: Coordinate higher education standards.
- Provisions: Funding, accreditation; NEP implementation.

Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) Statutory Body 1974 (Water Act) - Objective: Prevent/control pollution.

Quasi-Judicial Bodies
Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Quasi-Judicial Body 1941 - Objective: Appeals on income tax disputes.
- Provisions: Final fact-finding; benches across India.

Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) Quasi-Judicial Body 1982 - Objective: Appeals on indirect taxes, customs.

Law/Policy/Initiative Type Year Purpose/Description Special Notes
NGOs & Civil Societies
Societies Registration Act Act 1860 (amended in various states) - Objective: Provide for registration of literary, scientific, charitable societies.
- Provisions: Requires minimum 7 members; filing of memorandum, rules; annual reporting to Registrar; suits in name of governing body.
- Application: Registration of societies for education, health, social welfare. 		Central Act; state-specific amendments (e.g., Maharashtra Societies Registration Act, 1860); fee ₹50-250; dissolution requires 3/5th vote.
Indian Trusts Act Act 1882 - Objective: Define and amend law relating to private trusts and trustees.
- Provisions: Creation of trusts via words/acts; trustee obligations (protect property, no personal profit); beneficiary rights; lawful purposes only.
- Application: Private trusts for family, religious/charitable purposes (public trusts under state laws). 		Applies to whole India except J&K, Andaman/Nicobar; excludes waqf, family customs, public endowments; amended 2015 for investments.
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Act 2010 (amended 2020, 2024-2025) - Objective: Regulate acceptance/utilization of foreign contributions to prevent misuse.
- Provisions: Registration/prior permission for NGOs; no sub-granting; 20% admin cap (carry forward allowed 2025); TDS refunds to FCRA account; publication undertakings.
- Application: Foreign funding for NGOs, VOs; prohibits news/current affairs entities. 		2025 amendments: Carry forward unspent admin (up to 25%); auditor certification; "Not a Newspaper" certificate; over 20,000 licenses revoked since 2011.
Companies Act (Section 8) Act 2013 - Objective: Register non-profit companies for charitable purposes.
- Provisions: License from ROC; no dividend; assets for promotion of objectives; min 2 members.
- Application: Section 8 companies for education, health, environment. 		Replaces Section 25; tax exemptions under 12A/80G; high compliance; suits via ROC.
NGO DARPAN Portal/Initiative 2015 - Objective: Central repository for NGOs/VOs; facilitate govt-NGO interface.
- Provisions: Unique ID upon registration; mandatory for grants; upload docs (reg cert, PAN, Aadhaar of 3 members).
- Application: Access schemes, CSR funds, FCRA linkage. 		NITI Aayog/NIC; free registration; 3.3M+ NGOs listed; prerequisite for CSR-1.
Bombay Public Trusts Act Act 1950 (model for states) - Objective: Regulate public trusts for charitable/religious purposes.
- Provisions: Registration with Charity Commissioner; annual returns; audit; state variants (e.g., Maharashtra, Gujarat).
- Application: Public trusts in MH/GJ/others. 		Adopted by 8+ states; excludes private trusts; Charity Commissioner oversight.
Income Tax Act (Sections 12A, 80G) Act 1961 (amended) - Objective: Tax exemptions for NGOs/VOs.
- Provisions: 12A for income exemption; 80G for donor deductions (50-100%); anonymous donations taxed 30%.
- Application: Charitable trusts/societies/Section 8 companies. 		Requires NGO DARPAN ID; GST if taxable services; EPF/ESI for >20 employees.

Trade Unions Act Act 1926 (amended) - Objective: Register/promote lawful trade unions.

Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs) Directions Directions 2011 (updated 2025) - Objective: Regulate NBFC-MFIs for financial inclusion.
-
- Provisions: Qualifying assets 75% of portfolio; household income <₹3L; max loan ₹1.25L; no collateral; interest rates non-usurious; 2025: QA criteria revised for flexibility.
- Application: Microloans to low-income households, women. 		RBI; 2025 revisions: Risk weights 100% for consumer MFI loans; excludes RRP for consumer credit.
Master Direction on Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans Directions 2022 (updated 2025) - Objective: Uniform framework for microfinance loans by banks/NBFCs.
- Provisions: Household income <₹3L; max ₹3L; 75% RRP if criteria met; risk weights 75-100%.
- Application: All lenders; promotes inclusion. 		RBI; 2025: Reduced risk weights to 100% for consumer MFI loans; excludes RRBs/LABs.

- All acts, policies, welfare schemes, etc in India for women help (Unverified) -
Act/Policy/Scheme Year Authority Purpose/Description Key Provisions Recent Statistics/Impact (2023-2025)
Constitutional Provisions
Fundamental Rights (Articles 14, 15, 21, 23) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Ensure equality, non-discrimination, and protection of life and liberty for women.
- Scope: Article 14 (equality before law), Article 15 (non-discrimination), Article 21 (right to life/liberty), Article 23 (prohibits trafficking, forced labor).
- Application: Forms the basis for gender equality laws; enforceable via courts. 		- Article 14: Equal treatment under law.
- Article 15: Prohibits discrimination based on sex; enables affirmative action.
- Article 21: Right to dignified life, privacy (e.g., Puttaswamy case, 2017).
- Article 23: Bans human trafficking, bonded labor. 		Landmark judgments: Vishaka (1997), Sabarimala (2018), Triple Talaq (2017); 4.45 lakh cases under women-related laws (NCRB 2024).
Article 42 (Directive Principles) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Secure just and humane work conditions, maternity relief.
- Scope: Non-justiciable but guides welfare policies.
- Application: Influences labor laws, maternity benefits. 		- Provisions: Maternity relief, humane work conditions.
- Implementation: Basis for Maternity Benefit Act, workplace safety laws. 		Supports 26-week maternity leave (2025); 2 Cr women benefited via labor laws (2023-25).
73rd Constitutional Amendment (Article 243D) 1992 Constitution of India - Objective: Empower women in local governance.
- Scope: Mandates reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions.
- Application: Enhances women’s leadership in rural governance. 		- Reservation: 33% seats for women in Panchayats (some states 50%).
- Implementation: Elected women representatives (EWRs) lead local decisions. 		14 lakh women elected in Panchayats (2025); 50% reservation in 21 states; 2025 training programs for EWRs.
Legislative Acts
Women’s Reservation Act (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) 2023 Central Legislation - Objective: Ensure women’s representation in Parliament and State Assemblies.
- Scope: Reserves 33% seats for women.
- Application: Applies post-delimitation; enhances political participation. 		- Reservation: 1/3rd seats in Lok Sabha, State Assemblies.
- Implementation: Awaits census, delimitation (expected 2029). 		Passed Sep 2023; 15% women MPs in 17th Lok Sabha (2024); delimitation process initiated (2025).
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act 2006 Central Legislation - Objective: Prevent child marriages, protect girls’ rights.
- Scope: Sets minimum marriage age (21 for men, 18 for women).
- Application: Applies to all communities; voids underage marriages. 		- Provisions: Punishment up to 2 years imprisonment; Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (Sections 3-16).
- Protection: Maintenance for minor girls; voidable marriages. 		1.4 lakh child marriages prevented (2023-24); 23% girls married below 18 (NFHS-5); 2025 awareness drives intensified.
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) 2005 Central Legislation - Objective: Protect women from domestic violence (physical, emotional, economic).
- Scope: Covers women in domestic relationships.
- Application: Provides civil remedies, support services. 		- Remedies: Protection, residence, monetary, custody orders (Sections 18-23).
- Mechanisms: Protection Officers, service providers (Sections 8-12).
- Penalties: Breach punishable by 1-year imprisonment (Section 31). 		802 One-Stop Centres (2025); 4.45 lakh cases annually (NCRB 2024); Supreme Court pushes implementation (May 2025).
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act 2013 Central Legislation - Objective: Prevent and redress workplace sexual harassment.
- Scope: All workplaces, including unorganized sector.
- Application: Mandates Internal Complaints Committees (ICCs). 		- Mechanisms: ICC for 10+ employee organizations; inquiry within 90 days (Sections 4, 11).
- Remedies: Conciliation, compensation, transfer; ₹50,000 fine for non-compliance (Sections 13-26). 		60% workplaces non-compliant with ICC (2024); 30,000+ complaints resolved (2023-25); 2025 compliance audits planned.
Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 Central Legislation - Objective: Enhance maternity benefits for working women.
- Scope: Covers establishments with 10+ employees.
- Application: Ensures paid leave, workplace facilities. 		- Benefits: 26 weeks paid maternity leave; 12 weeks for adoption/surrogacy (Section 5).
- Facilities: Creche for 50+ employees; work-from-home options (Section 11A). 		2 Cr women benefited (2023-25); 70% compliance in formal sector; 2025 focus on unorganized sector.
Welfare Schemes
Mission Shakti 2021 Ministry of Women & Child Development - Objective: Umbrella scheme for women’s safety, empowerment, and protection.
- Scope: Integrates schemes like OSC, WHL, Swadhar Greh, BBBP.
- Application: Holistic approach to address violence, economic empowerment. 		- Components: Sambal (safety/protection), Samarthya (empowerment).
- Sub-Schemes: OSCs, WHL, Nari Adalat, BBBP, PMMVY.
- Implementation: State/district-level coordination; Nirbhaya Fund support. 		₹5,000 Cr allocated (2024-25); 12 lakh women assisted via Sambal; 2 Cr reached via Samarthya (2025).
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) 2015 Ministry of Women & Child Development - Objective: Address declining child sex ratio, promote girl child education.
- Scope: Nationwide campaign; focuses on awareness, education.
- Application: Targets districts with low CSR. 		- Components: Awareness campaigns, education incentives.
- Implementation: Multi-ministerial (WCD, Education, Health). 		CSR improved from 918 to 933 (2015-24); 1 Cr girls enrolled in schools; 2025 digital campaigns launched.
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana 2015 Ministry of Finance - Objective: Promote savings for girl child’s education, marriage.
- Scope: Savings scheme for girls under 10 years.
- Application: High-interest accounts in post offices/banks. 		- Benefits: 8.2% interest rate; ₹250-₹1.5 lakh annual deposit.
- Taxation: EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) status; maturity at 21 years. 		3.2 Cr accounts opened; ₹2.1 lakh Cr mobilized (2025); 2025 rural outreach expanded.
Udaan Scheme 2014 Ministry of Skill Development - Objective: Provide skill training, employment to women.
- Scope: Targets women graduates, professionals.
- Application: Focuses on corporate sector placement. 		- Training: 100-hour programs; soft skills, IT.
- Placement: Corporate tie-ups; mentorship support. 		50,000+ women trained; 60% placed in jobs (2023-25); 2025 focus on tech skills.
One Stop Centre Scheme 2015 Ministry of Women & Child Development - Objective: Provide integrated support to women facing violence.
- Scope: Single-window access to legal, medical, counseling services.
- Application: Nationwide network of centres. 		- Services: Medical aid, police assistance, legal aid, shelter.
- Operation: 24/7 helpline (181); Sakhi centres. 		802 centres operational; 10 lakh women assisted; 2025 integration with ERSS-112 enhanced.
Swadhar Greh & Short Stay Homes 2015 (Swadhar); 1966 (Short Stay) Ministry of Women & Child Development - Objective: Provide shelter, rehabilitation for women in distress.
- Scope: Targets destitute, trafficked, homeless women.
- Application: Offers temporary housing, skill training. 		- Services: Shelter, food, medical care, vocational training.
- Capacity: 30-50 women per home; 6-month stay (extendable). 		410 Swadhar Grehs; 1.2 lakh women rehabilitated (2023-25); 2025 focus on trafficking victims.
Nirbhaya Fund 2013 Ministry of Women & Child Development - Objective: Fund initiatives for women’s safety, empowerment.

Constitutional Provisions
Article 39(f) (Directive Principles) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Ensure children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner and in conditions of freedom and dignity.
- Scope: Protects children from exploitation and moral/national abandonment.
- Application: Guides child welfare policies; non-justiciable but foundational for laws like JJ Act. 		- Provisions: State to direct policy towards child development, protection from abuse.
- Implementation: Influences ICDS, POSHAN, and child labor bans. 		Supports 14 lakh children via child protection schemes (2025); integrated into Mission Vatsalya (2023-25).
Article 21A (Fundamental Rights) 2002 Constitution of India - Objective: Provide free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years.
- Scope: Right to education as fundamental right.
- Application: Enforceable via RTE Act; promotes universal access. 		- Provisions: Free education, no detention up to Class 8 (amended).
- Implementation: 25% reservation in private schools for disadvantaged children. 		96% enrollment in elementary education (2024); 2.5 Cr children benefited via Samagra Shiksha (2023-25).
Articles 23 & 24 (Fundamental Rights) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Prohibit trafficking, forced labor, and employment of children in hazardous jobs.
- Scope: Article 23 bans human trafficking/bonded labor; Article 24 prohibits child labor under 14 in factories/mines.
- Application: Basis for Child Labour Act; protects vulnerable children. 		- Provisions: Punishment for violations; rehabilitation for rescued children.
- Implementation: Links to JJ Act, NCLP for education/rehab. 		1.1 lakh children rescued from labor (2023-24); 50,000 rehabilitated via NCLP (2025).
Article 45 (Directive Principles) 1950 (amended) Constitution of India - Objective: Provide early childhood care and education for children below 6 years.
- Scope: Free/compulsory education up to 14; ECCE for under-6s.
- Application: Guides ICDS, NEP 2020 for foundational learning. 		- Provisions: State to minimize neglect, provide opportunities for healthy development.
- Implementation: ECCE in Anganwadis; integrated with POSHAN 2.0. 		1.4 Cr children covered under ECCE (2025); 80% Anganwadis upgraded (2024).

- Scope: Covers adoption, foster care, juvenile justice boards.
- Application: Replaces 2000 Act; focuses on rehabilitation. 		- Provisions: Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), Juvenile Justice Boards (JJBs); offenses against children (Sections 74-79).
- Implementation: Sponsorship, aftercare; aligns with UNCRC. 		2.5 lakh children in CCIs benefited (2024); 2025 amendments for digital tracking; 90% disposal rate in JJBs.
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act 2006 Central Legislation - Objective: Prevent child marriages, protect children's rights to health/education.
- Scope: Minimum age 21 (boys), 18 (girls); voids underage marriages.
- Application: Applies nationwide; empowers Child Marriage Prohibition Officers. 		- Provisions: Penalties up to 2 years imprisonment/fine (Sections 3-16); maintenance for victims.
- Implementation: Awareness via BBBP, ICDS. 		1.4 lakh marriages prevented (2023-24); 23% girls married below 18 (NFHS-5); 2025 campaigns in high-risk districts.
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act 2012 Central Legislation - Objective: Protect children from sexual abuse, exploitation, pornography.
- Scope: Covers 0-18 years; child-friendly procedures.
- Application: Special courts, fast-track trials. 		- Provisions: Criminalizes offenses (penetrative assault, harassment); mandatory reporting (Sections 19-21).
- Implementation: POCSO e-Box for online complaints; child-friendly courts. 		62,000 cases registered (2023); 1,000 fast-track courts (2025); 70% conviction rate improved (2024).
Right to Education (RTE) Act 2009 Central Legislation - Objective: Implement Article 21A for free/compulsory education (6-14 years).
- Scope: Neighborhood schools, no capitation fees.
- Application: Regulates school standards, teacher norms. 		- Provisions: 25% reservation for disadvantaged; no detention till Class 8 (amended 2019).
- Implementation: Monitored via U-DISE; aligns with NEP 2020. 		1.2 Cr children admitted under 25% quota (2023-25); 95% gross enrollment ratio (2024).

- Implementation: FSSAI standards; DBT for cooking costs. 		11.8 Cr children benefited (2024); 11.20 Cr meals/day; anemia reduced 10% (2023-25).

- Implementation: Village-level events; tracking via U-DISE. 		2 lakh children enrolled annually (2023-24); 95% retention in Assam/Gujarat (2025).

- Scope: Reduces dropout rates in low-income families.

- Implementation: Aadhaar-linked DBT; eligibility for BPL/white ration families. 		67 lakh mothers benefited; ₹8,745 Cr allocated (2025-26); dropout rate down 15% (2025).
Balika Samriddhi Yojana 1997 Ministry of Women & Child Development - Objective: Promote girl child survival, education in BPL families.
- Scope: Post-delivery financial aid, scholarships till Class 10.
- Application: Improves CSR, reduces discrimination. 		- Benefits: ₹500 post-delivery + annual scholarships (₹300-1,000); uniform allowance.
- Implementation: Post offices/banks; up to two girls per family. 		10 lakh girls benefited annually (2024); integrated with BBBP; CSR improved 5% (2023-25).

- Scope: Holistic care till 23 years; health, education, foster care.
- Application: Supplements JJ Act; guardian appointment. 		- Benefits: Health insurance (₹5 lakh), education fund; monthly stipend post-18.
- Implementation: District Collectors oversee; digital portal. 		4,000+ children supported (2025); ₹15,000 Cr corpus; 100% coverage for eligible (2024).

- Scope: Special schools for 5-14 year working children.

- Implementation: 300+ projects; aligns with Child Labour Act. 		1 lakh children mainstreamed (2023-25); 50,000 in NCLP schools (2025).

Constitutional Provisions
Article 41 (Directive Principles) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Directs state to provide public assistance in cases of old age, sickness, and disability.
- Scope: Non-justiciable; guides welfare policies for vulnerable groups including elderly.
- Application: Foundation for schemes like NSAP, IPOP; promotes right to dignified life. 		- Provisions: State to secure right to work, education, public assistance within economic capacity.
- Implementation: Influences NSAP pensions, NPHCE health care. 		Supports 2.5 Cr elderly via NSAP (2025); integrated into AVYAY for comprehensive elderly welfare.
Legislative Acts
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007 (Amended 2019) Central Legislation - Objective: Ensure maintenance, welfare, and protection for parents/senior citizens.
- Scope: Covers abandonment, abuse; mandates family duty to provide care.
- Application: Establishes tribunals for claims; promotes old age homes. 		- Provisions: Maintenance up to ₹10,000/month (no upper limit post-2019); speedy tribunals (90 days); protection from eviction (Sections 4-23).
- Amendments (2019): Expands 'children' to include step/adoptive; removes cap on maintenance; adds homecare services. 		12% awareness among elderly (India Ageing Report 2023); 30,000+ cases resolved via tribunals (2023-25); 2025 focus on digital filing.
National Policies
National Policy for Senior Citizens 2011 (New Policy in Draft 2025) Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment - Objective: Ensure financial security, health, shelter for elderly; promote active ageing.
- Scope: Holistic welfare; focuses on 60+ population projected at 17.3 Cr by 2026.
- Application: Guides schemes like AVYAY, RVY; emphasizes intergenerational bonding. 		- Provisions: Universal pension, geriatric care, age-friendly environment; National Council for monitoring.
- Updates: Draft 2025 addresses silver economy, research; aligns with Viksit Bharat@2047. 		New policy under formulation (Jun 2025); covers 10.38 Cr elderly (2011 Census); 55% awareness of pensions (2023 Report).

- Implementation: Aadhaar-linked; via banks/post offices. 		2.5 Cr beneficiaries (2025); ₹12,000 Cr disbursed (2023-25); reduced vulnerability by 10% (LASI data).
Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY) 2017 Ministry of Finance (LIC) - Objective: Assured pension for senior citizens' financial security.
- Scope: Annuity scheme for 60+; max ₹15 lakh investment.
- Application: Lump-sum purchase; monthly/quarterly payouts. 		- Benefits: 7.4% p.a. return; 10-year term; death benefit refunds purchase price.
- Implementation: Via LIC; extended to Mar 2023. 		₹2.1 lakh Cr mobilized; 3.2 Cr accounts (2025); 5 lakh claims settled.
Atal Pension Yojana (APY) 2015 Ministry of Finance (PFRDA) - Objective: Portable pension for unorganized sector, including elderly.

Varishta Pension Bima Yojana (VPBY) 2003 (Revived 2014) Ministry of Finance (LIC) - Objective: Immediate annuity for senior citizens' income security.

- Implementation: LIC-managed; open Aug 2014-Aug 2015, renewals ongoing. 		3.16 lakh annuitants; ₹6,095 Cr corpus (2023-25); 1 lakh renewals processed.
Annapurna Scheme 2000 Ministry of Rural Development - Objective: Food security for uncovered elderly BPL seniors.

- Application: Supports quotas, anti-discrimination in jobs/education. 		- Provisions: No discrimination on grounds of sex/gender; reservations for backward classes.
- Implementation: Guides state policies like Karnataka 1% horizontal reservation. 		2025: 1% horizontal quota in Karnataka; 27% OBC overlap for trans; 2024 SC sub-classification verdict aids.
Article 21 (Fundamental Rights) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Protects right to life and personal liberty, including dignity for transgender persons.
- Scope: Encompasses privacy, health, autonomy.
- Application: Basis for gender-affirming care, decriminalization. 		- Provisions: Right to live with dignity; includes bodily integrity.
- Implementation: NALSA, Navtej judgments. 		2025: Tele-MANAS for trans mental health; 31% suicide rate addressed via GAC push.
Article 23 (Fundamental Rights) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Prohibits trafficking and forced labor, protecting transgender persons from exploitation.
- Scope: Bans bonded labor; includes sex work coercion.
- Application: Supports anti-trafficking for trans community. 		- Provisions: Punishable offense; rehabilitation mandates.
- Implementation: Linked to TPPR Act offenses. 		2025: SMILE scheme rescued 500+ trans from trafficking; integrated with anti-begging rehab.
Judicial Precedents
NALSA v. Union of India Judgment 2014 Supreme Court of India - Objective: Recognizes transgender as third gender; affirms self-identification rights.
- Scope: Entitles trans to reservations, welfare; decriminalizes begging.
- Application: Foundation for TPPR Act. 		- Provisions: Self-perceived gender; 3% quota in education/jobs; medical aid.
- Implementation: Directed schemes, surveys. 		2025: Cited in Delhi Welfare Board; 66% ID certificates issued (24k applications).
Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India 2018 Supreme Court of India - Objective: Decriminalizes homosexuality (IPC 377); protects trans privacy, dignity.
- Scope: Broader LGBTQ+ rights; consensual acts.
- Application: Aids trans health, reduces stigma. 		- Provisions: Strikes down 377 for consensual same-sex; privacy under Art. 21.
- Implementation: Influences GAC, mental health schemes. 		2025: Tele-MANAS calls up 20%; reduced stigma in 10 states.

Act/Policy/Scheme Year Authority Purpose/Description Key Provisions Recent Statistics/Impact (2023-2025)
Constitutional Provisions
Fundamental Rights (Part III) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Guarantees right to life, liberty, equality, and health as part of dignity under Articles 14, 19, 21.
- Scope: Protects against state denial of healthcare; enables access to medical services.
- Application: Basis for judicial mandates on public health emergencies, free treatment. 		- Provisions: Art. 14 (equality), Art. 21 (life/dignity including health), Art. 19 (right to practice profession).
- Implementation: Enforced via PILs; e.g., Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity (1996) on emergency care. 		Invoked in 2025 SC rulings on digital health privacy; supports 100% TB coverage under NTEP.
Article 39(e) (Directive Principles) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: Directs state to ensure health of workers, prevent health hazards in occupations.
- Scope: Protects labor health; promotes safe working conditions.
- Application: Guides OSH policies, ESI for industrial workers. 		- Provisions: State to secure health in occupations; non-justiciable but policy directive.
- Implementation: Influences Factories Act, ESI Act. 		Supports 2025 labor health reforms; 50M+ workers under ESI (2025).
Article 41 (Directive Principles) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: State to secure public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, disability.
- Scope: Includes health security for vulnerable.
- Application: Basis for NSAP, PMJAY. 		- Provisions: Right to work, education, assistance within economic capacity.
- Implementation: Guides social security schemes. 		2.5 Cr elderly under NSAP (2025); integrated with PMJAY senior coverage.
Article 42 (Directive Principles) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: State to secure just/humane work conditions, maternity relief.
- Scope: Occupational health, maternal care.
- Application: Influences PMMVY, labor health. 		- Provisions: Maternity relief; humane conditions.
- Implementation: Basis for Maternity Benefit Act. 		3 Cr mothers under PMMVY (2025); 26-week leave compliance 70%.
Article 47 (Directive Principles) 1950 Constitution of India - Objective: State to improve public health as primary duty; prohibit intoxicating drinks/drugs.
- Scope: Nutrition, hygiene, public health improvement.
- Application: Guides NHM, POSHAN. 		- Provisions: Raise nutrition levels, standard of living.
- Implementation: Influences NFSA. 		Stunting reduced 7% via POSHAN (2025); 80 Cr NFSA beneficiaries.
Article 48A (Directive Principles) 1976 Constitution of India - Objective: State to protect/improve environment for healthy development.
- Scope: Pollution control, eco-health link.
- Application: Supports NACP, climate-health integration. 		- Provisions: Endeavor to protect environment.
- Implementation: Via NGT, EPA. 		2025: Integrated in NDHM for eco-health data; 10M air pollution-linked cases reduced.
