Central Electricity Authority (CEA) 1951 To advise on power sector planning and development Statutory body under Electricity Act, 2003; assists MoP on policy, technical standards, grid codes; coordinates generation/transmission; includes renewables in national plans (e.g., 500 GW non-fossil by 2030).
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) 1998 To regulate inter-state power tariffs and transmission Statutory body under Electricity Act, 2003; sets tariffs for generators, traders; approves renewable purchase obligations (RPO); promotes competition in power markets.
Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) 1997 To regulate groundwater extraction Statutory body under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (Mo Jal Shakti); indirectly supports power via NOCs for hydro/thermal plants using groundwater; monitors over-exploitation in notified areas.
Central Transmission Utility (CTU) 2003 To plan and coordinate inter-state transmission Statutory function under Electricity Act, 2003 (via PGCIL); ensures grid stability for conventional/renewable integration; handles green energy corridors.
Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) 1948 To develop multi-purpose river valley projects Statutory corporation under DVC Act, 1948; manages hydro/thermal power (6,700 MW+); flood control, irrigation; integrates renewables in eastern grid.
Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Limited (IREDA) 1987 To finance renewable energy projects Navratna CPSE under MNRE; provides loans/equity for solar, wind, hydro; Rs. 50,000 Cr+ portfolio; supports off-grid renewables and green hydrogen.
National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC) 1975 To develop hydroelectric projects Navratna CPSE under MoP; 6,971 MW hydro capacity; surveys, constructs dams; incorporates pumped storage for renewable balancing.
National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) 1975 To promote thermal power generation Maharatna CPSE under MoP; 74,000 MW+ capacity (coal/gas); expanding renewables (15 GW solar/wind target by 2032); leads joint ventures.
National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) 1981 (autonomous 2013) To advance solar energy R&D Autonomous institution under MNRE; apex body for solar tech; tests modules, develops standards; supports National Solar Mission (100 GW+ target).
National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) 1998 To promote wind energy development Autonomous institution under MNRE; wind resource assessment, turbine testing; offshore wind guidelines; 50 GW wind target by 2030.
NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited (NVVN) 2002 To facilitate power trading Subsidiary of NTPC under MoP; trades surplus power; supports renewable energy certificates (REC) market.
Power Finance Corporation (PFC) 1986 To finance power infrastructure Navratna CPSE under MoP; Rs. 10 lakh Cr+ loans; funds conventional/renewable projects; manages RDSS scheme for distribution.
Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) 1989 To establish and operate national grid Maharatna CPSE under MoP; 1,80,000 km transmission lines; integrates 200 GW+ renewables; green energy corridors (9,000 km).
Rural Electrification Corporation (REC) 1969 To finance rural electrification Maharatna CPSE under MoP; Rs. 4 lakh Cr+ loans; supports off-grid renewables, solar pumps; merged with PFC in 2022 but operates distinctly.
Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy (SSS-NIBE) 1983 (autonomous 2011) To develop bioenergy technologies Autonomous institution under MNRE; R&D in biomass, biogas; supports 10 GW bioenergy target; rural applications.
Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) 2011 To implement solar and renewable schemes Schedule-A CPSE under MNRE; develops solar parks (50 GW+); wind-solar hybrid auctions; green hydrogen mission.
- India's important acts, laws, policies regarding internal security (Unverified) -
Law/Policy/Agency Type Year Purpose/Description Special Notes
Counter-Terrorism
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) Act 1967 (amended 2019) - Objective: Prevent unlawful activities and terrorism threatening India's sovereignty.
- Provisions: Declares groups as unlawful; allows preventive detention; criminalizes terror financing, membership.
- Application: Used against LeT, JeM, CPI(Maoist), SFJ. 		40+ groups banned; 1,200 arrests (2024); criticized for vague definitions, misuse; FATF-compliant.
Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act (TADA) Act 1987 (lapsed 1995) - Objective: Combat terrorism, especially Punjab insurgency.
- Provisions: Special courts, confessions admissible, preventive detention up to 1 year.
- Application: Targeted Khalistani groups (BKI, ISYF). 		Lapsed due to human rights concerns; convicted ~2% of 76,000 detained; provisions merged into UAPA.
Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA) Act 2002 (repealed 2004) - Objective: Strengthen anti-terror measures post-2001 Parliament attack.
- Provisions: Interception of communications, asset seizure, confessions admissible.
- Application: Used against J&K militants, Indian Mujahideen. 		Repealed amid misuse allegations; 500+ convictions; provisions incorporated into UAPA.
National Security Act (NSA) Act 1980 - Objective: Preventive detention for national security threats.
- Provisions: Detention without charge up to 12 months; restricts judicial review.
- Application: Used in J&K, Northeast for separatists, radicals. 		600+ detentions (2024); controversial for limiting habeas corpus; used in communal riots.
Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA) Act 1958 (amended 1990) - Objective: Empower armed forces in disturbed areas.
- Provisions: Grants shoot-to-kill powers, immunity from prosecution; allows search without warrants.
- Application: Enforced in J&K, Northeast; partially lifted in Nagaland (2022). 		Criticized for human rights violations; Irom Sharmila’s 16-year fast; 1,500+ cases under review (2025).
National Investigation Agency Act Act 2008 (amended 2019) - Objective: Establish NIA for terrorism-related investigations.
- Provisions: Grants pan-India jurisdiction, powers to probe terror financing, attacks.
- Application: Investigates LeT, ISIS, Khalistani modules. 		1,000+ cases registered (2024); 200 ISIS arrests; criticized for central overreach.
National Security Guard Act Act 1986 - Objective: Establish NSG for counter-terror operations.
- Provisions: Creates elite force for hostage rescue, anti-terror ops.
- Application: Deployed in 2008 Mumbai attacks, 2016 Pathankot. 		12,000 personnel; 10 ops in 2024; key in urban terror response; Black Cat commandos.
Chhattisgarh Special Public Security Act Act 2005 - Objective: Counter Naxalite insurgency in Chhattisgarh.
- Provisions: Allows detention for unlawful activities; targets Maoist networks.
- Application: Used against CPI(Maoist), tribal sympathizers. 		1,000+ arrests (2024); criticized for targeting activists; supports SAMADHAN strategy.
Information & Media
The Information Technology (IT) Act Act 2000 (amended 2008) - Objective: Regulate cyber activities and electronic commerce.
- Provisions: Penalizes cybercrimes (hacking, data theft); Section 69A allows content blocking.
- Application: Curbs terror propaganda, fake news on X, Telegram. 		1,200+ cybercrime cases (2024); Section 66A struck down (2015); aligns with NCSP.
IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules Act 2021 - Objective: Regulate social media, OTT platforms, digital news.
- Provisions: Mandates grievance officers, content removal within 36 hours, message traceability.
- Application: Targets ISIS, TRF propaganda; misinformation in riots. 		15 X accounts suspended (2025); 1,000+ fake posts removed; criticized for curbing free speech.
Press Council Act Act 1978 - Objective: Regulate print media to protect press freedom, public interest.
- Provisions: Establishes PCI to monitor media ethics; addresses inflammatory content.
- Application: Tackles communal violence triggered by reporting. 		PCI handled 500+ complaints (2024); advisory role only; lacks statutory enforcement.
The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP) Act 2023 - Objective: Safeguard personal data and privacy in digital ecosystems.
- Provisions: Mandates consent for data processing; penalties for breaches.
- Application: Protects against data leaks in terror financing, cybercrimes. 		2M affected by breaches (2024); rules notified (2025); Data Protection Board forming.
National Cyber Security Policy (NCSP) Policy 2013 - Objective: Protect critical information infrastructure from cyber threats.
- Provisions: Establishes CERT-In, NCIIPC; promotes cyber hygiene, skill development.
- Application: Counters cyberattacks (e.g., China’s APT10, Pakistan’s Transparent Tribe). 		50+ government websites secured (2025); 1M cybersecurity jobs vacant; India-US CERT MoU.
Financial
Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) Act 2002 (amended 2019) - Objective: Prevent money laundering and terror financing.
- Provisions: Asset seizure, rigorous KYC norms; ED as nodal agency.
- Application: Targets hawala, drug money, terror funding (e.g., LeT, SFJ). 		₹10,000 Cr seized (2024); 500+ convictions; FATF-compliant; used against D-Company.
Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) Act 1999 - Objective: Regulate foreign exchange to prevent economic destabilization.
- Provisions: Monitors cross-border transactions; penalizes violations.
- Application: Curbs terror funding via foreign remittances (e.g., Khalistani diaspora). 		₹5,000 Cr violations probed (2024); used in 100+ terror funding cases.
Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) Act Act 2015 - Objective: Tax undisclosed foreign assets; combat black money.
- Provisions: 30–90% tax penalties, imprisonment up to 7 years.
- Application: Targets terror financing via offshore accounts. 		₹20,000 Cr disclosed (2015–2024); 100+ cases linked to terror funding (2025).
The Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act Act 1988 (amended 2016) - Objective: Prohibit benami transactions to curb black money.
- Provisions: Confiscates properties held under false names; 7-year imprisonment.
- Application: Used against organized crime, terror funding. 		1,500 properties attached (2024); ₹2,000 Cr seized; linked to D-Company probes.
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Act 2010 (amended 2020) - Objective: Regulate foreign donations to prevent misuse.
- Provisions: Mandates FCRA registration; restricts political, media use.
- Application: Curbs terror funding via NGOs (e.g., SFJ, ISI-linked groups). 		20,000 NGOs de-registered (2020–2024); ₹1,000 Cr frozen; used against radical outfits.
Cryptocurrency and Regulation of Official Digital Currency Bill Act 2021 (proposed) - Objective: Regulate cryptocurrencies to prevent illegal transactions.
- Provisions: Bans private cryptocurrencies; proposes RBI digital currency.
- Application: Aims to curb crypto-based terror financing, drug trade. 		Pending in Parliament; ₹500 Cr crypto frauds probed (2025); RBI digital rupee piloted.
Law & Order
Police Act Act 1861 - Objective: Establish framework for police organization, duties.
- Provisions: Defines police powers, hierarchy; state-level implementation.
- Application: Governs law enforcement in riots, insurgencies, public order. 		Outdated; Prakash Singh reforms (2006) partially implemented; 1M police personnel (2025).
Defence of India Act Act 1962 - Objective: Ensure national security during emergencies.
- Provisions: Grants detention, resource control powers.
- Application: Used in 1962 war; invoked in border conflicts. 		Largely obsolete; emergency powers now under NSA, UAPA; historical significance.
Civil Defence Act Act 1968 - Objective: Protect civilians during war, disasters.
- Provisions: Establishes civil defence volunteers; coordinates relief.
- Application: Mobilized in riots, border tensions, disasters. 		50,000 volunteers trained (2024); supports NDRF; limited enforcement.
Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) Act 1999 - Objective: Combat organized crime and terrorism.
- Provisions: Stringent bail conditions, confessions admissible; extended detention.
- Application: Targets D-Company, terror syndicates. 		Adopted by 7 states; 2,000+ convictions (1999–2024); criticized for harsh provisions.
Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force (ITBPF) Act Act 1992 - Objective: Establish ITBPF for India-China border security.
- Provisions: Defines ITBPF roles in border patrol, counter-insurgency.
- Application: Deployed in Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh; anti-Naxal ops. 		60,000 personnel; key in 2020 Galwan clash; supports CRPF in Bastar.
The Inter-Services Organisations (Command, Control, and Discipline) Act Act 2023 - Objective: Enhance coordination among armed forces.
- Provisions: Establishes unified command for joint operations; disciplinary framework.
- Application: Strengthens counter-terror ops in J&K, Northeast. 		Supports theaterisation; first joint ops in 2025 (Operation Mahadev); under CDS oversight.
Trafficking
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (NDPS) Act 1985 - Objective: Control drug trafficking and abuse.
- Provisions: Prohibits production, sale, possession of narcotics; stringent penalties.
- Application: Targets Punjab-Mexico, Northeast-Myanmar drug routes. 		10,000 kg drugs seized (2024); 2,000 convictions; NCORD coordinates enforcement.
Customs Act Act 1962 - Objective: Regulate imports/exports to prevent smuggling.
- Provisions: Empowers DRI for seizures, arrests; controls border trade.
- Application: Targets arms, drug smuggling via Mundra, Kandla ports. 		₹5,000 Cr smuggled goods seized (2024); Mundra port heroin case (2021).
Passport Act Act 1967 - Objective: Regulate issuance of passports, travel documents.
- Provisions: Penalizes forged passports, illegal migration.
- Application: Curbs trafficking, terror movement across borders. 		1,000+ fake passport cases (2024); used against ISI-linked networks.
National Policy on Narcotics Policy 2012 - Objective: Reduce drug supply and demand; coordinate anti-narcotics efforts.
- Provisions: Promotes de-addiction, crop substitution; strengthens NCB.
- Application: Targets Golden Crescent/Triangle trafficking. 		₹100 Cr rehab funds (2024); 500 rehab centers; supports NDPS enforcement.
Investigation
Maritime & Regional Security
SAGAR Policy (Security and Growth for All in the Region) Policy 2015 - Objective: Enhance maritime security, regional cooperation in IOR.
- Provisions: Strengthens Navy, Coast Guard; promotes anti-piracy, anti-trafficking.
- Application: Counters Chinese influence, smuggling in Indian Ocean. 		India-Sri Lanka-Maldives joint patrols (2025); 10 piracy incidents foiled; Quad framework.
Coastal Security Scheme Policy 2005 (Phase II 2011) - Objective: Strengthen coastal security post-2008 Mumbai attacks.
- Provisions: Funds coastal police stations, boats; integrates Navy, Coast Guard.
- Application: Prevents arms, drug smuggling via sea routes. 		204 coastal police stations; 1,000 boats deployed; 2025 Gujarat port raids.
Anti-Maritime Piracy Act Act 2022 - Objective: Prevent and punish maritime piracy in India’s EEZ and beyond.
- Scope: Criminalizes piracy, attempted piracy, abetment.
- Application: Aligns with UNCLOS, SUA Convention for maritime security. 		Passed by Indian Parliament 2022; first piracy conviction 2025; supports SAGAR initiative.
Miscellaneous
Public Gambling Act Act 1867 - Objective: Prohibit public gambling to maintain public order.
- Provisions: Penalizes gambling houses, betting activities.
- Application: Targets illegal betting rackets linked to crime syndicates. 		500+ raids (2024); linked to organized crime; outdated for online gambling.
National Security Strategy (NSS) Policy Proposed (2025) - Objective: Provide comprehensive framework for internal, external security.
- Provisions: Integrates cyber, terror, border security strategies.
- Application: Aims to unify Naxal, J&K, Northeast responses. 		Under NSC review; draft released (2025); aligns with theaterisation, Quad.
- India's important bodies regarding internal security (Unverified) -
Body/Law Type Year Authority Purpose/Description Special Notes
Cybersecurity & Information
CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) Agency 2004 Statutory - Objective: Nodal agency for cybersecurity incident response under IT Act, 2000.
- Provisions: Issues advisories, conducts audits, coordinates with global CERTs; mandates incident reporting within 6 hours.
- Application: Handles DDoS, ransomware; responded to 1,200+ incidents in 2024. 		Under MeitY; handled AIIMS breach (2025); 9,700 audits (2024–25); collaborates with NCIIPC, I4C.
National Cybersecurity Coordination Centre (NCCC) Agency 2015 Executive - Objective: Monitor cyberspace threats, facilitate intelligence sharing.
- Provisions: Scans traffic at entry/exit points; coordinates with ISPs, LEAs for e-surveillance.
- Application: Supports CERT-In in threat detection; generates situational awareness. 		Under NTRO; resource constraints (2025); integrates with MAC; privacy concerns; 5G monitoring focus.
NCIIPC (National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre) Agency 2014 Statutory - Objective: Protect critical information infrastructure under Section 70A, IT Act.
- Provisions: Identifies CII sectors (power, telecom, banking); sets protection standards.
- Application: Coordinates with NSCS; runs vulnerability disclosure program. 		Under NTRO/PMO; 24x7 help desk; collaborated on 2025 Cybersecurity Framework; protects 10+ CII sectors.
I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre) Agency 2018 Executive - Objective: Coordinate national response to cybercrimes under MHA.
- Provisions: Manages National Cybercrime Reporting Portal; includes TAU, JIT, Forensic Lab.
- Application: Handles reporting, forensics; coordinates MLAT for global cybercrimes. 		Under NCRB/MHA; 1M+ reports (2024); includes NCTC, RCIC; key in 2025 fraud busts; women safety focus.
Central Monitoring System (CMS) Agency 2013 Executive - Objective: Centralize telecom traffic monitoring for security.
- Provisions: Enables real-time interception of calls, data without service provider involvement.
- Application: Used by LEAs for terror surveillance, cyber threat tracking. 		Under DoT; privacy concerns; integrates with NATGRID; operational in 2025 for J&K monitoring.
Network Traffic Analysis (NETRA) Agency 2013 Executive - Objective: Analyze internet traffic for security threats.
- Provisions: DRDO-developed tool for keyword-based surveillance; flags suspicious communications.
- Application: Detects terror chatter, online radicalization. 		Under DRDO; expanded in 2025; mass surveillance concerns; AI-enhanced version deployed.
National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) Agency 2004 Executive - Objective: Provide technical intelligence for national security.
- Provisions: Handles SIGINT, geospatial intel; oversees NCCC, NCIIPC.
- Application: Supports cyber ops, satellite surveillance for internal threats. 		Under PMO; key in 2025 cyber threat assessments; coordinates with DCA, CERT-In.
Financial
Financial Intelligence Unit - India (FIU-IND) Agency 2004 Statutory - Objective: Analyze suspicious financial transactions to combat ML/TF.
- Provisions: Processes STRs/CTRs under PMLA; disseminates intel to LEAs.
- Application: Tracks terror funding, hawala; supports FATF compliance. 		Under MoF; 1M STRs processed (2024); 500+ terror leads; Egmont Group member; 2025 SFJ funding probe.
FICN Coordination Group (FCORD) Agency 2016 Executive - Objective: Combat counterfeit currency circulation.
- Provisions: Coordinates RBI, MHA, LEAs for detection, investigation.
- Application: Targets ISI-backed fake notes funding terror. 		Under MHA; 1,000+ fake notes seized (2024); integrated with NIA; 2025 digital currency focus.
Enforcement Directorate (ED) Agency 1956 Executive - Objective: Enforce PMLA, FEMA for economic offences.
- Provisions: Investigates ML/TF; attaches assets; coordinates with FIU-IND.
- Application: Probes terror funding, hawala (e.g., LeT, Khalistan). 		Under MoF; ₹15,000 Cr attached (2024); 300+ terror cases; FATF audits (2025).
Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) Agency 1957 Executive - Objective: Combat smuggling, customs evasion, economic offences.
- Provisions: Investigates under Customs Act; coordinates with NCB, ED.
- Application: Targets drug, arms, gold smuggling. 		Under MoF; 3,000 kg heroin seized (2021–2024); 500 arrests; key in Mundra port case (2021).
Intelligence & Coordination
National Security Council (NSC) 1998 Executive - Objective: Apex body for national security decision-making.
- Provisions: Chaired by PM; includes Cabinet ministers, service chiefs.
- Application: Advises on J&K, Naxal, cyber policies. 		Under PMO; NSCS as secretariat; 2025 reconstitution with Alok Joshi as NSAB Chair.
Strategic Policy Group (SPG) 1998 Executive - Objective: Operational arm of NSC for crisis management.
- Provisions: Led by NSA; coordinates MHA, MoD, MEA responses.
- Application: Handles terror attacks, border incursions. 		Under NSC; key in 2025 Operation Sindoor coordination.
National Security Advisory Board (NSAB) 1998 Executive - Objective: Advise NSC on long-term security policies.
- Provisions: 7-10 experts; reports to NSA; includes NIB, TCG.
- Application: Policy on cyber, maritime security. 		Reconstituted Apr 2025 with Alok Joshi as Chair; advises on 2025 NSS draft.
National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS) 1998 Executive - Objective: Secretariat for NSC; strategic coordination.
- Provisions: Led by NSA; coordinates cyber, intel policies.
- Application: Oversees NCIIPC, NCCC; bilateral cyber dialogues (US, UK). 		Under PMO; nodal for cybersecurity (2025 amendment); engages SCO, Quad.
Joint Intelligence Committee (JIC) 1968 Executive - Objective: Assess and analyze intelligence from IB, RAW, military.
- Provisions: Under NSCS; prepares daily assessments for PM.
- Application: Domestic/foreign intel fusion for threats. 		Under Cabinet Secretariat; 2025 updates on J&K infiltration; coordinates with MAC.
The National Intelligence Grid (NATGRID) 2008 Executive - Objective: Integrate databases for real-time terror intel.
- Provisions: Links 21 ministries' data (bank, immigration, telecom).
- Application: Tracks suspects, foils plots via data analytics. 		Under MHA; operational 2025; privacy safeguards added; connects 20+ databases.
Multi-Agency Centre (MAC) 2001 Executive - Objective: Real-time intel sharing among agencies.
- Provisions: Under IB; 24x7 ops room; links RAW, NIA, state police.
- Application: Counters terror, insurgency threats. 		Under MHA; foiled 10 plots (2024); expanded in 2025 for cyber intel.
Intelligence Bureau (IB) Agency 1887 (reformed 1947) Executive - Objective: Domestic intelligence for internal security.
- Provisions: Counter-intelligence, counter-terrorism; oversees MAC.
- Application: Monitors J&K, Naxal, communal threats. 		Under MHA; foiled 15 plots (2024); 2025 Pahalgam attack probe; grants security clearances.
Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) Agency 1968 Executive - Objective: External intelligence with internal security overlap.
- Provisions: Counters cross-border threats; supports J&K ops.
- Application: Tracks LeT, JeM funding in PoK. 		Under Cabinet Secretariat; key in 2025 IAF strikes; coordinates with MAC.
Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA) Agency 2002 Executive - Objective: Coordinate military intelligence for security.
- Provisions: Integrates army, navy, air force intel; supports internal ops.
- Application: Border security, counter-insurgency. 		Under MoD; nodal for defence intel; 2025 focus on LAC; coordinates with RAW, IB.
Investigation
National Investigation Agency (NIA) Agency 2008 Statutory - Objective: Investigate terror-related offences pan-India.
- Provisions: Under NIA Act; probes UAPA cases, terror financing.
- Application: Handles J&K, Northeast, ISIS cases. 		Under MHA; 1,000+ cases (2024); 200 ISIS arrests; 2025 Hyderabad module bust.
Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) Agency 1986 Statutory - Objective: Coordinate anti-narcotics operations under NDPS Act.
- Provisions: Conducts raids, intelligence gathering; international cooperation.
- Application: Targets Punjab, Northeast drug cartels (e.g., Sinaloa links). 		Under MHA; 500 kg meth seized (2025); 1,000 NDPS cases (2024); UNODC partner.
Maritime & Regional Security
National Command Control Communication and Intelligence Network (NC3I) 2014 Executive - Objective: Enhance coastal security via integrated command.
- Provisions: Links radars, vessels for real-time surveillance.
- Application: Monitors EEZ, prevents smuggling, incursions. 		Under Navy; 51 radar stations; integrated with IFC-IOR (2025).
Information Fusion Centre - Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) 2018 Executive - Objective: Fuse maritime intel from regional partners.
- Provisions: 24x7 center; shares data on piracy, trafficking.
- Application: Counters IOR threats with 25+ countries. 		In Gurugram; 10 incidents foiled (2024); Quad partner (2025).
Coastal Surveillance Network (CSN) 2005 Executive - Objective: Monitor coastal areas for threats.
- Provisions: 200+ coastal stations with radars, cameras.
- Application: Detects smuggling, infiltration. 		Under MHA; integrated with NC3I; 2025 drone surveillance upgrades.
National Committee for Strengthening Maritime and Coastal Security (NCSMCS) 2004 Executive - Objective: Coordinate maritime security policies.
- Provisions: Chaired by Cabinet Secretary; includes MoD, MHA, MEA.
- Application: Oversees CSN, IFC-IOR implementation. 		Under Cabinet Secretariat; 2025 SAGAR alignment review.
Trafficking & Human Security
Anti-Trafficking Nodal Cell 2017 Executive - Objective: Coordinate anti-human trafficking efforts.
- Provisions: Under MHA; links states, NGOs for rescues, rehab.
- Application: Targets cross-border trafficking from Bangladesh, Nepal. 		Under MHA; 1,000+ rescues (2024); supports I4C for cyber trafficking; 2025 expansion.
Trafficking of Persons (Prevention, Protection and Rehabilitation) Bill Law 2021 (introduced) Statutory - Objective: Prevent trafficking, protect victims.
- Provisions: Establishes Anti-Trafficking Units, Rehab Fund; 10-year punishment.
- Application: Covers sex, labor trafficking; state-level implementation. 		Pending in Parliament (2025); replaces Immoral Traffic Act; 47,000 cases (2024 NCRB).
Miscellaneous
National Command Authority (NCA) 2003 Executive - Objective: Oversee nuclear command and control.
- Provisions: Chaired by PM; includes Political Council, Exec Council.
- Application: Ensures nuclear security, deterrence. 		Under PMO; integrates with NSC; strategic role in crisis management.
National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) Agency 1986 Executive - Objective: Compile crime data, assist investigations.
- Provisions: Maintains CCDS, CCTNS; supports I4C, NIA.
- Application: Tracks terror, cybercrimes; annual Crime in India report. 		Under MHA; 47,000 trafficking cases (2024); cybercrime portal integration; 2025 AI analytics pilot.
- World's important acts, laws, policies relevant against terrorism, cyber crime, etc (Unverified) -
Convention/Law/Policy Year Authority Purpose/Description Key Provisions Special Notes
Cybercrime
Budapest Convention on Cybercrime 2001 International Treaty - Objective: Harmonize national laws on cybercrime and enhance international cooperation.
- Scope: Addresses offences like illegal access, data interference, system interference, misuse of devices.
- Application: Facilitates extradition, mutual legal assistance for cybercrime. 		- Substantive Provisions: Criminalizes hacking, fraud, child pornography, copyright infringement (Articles 2-10).
- Procedural Provisions: Allows search/seizure of electronic data, real-time data collection (Articles 16-21).
- Cooperation: Expedited data preservation, mutual assistance (Articles 23-31). 		Adopted in Budapest; 69 parties (2025); Second Additional Protocol (2022) on enhanced cooperation; India not a party but aligns IT Act with it.
United Nations Convention on Cybercrime 2024 International Treaty - Objective: Establish global framework to combat cybercrime, including cyber-terrorism.
- Scope: Covers cyber-dependent crimes, online fraud, child exploitation, cyber-terrorism.
- Application: Promotes global cooperation, capacity building; addresses Budapest Convention gaps. 		- Offences: Criminalizes cyber-enabled crimes, ICT misuse for terrorism (Articles 6-15).
- Cooperation: Mutual legal assistance, 24/7 contact points, victim protection (Articles 24-40).
- Capacity Building: Technical assistance for developing nations (Articles 41-47). 		Adopted by UNGA Dec 2024; not yet in force (2025); India supported; addresses privacy, sovereignty concerns; UNODC oversight.
Transnational Organized Crime
United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC / Palermo Convention) 2000 International Treaty - Objective: Combat transnational organized crime, including human trafficking, migrant smuggling, arms trafficking.
- Scope: Defines organized criminal groups; focuses on prevention, criminalization, cooperation.
- Application: Main global instrument against crime syndicates; 191 parties. 		- Core Provisions: Criminalizes participation in organized groups, money laundering, corruption (Articles 5-10).
- Protocols: Trafficking in Persons, Migrant Smuggling, Firearms (2000-2001).
- Cooperation: Extradition, joint investigations, asset recovery (Articles 13-24). 		Adopted in Palermo; in force 2003; India ratified 2011; UNODC custodian; used in 2025 Sinaloa cartel probes.
Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons (Palermo Protocol) 2000 International Treaty - Objective: Prevent trafficking in persons, protect victims, punish traffickers.
- Scope: Defines trafficking as recruitment by force for exploitation.
- Application: Global anti-trafficking framework; 181 parties. 		- Prevention: Border controls, demand reduction (Articles 9-11).
- Protection: Victim assistance, non-criminalization, repatriation (Articles 6-8).
- Punishment: Criminalization, extradition (Articles 10-16). 		In force 2003; influences India’s Trafficking Bill 2021; 47,000 trafficking cases in India (2024 NCRB).
Terrorism
Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Maritime Navigation (SUA Convention) 1988 International Treaty - Objective: Prevent terrorism and unlawful acts threatening maritime navigation.
- Scope: Criminalizes acts endangering ships or maritime safety.
- Application: Protects international shipping; 170 parties. 		- Offences: Ship seizure, violence, damaging ships (Article 3).
- Jurisdiction: State jurisdiction over offenders, extradition (Articles 6-10).
- 2005 Protocol: Covers WMD transport, boarding procedures. 		Adopted by IMO; in force 1992; India ratified 1995; influences Anti-Maritime Piracy Act 2022.
Drug Trafficking
United Nations Convention Against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Vienna Convention) 1988 International Treaty - Objective: Combat global drug trafficking and abuse.
- Scope: Covers production, trafficking, and precursor chemicals.
- Application: Strengthens international anti-drug cooperation; 190 parties. 		- Offences: Criminalizes drug production, trafficking, money laundering (Article 3).
- Controls: Regulates 22 substances, precursor monitoring (Articles 12-14).
- Cooperation: Extradition, mutual legal assistance (Articles 6-9). 		In force 1990; India ratified 1990; supports NCB operations; 500 kg meth seized in India (2025).
Corruption
United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC) 2003 International Treaty - Objective: Prevent and combat corruption, promote integrity.
- Scope: Covers bribery, embezzlement, money laundering, asset recovery.
- Application: Global anti-corruption framework; 190 parties. 		- Prevention: Anti-corruption bodies, public sector transparency (Articles 5-14).
- Criminalization: Bribery, illicit enrichment, abuse of power (Articles 15-25).
- Asset Recovery: Return of stolen assets (Articles 51-59). 		In force 2005; India ratified 2011; supports ED’s PMLA probes; ₹15,000 Cr assets attached (2024).
Maritime Security
United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) 1982 International Treaty - Objective: Establish legal framework for maritime activities and security.
- Scope: Defines territorial seas, EEZ, piracy, maritime boundaries.
- Application: Governs global maritime law; 168 parties. 		- Jurisdiction: Territorial sea (12 nm), EEZ (200 nm) rights (Articles 2-33).
- Piracy: Universal jurisdiction over piracy, state cooperation (Articles 100-107).

- All Indian constitutional articles, laws, acts, policies, etc for ethics (Unverified) -
Key Events/Initiatives Type Details (Ethical Focus & Key Provisions)
PRE-INDEPENDENCE (1800s–1947)
Indian Penal Code, 1860 Act Description:
  • Introduced by Lord Macaulay under British India
  • First comprehensive criminal code in India
  • Sections 161–165 (later repealed) specifically penalized public servants
  • Penalized accepting bribes or gratuities
  • Established criminal liability for abuse of official position
Ethical focus:
  • Integrity in public office
  • Prevention of corruption
  • Accountability of colonial administrators
  • Foundation of public servant liability
Indian Evidence Act, 1872 Act Description:
  • Regulates admissibility of evidence in Indian courts
  • Section 123: Protects official communications from disclosure
  • Section 114: Allows courts to presume corruption in certain cases
  • Ensures structured use of evidence in corruption trials
Ethical focus:
  • Fairness in judicial proceedings
  • Veracity and reliability of evidence
  • Ethical use of official information
  • Judicial integrity
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 Act Description:
  • Governs arrest, investigation, and trial procedures
  • Sections 154–176: Mandates FIR registration
  • Requires fair and impartial investigation
  • Protects against arbitrary police action
Ethical focus:
  • Due process of law
  • Accountability in criminal investigations
  • Protection from arbitrary arrest
  • Ethical policing standards
Prevention of Corruption Act Roots (Colonial Era) Act (Legacy) Description:
  • Early anti-corruption provisions under IPC and Police Act, 1861
  • Public servants liable for criminal misconduct
  • Laid foundation for independent anti-corruption law
  • Precursor to Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Ethical focus:
  • Public servant integrity
  • Deterrence against misuse of power
  • Accountability in colonial bureaucracy
POST-INDEPENDENCE (1947–1970s)
Articles 14 & 21 (1950) Constitutional Article Description:
  • Article 14: Equality before the law and equal protection
  • Article 21: No deprivation of life/liberty except by procedure established by law
  • Expanded in Maneka Gandhi case (1978) to include fairness and reasonableness
Ethical focus:
  • Non-arbitrary governance
  • Integrity in public actions
  • Protection from unethical state overreach
  • Rule of law as ethical foundation
Article 48A & 51A(g) (1976, 42nd Amendment) Constitutional Article Description:
  • Article 48A: State duty to protect and improve the environment
  • Article 51A(g): Fundamental duty of citizens to protect nature, wildlife, forests
  • Introduced via 42nd Constitutional Amendment
Ethical focus:
  • Intergenerational equity
  • Moral responsibility for sustainability
  • Civic environmental ethics
  • State-citizen partnership in conservation
Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 Act Description:
  • Established Medical Council of India (MCI)
  • Regulates medical education and professional practice
  • Section 20A: Empowers code of ethics (2002 Regulations)
  • Prohibits fee splitting, false advertising, unethical practices
Ethical focus:
  • Professional integrity
  • Patient confidentiality
  • Trust in doctor-patient relationship
  • Ethical medical conduct
All India Service (Conduct) Rules, 1968 Rule Description:
  • Applies to IAS, IPS, Indian Forest Service
  • Rule 3: Maintain absolute integrity and devotion to duty
  • Rule 16: Annual immovable property return mandatory
  • Rule 4: No political activity or membership
Ethical focus:
  • Political neutrality
  • Conflict of interest avoidance
  • Transparency in assets
  • Ethical civil service conduct
Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 (Amended 2021) Act Description:
  • Allows termination up to 20 weeks (24 weeks in special cases)
  • Requires one/two doctor opinions based on gestational age
  • Mandatory consent of the woman
  • Amended in 2021 to expand access and privacy
Ethical focus:
  • Women’s bodily autonomy
  • Medical ethics in reproductive care
  • Beneficence and non-maleficence
  • Confidentiality and dignity
Nolan Committee Principles (1995, UK; Adopted via 2nd ARC) International Guideline Description:
  • 7 principles: Selflessness, Integrity, Objectivity, Accountability, Openness, Honesty, Leadership
  • Recommended by 2nd ARC (2007) for Indian civil service code
  • Adopted as ethical benchmark for public servants
Ethical focus:
  • Universal ethical governance standards
  • Leadership by example
  • Moral accountability in public life
1980s–1990s
Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 Act Description:
  • Prohibits holding property in another’s name to evade tax or law
  • Section 3: Bans all benami transactions
  • Penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment
  • Foundation for 2016 amendment
Ethical focus:
  • Financial transparency
  • Anti-corruption in asset holding
  • Prevention of black money
  • Tax justice
Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 Act Description:
  • Consolidates and strengthens anti-corruption laws
  • Sections 7–12: Criminalize taking bribe, criminal misconduct
  • Defines “public servant” broadly
  • 2018 amendment protects bona fide decisions
Ethical focus:
  • Integrity in public service
  • Zero tolerance for undue advantage
  • Public trust in governance
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Key Amendments 1988–1996) Act Description:
  • Section 8: Disqualification on conviction for certain offenses
  • Section 123: Defines corrupt practices (bribery, undue influence)
  • 1988 amendment introduced anti-defection law (10th Schedule)
Ethical focus:
  • Clean politics
  • Free and fair elections
  • Voter sovereignty
  • Electoral integrity
Model Code of Conduct (Election Commission of India, 1991) Policy Description:
  • Voluntary code enforced during elections
  • Prohibits hate speech, misuse of government machinery
  • Bans voter inducements, personal attacks
  • Enforced via ECI observers and expenditure monitoring
Ethical focus:
  • Electoral integrity
  • Level playing field
  • Democratic fairness
Right to Information Act, 2005 (Roots in 1990s PILs & FOI Movement) Act Description:
  • Section 4: Proactive disclosure by public authorities
  • Section 8: Limited exemptions for national security
  • Overrides Official Secrets Act, 1923
  • Roots in 1990s freedom of information movement
Ethical focus:
  • Transparency in governance
  • Accountability of public officials
  • Citizen empowerment
  • Fight against administrative secrecy
Companies Act, 1956 (Section 135 CSR Roots) Act Description:
  • Precursor to mandatory CSR in 2013 Act
  • Introduced voluntary CSR guidelines
  • Encouraged ethical business beyond profit
Ethical focus:
  • Corporate social responsibility
  • Stakeholder theory
  • Ethical business conduct
OECD Principles of Corporate Governance (1999) International Guideline Description:
  • 6 principles: Shareholder rights, equitable treatment
  • Stakeholder role, disclosure, board duties, sustainability
  • Adopted in India via SEBI regulations
Ethical focus:
  • Corporate integrity
  • Transparency in reporting
  • Long-term value creation
Model Police Act, 2006 (Drafted in 1990s by Ribeiro & Malimath Committees) Policy Description:
  • Section 4: Emphasizes police accountability
  • Recommends independent complaints authority
  • Mandates human rights training
  • Drafted in 1990s, enacted in some states post-2006
Ethical focus:
  • Community policing
  • Fairness in law enforcement
  • Dignity in policing
2000s
Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 (Enacted in 2011, Notified 2014) Act Description:
  • Section 11: Ensures anonymity and protection from victimization
  • Allows disclosure to Competent Authority (CVC)
  • Enacted in 2011, notified in 2014
Ethical focus:
  • Public interest reporting
  • Courage in truth-telling
  • Institutional support for whistleblowers
Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 Act Description:
  • Independent anti-corruption ombudsman
  • Covers PM, ministers, MPs, Group A officers
  • Section 14: Inquiry into allegations of misconduct
Ethical focus:
  • Political accountability
  • Institutional integrity
  • End to impunity
Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Amendment Act, 2016 Amendment Description:
  • Strengthens 1988 Act with stricter penalties
  • Section 2(9): Defines benami property
  • Penalty: Up to 7 years + property confiscation
  • Over 100 attachments by ED by 2025
Ethical focus:
  • Anti-money laundering
  • Financial transparency
  • Tax justice
Companies Act, 2013 (Section 135 – CSR) Act Description:
  • Mandatory CSR: 2% of average net profit (3 years)
  • Spent on Schedule VII activities (education, health, environment)
  • CSR Committee mandatory for eligible companies
Ethical focus:
  • Corporate citizenship
  • Social justice
  • Stakeholder governance
2nd Administrative Reforms Commission – 4th Report on Ethics in Governance (2007) Report Description:
  • Recommends ethics code for civil servants
  • Adoption of Nolan principles
  • Whistleblower protection, ethics audits
  • Political funding reform
Ethical focus:
  • Systemic integrity
  • Accountability in public service
  • Ethical leadership
Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (Amended 2019) Act Description:
  • Section 3: Defines offense of money laundering
  • ED investigates predicate offenses under PCA
  • 2019 amendment expanded scope
Ethical focus:
  • Integrity in financial systems
  • Prevention of corruption proceeds
  • Financial accountability
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Act, 2013 Act Description:
  • Section 4: Mandatory social impact assessment
  • Section 26: Consent of 70–80% landowners required
  • Replaced colonial Land Acquisition Act, 1894
Ethical focus:
  • Fairness in public projects
  • Transparency in land deals
  • Consent and protection of vulnerable
2020s
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 Act Description:
  • Section 8: Consent must be free, informed, specific, unconditional
  • Data fiduciary accountability and data minimization
  • Applies to digital personal data processed in India
Ethical focus:
  • Privacy as dignity
  • User control over data
  • Ethical AI and data use
  • Accountability of data handlers
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Replaces IPC) Act Description:
  • Section 61: Criminal breach of trust
  • Section 69: Seduction with false promise of marriage
  • Replaces Indian Penal Code, 1860
Ethical focus:
  • Integrity in personal and public dealings
  • Criticized for ethics gaps in safeguards
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Replaces CrPC) Act Description:
  • Section 173: Ethics in police reporting
  • Allows digital trials, e-FIR, video recording
  • Replaces Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
Ethical focus:
  • Due process in modern form
  • Transparency in investigation
  • Modern ethical policing
IT (Intermediary Guidelines & Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (Amended 2025) Rule Description:
  • Rule 3(1)(b): Mandates labeling of AI-generated content
  • Grievance officer response within 24 hours
  • 2025 amendment: Deepfake disclaimers mandatory
Ethical focus:
  • Transparency in digital content
  • Misinformation control
  • Digital media ethics
Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 (SC Review 2025) Act Description:
  • Section 3: Prohibits discrimination
  • Section 12: Mandates welfare schemes
  • 2025 Jane Kaushik case mandates full implementation
Ethical focus:
  • Inclusion and dignity
  • Equality for transgender persons
  • State responsibility for marginalized
Lokpal Amendment Bill, 2024 Amendment Description:
  • Addresses 2025 Supreme Court concerns
  • Focuses on delays in Lokpal appointments
  • Strengthens inquiry and prosecution process
Ethical focus:
  • Accountability in anti-corruption bodies
  • Faster justice delivery
  • Operational independence of Lokpal

- All bodies, organization, etc for ethics for India (Unverified) -
Key Bodies/Organizations/Committees Type Details (Description & Ethical Focus)
PRE-INDEPENDENCE (1800s–1947)
Indian Medical Association (IMA), 1928 Voluntary Body Description:
  • Founded as All India Medical Association
  • Represents 3.5 lakh+ doctors across India
  • Voluntary body for medical ethics, education, and advocacy
  • Historically advocated ethical practice during colonial era
Ethical focus:
  • Professional integrity
  • Patient rights
  • Issues code of ethics
  • Promotes ethical medical conduct
Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) Precursor Bodies, 1911 Precursor Body Description:
  • Roots in Advisory Board for Medical Research
  • Established under British India for scientific inquiry
  • Apex biomedical research body precursor
  • Evolved into modern ICMR post-independence
Ethical focus:
  • Early ethics guidelines for human trials
  • Foundation for research integrity
  • Precursor to National Ethical Guidelines (2017)
POST-INDEPENDENCE (1947–1970s)
Medical Council of India (MCI), 1956 Statutory Body Description:
  • Statutory body under Indian Medical Council Act, 1956
  • Regulates medical education and practice
  • Maintains Indian Medical Register
  • Enforces code of medical ethics
  • Dissolved in 2020, replaced by NMC
Ethical focus:
  • Professional misconduct inquiries
  • Patient confidentiality
  • Ethical standards in medical education
Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), 1964 Statutory Body Description:
  • Statutory body under CVC Act, 2003 (roots in 1964)
  • Supervises vigilance in central government
  • Advisory Board on Corruption Prevention
  • Oversees 4 million+ central government employees
Ethical focus:
  • Integrity in public service
  • Anti-corruption framework
  • Ethical conduct enforcement
Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), 1911 (Reorganized 1949) Research Body Description:
  • Apex biomedical research agency under MoHFW
  • Reorganized post-independence in 1949
  • Funds and conducts health research
  • ICMR Bioethics Unit at NCDIR, Bengaluru
  • Promotes ethical biomedical research
Ethical focus:
  • National Ethical Guidelines for Biomedical Research (2017)
  • Oversees 500+ Institutional Ethics Committees
  • Ensures human subject protection
1980s–1990s
Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), 1963 (Active Expansion) Investigative Agency Description:
  • Premier investigative agency under DoPT
  • Established via Delhi Special Police Establishment Act
  • Probes corruption, economic offenses, major crimes
  • Special Police Establishment (SPE) for integrity cases
Ethical focus:
  • Accountability in public servants
  • Anti-corruption enforcement
  • Integrity in investigation
Lokpal & Lokayuktas Precursor (Committee), 1963 Committee Description:
  • 1st Administrative Reforms Commission recommendation
  • Proposed independent ombudsman for corruption
  • Led to Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
Ethical focus:
  • Institutional integrity
  • Political and bureaucratic accountability
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), 1993 Statutory Body Description:
  • Statutory body under Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
  • Investigates human rights violations
  • 2025: Processed 1.5 lakh+ complaints
  • Focus on custodial deaths, police reforms
Ethical focus:
  • Human dignity
  • Accountability of state agencies
  • Ethical governance in law enforcement
State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs), 1993 State-Level Body Description:
  • 15 SHRCs operational across states
  • State-level human rights protection
  • E.g., Maharashtra SHRC handles police ethics cases
Ethical focus:
  • Local accountability
  • Ethical public service delivery
  • Decentralized rights enforcement
2nd Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC), 2005 Commission Description:
  • Chaired by Veerappa Moily
  • 15 reports on governance reforms
  • 4th Report (2007): Ethics in Governance
Ethical focus:
  • Nolan Principles adoption
  • Whistleblower protection
  • Ethics code for civil servants
National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers (NABH), 2006 Accreditation Board Description:
  • Constituent board of Quality Council of India
  • Accredits hospitals and healthcare facilities
  • 2,500+ accredited hospitals by 2025
Ethical focus:
  • Patient safety
  • Ethics committee compliance
  • Quality and ethical healthcare delivery
2000s–2010s
National Medical Commission (NMC), 2020 (Replaces MCI) Statutory Body Description:
  • Statutory body under NMC Act, 2019
  • Replaced Medical Council of India in 2020
  • Regulates medical education and profession
  • 4 autonomous boards: UGMEB, PGMEB, MARB, EMRB
Ethical focus:
  • Professional misconduct regulation
  • Code of ethics enforcement
  • Ethics and Medical Registration Board (EMRB)
Lokpal, 2013 Statutory Ombudsman Description:
  • Statutory anti-corruption ombudsman under Lokpal Act, 2013
  • Covers PM, ministers, MPs, Group A officers
  • Inquires into corruption allegations
  • 2025: Received 1,200+ complaints
Ethical focus:
  • Political integrity
  • Accountability at highest levels
  • End to impunity
Lokayuktas, 2013 State-Level Ombudsman Description:
  • State-level anti-corruption ombudsmen
  • 20+ Lokayuktas operational across states
  • E.g., Karnataka Lokayukta probes public servant ethics
Ethical focus:
  • State-level corruption probe
  • Ethical conduct in state administration
National Commission for Women (NCW), 1992 Statutory Body Description:
  • Statutory body under NCW Act, 1990
  • Protects and promotes women’s rights
  • 2025: Handled 25,000+ complaints
Ethical focus:
  • Gender justice
  • Accountability in gender-based violence
  • Women’s dignity and equality
National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), 2004 Constitutional Body Description:
  • Constitutional body under Article 338
  • Safeguards rights of Scheduled Castes
  • Investigates atrocities and discrimination
Ethical focus:
  • Anti-discrimination
  • Integrity in affirmative action
  • Social justice enforcement
National Commission for Minorities (NCM), 1992 Statutory Body Description:
  • Statutory body under NCM Act, 1992
  • Protects rights of religious and linguistic minorities
  • Monitors minority welfare schemes
Ethical focus:
  • Secularism
  • Accountability in minority welfare
  • Inclusive governance
National Green Tribunal (NGT), 2010 Statutory Tribunal Description:
  • Statutory body under NGT Act, 2010
  • Fast-track environmental justice
  • 50,000+ cases resolved by 2025
Ethical focus:
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Accountability for polluters
  • Intergenerational equity
Ethics Committees in Parliament (Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha), 1997/2000 Parliamentary Committee Description:
  • Lok Sabha Ethics Committee (1997)
  • Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee (2000)
  • 2025: Investigated 15 MP conduct cases
Ethical focus:
  • Parliamentary conduct
  • MP integrity
  • Corruption inquiries
2020s
National Ethics Committee Registry for Biomedical and Health Research (NECRBHR), 2019 Registry Description:
  • Under Department of Health Research (DHR), MoHFW
  • Registers Ethics Committees for biomedical research
  • 1,083 registered ECs (as of Sep 2023)
  • 2025: AI ethics integration
Ethical focus:
  • Research ethics compliance
  • Adherence to ICMR Guidelines
  • Human subject protection
Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) Ethics Committees, 2019 Regulatory Body Description:
  • Regulatory body under New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
  • Registers ECs for clinical trials
  • 841 institutional, 242 independent ECs
  • 2025: 1,200+ registered
Ethical focus:
  • Clinical trial integrity
  • Subject protection
  • Ethical review of drug trials
Institutional Ethics Committees (IEC), 2006 (ICMR Guidelines) Institutional Committee Description:
  • Under ICMR National Ethical Guidelines
  • 500+ IECs in medical institutions
  • Composition: 7–15 members, including layperson
  • 2025: Focus on AI and biotech ethics
Ethical focus:
  • Review of biomedical research
  • Informed consent
  • Risk-benefit assessment
Independent Ethics Committees (IEC-Ind), 2013 Independent Committee Description:
  • Registered with CDSCO
  • 242 standalone ethics committees
  • Primarily for bioequivalence studies
  • 2025: Expanded to pharma ethics
Ethical focus:
  • Independent ethical review
  • Cannot review clinical trials
  • Ensures unbiased assessment
National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), 1987 (Ethics Accreditation) Accreditation Board Description:
  • Under Quality Council of India
  • Accredits testing and calibration labs
  • 2,500+ labs accredited by 2025
Ethical focus:
  • Integrity in research data
  • Ethical testing standards
  • Scientific credibility
National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC), 1993 (Statutory 2018) Constitutional Body Description:
  • Constitutional body under Article 338B
  • Granted constitutional status in 2018
  • Protects rights of Other Backward Classes (OBCs)
Ethical focus:
  • Social justice
  • Accountability in reservation implementation
  • Equity in opportunity
- All bodies, organization, etc for ethics for World (Unverified) -
Key Bodies/Organizations/Committees Type Details (Description & Ethical Focus)
PRE-1980s (Early Foundations)
World Medical Association (WMA), 1947 Voluntary Association Description:
  • Founded post-WWII by 27 national medical associations
  • Global federation of 115+ national medical associations
  • Represents 10M+ physicians worldwide
  • Developed WMA Declaration of Helsinki (1964, revised 2013)
Ethical focus:
  • Medical research ethics
  • Informed consent
  • Patient safety
  • Non-maleficence
  • Global standard for human trials
International Association for Bioethics (IAB), 1992 Voluntary Association Description:
  • Founded in 1992
  • Global forum for bioethics scholars
  • Promotes ethical reflection on life sciences
  • Hosts biennial World Congress of Bioethics
Ethical focus:
  • Multidisciplinary dialogue
  • Intellectual freedom
  • Human dignity in research
  • 1,000+ members from 60+ countries
1980s–1990s
International Bioethics Committee (IBC), UNESCO, 1993 Advisory Committee Description:
  • 36 independent experts from diverse disciplines & regions
  • Advises UNESCO Director-General on bioethics
  • Produced Universal Declaration on Bioethics and Human Rights (2005)
  • Meets annually
Ethical focus:
  • Human dignity
  • Non-discrimination
  • Benefit-sharing in life sciences
Intergovernmental Bioethics Committee (IGBC), UNESCO, 1998 Governmental Committee Description:
  • 36 UNESCO Member States
  • Examines IBC recommendations
  • Endorsed Declaration on Human Genetic Data (2003)
  • Endorsed Universal Declaration on Bioethics (2005)
  • Biennial sessions
Ethical focus:
  • Global consensus on science ethics
  • Human rights integration
World Commission on the Ethics of Scientific Knowledge and Technology (COMEST), UNESCO, 1998 Commission Description:
  • 18 scholars from science, law, philosophy, culture
  • Advises on ethics of emerging technologies
  • Produced reports on water ethics (2004), climate change (2010)
  • 2025 focus: quantum computing ethics
Ethical focus:
  • Moral implications of innovation
  • Sustainability
  • Equity
Transparency International (TI), 1993 Civil Society Org Description:
  • Global non-governmental organization
  • Leads anti-corruption movement
  • Publishes Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) annually
  • 100+ national chapters
  • Publishes Global Corruption Report
Ethical focus:
  • Transparency
  • Accountability
  • Integrity in public & private sectors
Global Ethics Foundation, Germany, 1995 Foundation Description:
  • Promotes Hans Küng’s "Global Ethic" (interfaith principles)
  • Focuses on education and dialogue across cultures
  • Teacher training programs in 100+ countries
Ethical focus:
  • Intercultural harmony
  • Anti-corruption
  • Human rights
European Business Ethics Network (EBEN), 1987 (Global Expansion) Network Description:
  • Academic and practitioner network
  • 1,500+ members in 40 countries
  • Annual congress on corporate ethics
  • Bridges academia and industry
Ethical focus:
  • Business ethics research
  • Ethical leadership
  • Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
2000s
European Group on Ethics in Science and New Technologies (EGE), EU, 1991 (Active 2000s) Advisory Group Description:
  • 15 independent experts advising EU Commission
  • Issues opinions on AI, gene editing, nanotech
  • 25 opinions issued (1991–2025)
Ethical focus:
  • Ethics of emerging technologies
  • Human dignity
  • Societal impact
Global Summit of National Ethics Committees (GSNEC), WHO/UNESCO, 2008 Global Forum Description:
  • Biennial forum
  • 8th in Singapore (2010), 10th in Mexico (2014)
  • 100+ national bioethics committees exchange views
Ethical focus:
  • Global dialogue on organ transplantation
  • TB ethics
  • Pandemic preparedness
  • Promotes ethical infrastructure
Bioethics Advisory Committee (BAC), Singapore, 2000 Committee Description:
  • National advisory body
  • Advises government on bioethics policy
  • Hosted 8th GSNEC (2010)
Ethical focus:
  • Genetic testing
  • Stem cell research
  • Human-animal chimeras
  • Balances innovation and ethics
Forum for Ethics Committees in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), 2001 Regional Forum Description:
  • WHO/UNESCO-supported network
  • 12 CIS countries’ ethics committees collaborate
Ethical focus:
  • Regional bioethics training
  • Harmonized GCP standards
  • Research ethics consensus
Global Ethics Observatory (GEObs), UNESCO, 2005 Database Description:
  • UNESCO platform with 4 databases
  • Maps ethics experts, committees, education, legislation
  • 1,000+ entries across 190+ countries
Ethical focus:
  • Global capacity building in ethics
  • Knowledge sharing
Global Network of WHO Collaborating Centres for Bioethics, 2005 Network Description:
  • WHO-led
  • 20+ centers for bioethics training and policy support
  • 2025: 50+ centers
Ethical focus:
  • Capacity building
  • International standards for health research ethics
Institute for Global Ethics, USA, 1989 (Global Expansion 2000s) Organization Description:
  • Independent non-profit
  • Research and education on ethical decision-making
  • Programs in 20+ countries
Ethical focus:
  • Moral leadership
  • Anti-corruption
  • Values-based governance
2010s
International Anti-Corruption Coordination Centre (IACCC), 2017 Coordination Centre Description:
  • Hosted by INTERPOL
  • 60+ countries coordinate cross-border anti-corruption
  • 500+ operations since inception
Ethical focus:
  • Global integrity
  • Asset recovery
  • Transnational bribery
Ethics Committee, International Council of Museums (ICOM), 2013 Committee Description:
  • 15-member ICOM body
  • Monitors compliance with ICOM Code of Ethics for Museums (2004)
  • 2025 mandate renewal
Ethical focus:
  • Cultural heritage integrity
  • Repatriation ethics
  • Illicit trafficking
Public Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Ethics Network (PHEPREN), WHO, 2016 Network Description:
  • WHO-led global network
  • 50+ partners address ethics in pandemics
  • 2025: AI health ethics integration
Ethical focus:
  • Equity in vaccine allocation
  • Dignity in lockdowns
  • Research during emergencies
Global Summit of National Ethics Committees (GSNEC), 10th (Mexico, 2014) Global Forum Description:
  • WHO/UNESCO biennial
  • 120+ national committees
  • 2014 focused on TB and organ trade ethics
  • 12th planned for 2025
Ethical focus:
  • Global consensus on emerging bioethical challenges
Ethics Review Committee (ERC), MSI Reproductive Choices, 2010s Review Board Description:
  • Independent IRB
  • Reviews reproductive health research across 37 countries
  • Follows Helsinki and Belmont principles
Ethical focus:
  • Informed consent
  • Protection of vulnerable populations
Global Health Ethics Consortium (GHEC), WHO, 2015 Network Description:
  • WHO initiative
  • 20+ global partners for health ethics guidance
  • 2025: Digital health ethics toolkit
Ethical focus:
  • Pandemic ethics
  • Equity in research
  • AI in healthcare
Ethics Advisory Board, European Commission (Horizon Europe), 2014 Advisory Body Description:
  • Advises on EU-funded research
  • Ensures ethical compliance in 10,000+ projects
  • GDPR-aligned
Ethical focus:
  • Research integrity
  • Data protection
  • Dual-use risks
2020s
Global Ethics Sustainability Standards Task Force, IESBA (IFAC), 2023 Task Force Description:
  • 15 experts from 10 countries
  • Develops International Ethics Standards for Sustainability Assurance (IESSA)
  • Final standards 2025
Ethical focus:
  • Accountability in ESG reporting
  • Anti-greenwashing
  • Integrity in supply chains
IESBA Sustainability Reporting Group (SRG), 2024 Working Group Description:
  • 10-member advisory group to IESBA
  • Advises on ethics for sustainability disclosures
  • Chaired by Channa Wijesinghe
Ethical focus:
  • Global standards for ethical reporting
  • Independence in assurance
Global Ethics Network, UNESCO, 2020 Network Description:
  • UNESCO initiative
  • Connects 100+ national ethics/bioethics committees
  • 2025: Quantum computing ethics framework
Ethical focus:
  • Global dialogue on AI
  • Climate ethics
  • Neurotech ethics
Ethics Committee, International Council of Museums (ICOM), 2023 Committee Description:
  • ICOM body
  • 15 members monitor Code of Ethics for Museums
  • 2025 mandate includes deepfake detection
Ethical focus:
  • Cultural repatriation
  • AI in curation
  • Digital heritage ethics
Global Summit of National Ethics Committees (GSNEC), 12th (2025) Global Forum Description:
  • WHO/UNESCO
  • 120+ committees
  • 2025 in Asia
Ethical focus:
  • AI ethics
  • Climate justice
  • Gene editing
  • Global consensus on emerging tech
WHO Ethics & Health Team (EHT), 2020 (Reorganized) Advisory Body Description:
  • WHO unit
  • Leads global health ethics
  • Integrated with PHEPREN
  • 2025: AI governance in health systems
Ethical focus:
  • Pandemic ethics
  • Digital health
  • Equity in access
